TauCeti.isZero_cyclicCohomology_self_of_.doc: The cyclic cohomology of the ground ring vanishes in odd degree.

TauCeti.isWeakHomotopyEquivalence_cwAppr.doc:
**CW approximation** (Hatcher, Proposition 4.13). For a path-connected space `X`, the map
`TauCeti.cwApproximationMap X x` from the CW complex `TauCeti.cwApproximation X x` to `X` is a weak
homotopy equivalence.

TauCeti.isUnimodular_leechLattice.doc: **The Leech lattice is unimodular**, being glued along a Lagrangian subgroup.

TauCeti.isSolvable_gal_iff_exists_isRoot.signature:
TauCeti.isSolvable_gal_iff_exists_isRoot_specialize_quinticF20Spec.{u} {F : Type u} [Field F]
  {f : Polynomial F} (hf : f.Monic) (hsep : f.Separable) (hirr : Irreducible f)
  (hdeg : f.natDegree = 5) (hres : TauCeti.ResolventSeparationEvidence TauCeti.quinticF20Spec f) :
  Group.IsSolvable f.Gal ↔ ∃ a, (TauCeti.quinticF20Spec.specialize F f).IsRoot a
TauCeti.isSolvable_gal_iff_exists_isRoot.doc:
**The quintic resolvent solvability criterion.** Let `f` be a monic irreducible separable
quintic over a field.  If the specialization of Dummit's `F₂₀` resolvent is separable, then
the polynomial Galois group is solvable if and only if that resolvent has a root in the base
field.

TauCeti.isSemialgebraic_iff_definable_ri.signature:
TauCeti.isSemialgebraic_iff_definable_ring_real.{u_2} {σ : Type u_2} {s : Set (σ → ℝ)} :
  TauCeti.IsSemialgebraic s ↔ Set.univ.Definable FirstOrder.Language.ring s
TauCeti.isSemialgebraic_iff_definable_ri.doc:
**Tarski's theorem for the real field.** A subset of `σ → ℝ` is semialgebraic if and only if
it is definable with parameters in the field `ℝ`, that is, in the language of rings with its usual
interpretation.

TauCeti.isRiemannRochDivisor_weilDiffere.doc:
**The Riemann–Roch theorem** (Stichtenoth, Theorem 1.5.15), for the divisor `(ω)` itself:
the divisor of a nonzero Weil differential is a Riemann–Roch divisor for the genus.

TauCeti.isObjectwiseCongruenceInvariant_.signature:
TauCeti.isObjectwiseCongruenceInvariant_iff_of_equivalence.{u_1, v_1, u_2, v_2, u_3} {H : Type u_1}
  [Group H] {K : ℕ → Subgroup H} {C : Type u_2} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v_1, u_2} C]
  [CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.MonoidalLeftAction (CategoryTheory.Discrete H) C] {D : Type u_3}
  [CategoryTheory.Category.{v_2, u_3} D]
  [CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.MonoidalLeftAction (CategoryTheory.Discrete H) D] (e : C ≌ D)
  [e.functor.LeftLinear (CategoryTheory.Discrete H)] :
  TauCeti.IsObjectwiseCongruenceInvariant K C ↔ TauCeti.IsObjectwiseCongruenceInvariant K D
TauCeti.isObjectwiseCongruenceInvariant_.doc:
Objectwise congruence invariance is independent of an equivariant presentation of
the category. Only the forward functor of the equivalence needs a specified lineator.

TauCeti.isMeagre_image_criticalPoints_of.signature:
TauCeti.isMeagre_image_criticalPoints_of_isFredholm.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
  [CompleteSpace E] [CompleteSpace F] {U : Set E} [LindelofSpace ↑U] {f : E → F} {n : WithTop ℕ∞}
  (hf : ∀ x ∈ U, ContDiffAt ℝ n f x) (hFred : ∀ x ∈ U, (fderiv ℝ f x).IsFredholm)
  (hn :
    ∀ x ∈ U,
      ↑(Module.finrank ℝ ↥(↑(fderiv ℝ f x)).ker * Module.finrank ℝ ↥(↑(fderiv ℝ f x)).ker + 1) ≤
        n) :
  IsMeagre (f '' (U ∩ {x | ¬Function.Surjective ⇑(fderiv ℝ f x)}))
TauCeti.isMeagre_image_criticalPoints_of.doc:
**The Sard--Smale theorem.** The critical values of a sufficiently smooth Fredholm map on a
Lindelöf subset of a Banach space form a meagre set. The subset need not be open; smoothness
is assumed at each of its points in the ambient space. Every subset of a separable Banach space
is Lindelöf.

Sard's theorem itself is false in infinite dimensions, and "measure zero" has no meaning there;
what survives is that the Fredholm condition confines the failure of regularity to a
finite-dimensional direction, in which the finite-dimensional theorem applies fibrewise.

The regularity threshold is the pointwise one of
`TauCeti.exists_mem_nhds_isClosed_isNowhereDense_image_criticalPoints`: at each point `C^k` with
`k ≥ (dim ker)² + 1`. In particular `n = ∞` needs no side condition.

TauCeti.isManifold_symChartedSpace.signature:
TauCeti.isManifold_symChartedSpace.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace α] [T2Space α]
  [ChartedSpace ℂ α] [IsManifold (modelWithCornersSelf ℂ ℂ) 1 α] {n : ℕ} :
  IsManifold (modelWithCornersSelf ℂ (Fin n → ℂ)) ⊤ (Sym α n)
TauCeti.isManifold_symChartedSpace.doc:
**The symmetric power of a complex curve is a complex analytic manifold.** For a Hausdorff
one-dimensional complex manifold `α`, the elementary-symmetric charts of `Sym α n` have analytic
transition maps, so `TauCeti.symChartedSpace` makes `Sym α n` an analytic manifold modelled on
`Fin n → ℂ`.

TauCeti.isLimitLocalHomologySystemCone.signature:
TauCeti.isLimitLocalHomologySystemCone.{w} {Λ : Type w} [Ring Λ] (N : ModuleCat Λ) (M E : Type w)
  [TopologicalSpace M] [T2Space M] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [ChartedSpace E M] [CompactSpace M] {n : ℕ} (hn : Module.finrank ℝ E = n) :
  CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit (TauCeti.localHomologySystemCone N M E n)
TauCeti.isLimitLocalHomologySystemCone.doc:
**The top homology of a compact manifold is the module of parallel families of local
classes.** For a compact Hausdorff space modelled on a real normed space of finite dimension `n`,
the restrictions `Hₙ(M, M ∖ M; N) ⟶ Hₙ(M, M ∖ {x}; N)` exhibit `Hₙ(M, M ∖ M; N)` as the limit of
the local homology system: every transport-invariant family of local classes is the family of
restrictions of exactly one class.

TauCeti.isLeast_lintegral_isContinuityEq.signature:
TauCeti.isLeast_lintegral_isContinuityEquation.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [BorelSpace E]
  {μ₀ μ₁ : MeasureTheory.Measure E} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ₀]
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ₁] {p : ENNReal} (hp : 1 ≤ p) (hp_top : p ≠ ⊤)
  (hfin : TauCeti.wassersteinEDist p μ₀ μ₁ ≠ ⊤) :
  IsLeast
    {A |
      ∃ ν v,
        TauCeti.IsContinuityEquation (fun t => ↑(ν t)) v 0 1 ∧
          ContinuousOn ν (Set.Icc 0 1) ∧
            ↑(ν 0) = μ₀ ∧
              ↑(ν 1) = μ₁ ∧ ∫⁻ (t : ℝ) in Set.Ioo 0 1, ∫⁻ (x : E), ‖v t x‖ₑ ^ p.toReal ∂↑(ν t) = A}
    (TauCeti.wassersteinEDist p μ₀ μ₁ ^ p.toReal)
TauCeti.isLeast_lintegral_isContinuityEq.doc:
**The Benamou–Brenier formula.** For `1 ≤ p < ∞` and probability measures `μ₀`, `μ₁` on a
finite-dimensional real normed space at finite Wasserstein distance, `W_p (μ₀, μ₁) ^ p` is the
least `p`-action `∫₀¹ ∫ ‖vₜ‖ ^ p dνₜ dt` of a curve `t ↦ νₜ` of finite measures, narrowly
continuous on `[0, 1]` and joining `μ₀` to `μ₁`, solving the continuity equation with velocity `v`
on `(0, 1)`. The minimum is attained by the displacement interpolation of an optimal coupling.

TauCeti.isIndecomposableModule_iff_exist.signature:
TauCeti.isIndecomposableModule_iff_exists_linearEquiv_quotient_span_op_root_X_pow_pow.{u, v}

            (M ≃ₗ[(AdjoinRoot (Polynomial.X ^ n))ᵐᵒᵖ]
              (AdjoinRoot (Polynomial.X ^ n))ᵐᵒᵖ ⧸
                Ideal.span {MulOpposite.op (AdjoinRoot.root (Polynomial.X ^ n) ^ i)})
TauCeti.isIndecomposableModule_iff_exist.doc:
**The indecomposable finitely generated right modules over `A = K[X]/(Xⁿ)` are exactly the
`M_i`**, up to isomorphism: such a module is indecomposable exactly when it is isomorphic to
`A ⧸ (x ^ i)` for some `0 < i ≤ n`.

TauCeti.isHurewiczFibration_iff_nonempty.doc:
A map is a Hurewicz fibration for test spaces in `Type (max u v)` if and only if it has a
lifting function.

TauCeti.isFormal_liuWangAffineD4AInfinit.signature:
TauCeti.isFormal_liuWangAffineD4AInfinityAlgebra.{w} {k : Type w} [CommRing k] (c : k) :
  (TauCeti.liuWangAffineD4AInfinityAlgebra k c).IsFormal
TauCeti.isFormal_liuWangAffineD4AInfinit.doc:
**Liu--Wang's `A∞` algebra is formal**, for every scalar `c`: the displayed quartic operation
`m₄` is a Hochschild coboundary of the strict zigzag algebra, so it defines the trivial
`A∞` deformation.

TauCeti.isFiniteRepType_iff_titsForm_pos.signature:
TauCeti.isFiniteRepType_iff_titsForm_posDef.{u, v, w} {Q : Type v} [Quiver Q] [Fintype Q]
  [(a b : Q) → Fintype (a ⟶ b)] {k : Type u} [Field k]
  (hconn : (TauCeti.Quiver.underlyingGraph Q).Connected) :
  TauCeti.IsFiniteRepType k Q ↔ (TauCeti.titsForm Q).PosDef
TauCeti.isFiniteRepType_iff_titsForm_pos.doc:
**Gabriel's theorem, Tits form version.** A finite connected quiver has finite
representation type exactly when its Tits form is positive definite.

TauCeti.isFiniteEtaleSplit_iff_exists_se.signature:
TauCeti.isFiniteEtaleSplit_iff_exists_section.{u} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] :
  TauCeti.IsFiniteEtaleSplit R ↔
    ∀ (T : Type u) [inst : CommRing T] [inst_1 : Algebra R T] [Algebra.Etale R T]
      [Module.Finite R T] [Module.FaithfullyFlat R T], Nonempty (T →ₐ[R] R)
TauCeti.isFiniteEtaleSplit_iff_exists_se.doc:
A ring has no nonsplit finite étale covers if and only if every faithfully flat finite étale
algebra over it admits a section. Faithful flatness is needed: over a nonzero ring the zero
algebra is finite étale and totally split, but has no section.

TauCeti.isDemushkin_absoluteGaloisGroupP.signature:
TauCeti.isDemushkin_absoluteGaloisGroupProP_of_mu (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (K : Type) [Field K]
  [ValuativeRel K] [TopologicalSpace K] [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K]
  (hmu : ∃ ζ, IsPrimitiveRoot ζ p) : TauCeti.IsDemushkin p (TauCeti.absoluteGaloisGroupProP p K)
TauCeti.isDemushkin_absoluteGaloisGroupP.doc:
**Demushkin's theorem**: the maximal pro-`p` quotient `G_K(p)` of the absolute Galois group of
a nonarchimedean local field `K` containing a primitive `p`th root of unity is a Demushkin group.

TauCeti.isCompl_eisensteinSubspace_range.signature:
TauCeti.isCompl_eisensteinSubspace_range_cuspToModFormCharSpace {N k : ℕ} [NeZero N]
  (χ : (ZMod N)ˣ →* ℂˣ) (hk : 3 ≤ ↑k) :
  IsCompl (TauCeti.eisensteinSubspace χ hk) (TauCeti.cuspToModFormCharSpace (↑k) χ).range
TauCeti.isCompl_eisensteinSubspace_range.doc:
**The cusp–Eisenstein decomposition of `M_k(N, χ)`**: in weight `k ≥ 3`, the span of the
Eisenstein series of nebentypus `χ` is a complement of the image of `S_k(N, χ)` in `M_k(N, χ)`.

TauCeti.inverseRegularizedGamma.doc:
The inverse `P⁻¹(s, u)` of the regularized lower incomplete gamma function in its argument.

For positive `s` this is the quantile of the Gamma law with shape `s` and rate `1`. For
nonpositive `s` it is `0`; the quantile itself supplies the value `0` outside `0 < u < 1`.

TauCeti.intervalIntegral_ofReal_cpow_neg.signature:
TauCeti.intervalIntegral_ofReal_cpow_neg_sub_one {u v : ℝ} (hu : 0 < u) (hv : 0 < v) (z : ℂ) :
  ∫ (x : ℝ) in u..v, ↑x ^ (-z - 1) = ∫ (t : ℝ) in Real.log u..Real.log v, Complex.exp (-z * ↑t)
TauCeti.intervalIntegral_ofReal_cpow_neg.doc:
**Substitution `x = exp t`.** For `0 < u` and `0 < v`, the integral of `x ^ (-z - 1)` over
`[u, v]` is the truncated Laplace transform `∫ t in log u..log v, exp (-z t)` of the constant
function `1`.

TauCeti.internalScottRank_lt_omega_one.signature:
TauCeti.internalScottRank_lt_omega_one.{u, v, w} {L : FirstOrder.Language} [L.IsRelational]
  {M : Type w} [L.Structure M] [Countable M] : TauCeti.internalScottRank M < Ordinal.omega 1
TauCeti.internalScottRank_lt_omega_one.doc:
Every countable structure has internal Scott rank below the first uncountable ordinal.
The relational language need not be countable.

TauCeti.internalEnergy_map_smul_add_smul.signature:
TauCeti.internalEnergy_map_smul_add_smul_gradient_le.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
  (ρ : MeasureTheory.Measure E) [ρ.IsAddHaarMeasure] {f : E → EReal} {U : ℝ → ℝ} [Nontrivial E]
  (hU0 : U 0 = 0)
  (hc : ConvexOn ℝ (Set.Ioi 0) fun s => s ^ Module.finrank ℝ E * U (s ^ Module.finrank ℝ E)⁻¹)
  (ha : AntitoneOn (fun s => s ^ Module.finrank ℝ E * U (s ^ Module.finrank ℝ E)⁻¹) (Set.Ioi 0))
  (hf : Convex ℝ {p | f p.1 ≤ ↑p.2}) (hbot : ∀ (x : E), f x ≠ ⊥) {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E}
  [MeasureTheory.SigmaFinite μ] (hμ : μ.AbsolutelyContinuous ρ)
  (hμD : ∀ᵐ (x : E) ∂μ, x ∈ interior {x | f x ≠ ⊤}) (h₀ : TauCeti.internalEnergy U ρ μ ≠ ⊥)
  (h₁ :
    TauCeti.internalEnergy U ρ (MeasureTheory.Measure.map (gradient fun x' => (f x').toReal) μ) ≠ ⊥)
  {t : ℝ} (ht : t ∈ Set.Icc 0 1) :
  TauCeti.internalEnergy U ρ
      (MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x => (1 - t) • x + t • gradient (fun x' => (f x').toReal) x)
        μ) ≤
    ↑(1 - t) * TauCeti.internalEnergy U ρ μ +
      ↑t *
        TauCeti.internalEnergy U ρ (MeasureTheory.Measure.map (gradient fun x' => (f x').toReal) μ)
TauCeti.internalEnergy_map_smul_add_smul.doc:
**McCann's displacement convexity of internal energies.** Let `E` be a real inner product space
of finite dimension `n ≥ 1` with an additive Haar measure `ρ`, and let `U : ℝ → ℝ` satisfy
`U 0 = 0` and McCann's condition: `s ↦ sⁿ U(s⁻ⁿ)` is convex and nonincreasing on `(0, ∞)`. Let
`f : E → EReal` be convex (convex real epigraph, never `⊥`), with real representative `F`, and let
`μ` be a σ-finite measure, absolutely continuous with respect to `ρ` and carried by the interior of
the effective domain of `f`. Then the internal energy is convex along the interpolation
`μₜ = (Tₜ)₊ μ`, `Tₜ x = (1 - t) • x + t • ∇F x`:
`𝓤(μₜ) ≤ (1 - t) 𝓤(μ) + t 𝓤((∇F)₊ μ)` for `t ∈ [0, 1]`, provided neither endpoint has energy `⊥`.
The endpoint `(∇F)₊ μ` need not be absolutely continuous; its singular part is charged at the
recession constant `U'(∞)`.

TauCeti.integral_posDef_multivariateGamm.signature:
TauCeti.integral_posDef_multivariateGamma {p : ℕ} {a : ℝ} (ha : (↑p - 1) / 2 < a) :
  ∫ (A : ↥(selfAdjoint.submodule ℝ (Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) ℝ))) in {A | (↑A).PosDef},
      (↑A).det ^ (a - (↑p + 1) / 2) * Real.exp (-(↑A).trace) ∂TauCeti.symmetricLebesgue p =
    TauCeti.multivariateGamma p a
TauCeti.integral_posDef_multivariateGamm.doc:
**The multivariate Gamma integral.** For `((p : ℝ) - 1) / 2 < a`, the integral of
`(det A) ^ (a - (p + 1) / 2) * exp (-trace A)` over the cone of positive-definite symmetric
`p × p` matrices, against `TauCeti.symmetricLebesgue p`, is `Γ_p(a)`.

TauCeti.integralTopForm_mpullback_Icc_eq.doc:
For `a < b`, the line integral of a continuous real `1`-form along a `C¹` curve is the
canonical oriented integral over `[a, b]` of the pullback of the form along the curve.

TauCeti.integralTopForm_mextDeriv.signature:
TauCeti.integralTopForm_mextDeriv.{u_1} {n : ℕ} {M : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace M]
  [ChartedSpace (EuclideanHalfSpace (n + 1)) M]
  [IsManifold (modelWithCornersEuclideanHalfSpace (n + 1)) (↑⊤) M] [T2Space M] [SigmaCompactSpace M]
  (o : TauCeti.Manifold.Orientation (modelWithCornersEuclideanHalfSpace (n + 1)) M (Fin (n + 1)))
  {φ : TauCeti.RoughForm (modelWithCornersEuclideanHalfSpace (n + 1)) M ℝ n}
  (hφ : TauCeti.IsSmoothForm (modelWithCornersEuclideanHalfSpace (n + 1)) 1 φ)
  (hc : IsCompact (tsupport φ)) :
  TauCeti.integralTopForm o (TauCeti.mextDeriv φ) =
    TauCeti.integralTopForm (TauCeti.boundaryOrientation o) (TauCeti.boundaryRestriction φ)
TauCeti.integralTopForm_mextDeriv.doc:
Stokes' theorem for a compactly supported C1 form on an oriented smooth manifold with
boundary. The boundary carries its outward-first orientation.

TauCeti.instHasSemialgebraicProjectionsR.doc:
**The Tarski–Seidenberg theorem.** The projection of a semialgebraic subset of `ℝ ^ (n + 1)`
forgetting the coordinate `0` is semialgebraic. So quantifier elimination, the identification of
semialgebraic sets with definable sets, and the image and composition laws of semialgebraic
functions, which assume `HasSemialgebraicProjections`, hold over `ℝ` unconditionally.

TauCeti.instCWComplexCellularClassifying.signature:
TauCeti.instCWComplexCellularClassifyingSpace.{u} {S : Type u} (R : Set (FreeGroup S)) :
  Topology.CWComplex Set.univ
TauCeti.instCWComplexCellularClassifying.doc:
**The cellular classifying space is a CW complex.** Its cells are those of the presentation
complex, one `0`-cell, one `1`-cell for each generator and one `2`-cell for each relator, together
with the cells of dimension at least `3` attached to kill the higher homotopy groups
(`TauCeti.killHomotopyGroupsCWComplexCellEquiv`).

TauCeti.injective_freeGroup_lift_transve.doc:
**Sanov's theorem.** The matrices `[[1, 2], [0, 1]]` and `[[1, 0], [2, 1]]` freely generate
a free subgroup of rank two of `SL(2, ℤ)`. This is the case `R = ℤ`, `c = d = 2` of
`injective_freeGroup_lift_transvection_of_two_le_abs`.

TauCeti.infinite_totallyRamifiedOfDegree.signature:
TauCeti.infinite_totallyRamifiedOfDegree.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [ValuativeRel K]
  [TopologicalSpace K] [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K] {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hnK : ↑n = 0) :
  (TauCeti.totallyRamifiedOfDegree K n).Infinite
TauCeti.infinite_totallyRamifiedOfDegree.doc:
**Infinitely many totally ramified extensions in equal characteristic.** If `0 < n` and
`(n : K) = 0`, that is, `K` has characteristic `p > 0` with `p ∣ n`, then `σ_K(n)` is infinite:
its discriminant exponents are unbounded.

TauCeti.index_square_le_of_closure_eq_to.signature:
TauCeti.index_square_le_of_closure_eq_top.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [CommGroup G] {S : Finset G}
  (hS : Subgroup.closure ↑S = ⊤) : (Subgroup.square G).index ≤ 2 ^ S.card
TauCeti.index_square_le_of_closure_eq_to.doc:
In a commutative group generated by a finite set `S`, the subgroup of squares has index at
most `2 ^ S.card`. The quotient by the squares is an elementary abelian `2`-group spanned by
the image of `S`.

TauCeti.hyperbolicSixSpinEquivSpecialLin.signature:
TauCeti.hyperbolicSixSpinEquivSpecialLinear.{u_1} (K : Type u_1) [Field K] [NeZero 2] :
  ↥(spinGroup (TauCeti.splitEvenForm K 3)) ≃* Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin 4) K
TauCeti.hyperbolicSixSpinEquivSpecialLin.doc:
**The Spin group of three hyperbolic planes is `SL₄(K)`.** This is
`TauCeti.spinGroupEquivSpecialLinearGroupOfFinrankEqSix` for the canonical split polarization, so a
Spin element goes to the matrix of its even half-spin action in
`TauCeti.spinSixHalfSpinStandardBasis`. By `TauCeti.coe_hyperbolicSixSpinEquivSpecialLinear_apply`
it is the restriction of `TauCeti.hyperbolicSixEvenUnitaryEquivGeneralLinear` to Spin, so `Spin(Q)`
is the determinant-one subgroup of the reverse-unitary group `U(C₀, σ) ≅ GL₄(K)`. Over `ℚ`, three
hyperbolic planes give the split rational six-dimensional form, with `U(C₀, σ) ≅ GL₄(ℚ)` and
`Spin(Q) ≅ SL₄(ℚ)`.

TauCeti.hurwitz_genus_formula.signature:
TauCeti.hurwitz_genus_formula.{u, u', v, v'} {k : Type u} {k' : Type u'} {F : Type v} {F' : Type v'}
  [Field k] [Field k'] [Field F] [Field F'] [Algebra k k'] [Algebra k F] [Algebra k' F']
  [Algebra F F'] [Algebra k F'] [IsScalarTower k k' F'] [IsScalarTower k F F']
  [FiniteDimensional F F'] [Algebra.IsSeparable F F'] [FiniteDimensional k k']
  [Algebra.IsSeparable k k'] (hF : TauCeti.IsFunctionField k F)
  (hF' : TauCeti.IsFunctionField k' F') (hex : IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F)
  (hex' : IsIntegrallyClosedIn k' F') :
  ↑(Module.finrank k k') * (2 * ↑(TauCeti.genus k' F') - 2) =
    ↑(Module.finrank F F') * (2 * ↑(TauCeti.genus k F) - 2) +
      ↑(Module.finrank k k') * TauCeti.Divisor.degree (TauCeti.Divisor.different k' F' hF)
TauCeti.hurwitz_genus_formula.doc:
**The Hurwitz genus formula** (Stichtenoth, Theorem 3.4.13): for a finite separable extension
`F' / k'` of the function field `F / k`, both with exact constants and with `k' / k` finite
separable, `[k' : k] · (2g' - 2) = [F' : F] · (2g - 2) + [k' : k] · deg Diff(F'/F)`.

TauCeti.homotopyOperator.signature:
TauCeti.homotopyOperator.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {E : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3}
  {F : Type u_4} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [TopologicalSpace H]
  {I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M] [NormedAddCommGroup F]
  [NormedSpace ℝ F] {k : ℕ}
  (φ :
    TauCeti.RoughForm (I.prod (modelWithCornersEuclideanHalfSpace 1)) (M × ↑(Set.Icc 0 1)) F
      (k + 1)) :
  TauCeti.RoughForm I M F k
TauCeti.homotopyOperator.doc:
The **homotopy operator** on forms on the cylinder `M × [0, 1]`: the `k`-form
`x ↦ ∫₀¹ φ(x, t)(∂ₜ, (·, 0)) dt` on `M` built from a `(k + 1)`-form `φ` on `M × [0, 1]`, where
`∂ₜ = (0, 1)` is the unit time vector and tangent vectors of `M` enter through
`ContinuousLinearMap.inl`. Equivalently `h φ = ∫₀¹ ιₜ^*(∂ₜ ⌟ φ) dt` for the slices
`ιₜ x = (x, t)`. For a `C¹` form with values in a Banach space on a `C²` manifold,
`d (h φ) + h (d φ) = ι₁^* φ - ι₀^* φ`
(`TauCeti.mextDeriv_homotopyOperator_add_homotopyOperator_mextDeriv`).

TauCeti.homotopyGroupMulAction.signature:
TauCeti.homotopyGroupMulAction.{u_1, u_2} {N : Type u_1} [Fintype N] {X : Type u_2}
  [TopologicalSpace X] {x : X} : MulAction (FundamentalGroup X x) (HomotopyGroup N X x)
TauCeti.homotopyGroupMulAction.doc:
**The fundamental group at `x` acts on every homotopy group based at `x`**, an element of
`π₁(X, x)` acting by transport around the loop it represents.

The action is a left action: transport composes covariantly and `FundamentalGroup.mul_def`
reverses the order of concatenation, so the two reversals cancel.

TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf.quotie.doc:
The sheaf of holomorphic functions on the normalization which have matching values on each
fibre of the quotient map. For paired node flags this is the normalization construction of the
structure sheaf of a nodal curve.

TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf.isFrac.signature:
TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf.isFractionRing_meromorphicGerms (a : ℂ) :
  IsFractionRing
    ↑((TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf (modelWithCornersSelf ℂ ℂ) ℂ).presheaf.stalk a)
    ↥(TauCeti.meromorphicGerms ℂ a)
TauCeti.holomorphicStructureSheaf.isFrac.doc:
The field of meromorphic germs at `a : ℂ` is the fraction field of the ring of holomorphic
germs at `a`.

TauCeti.hilbertSymbol_productFormula.signature:
TauCeti.hilbertSymbol_productFormula.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [NumberField K] (a b : Kˣ) :
  (∏ᶠ (v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)),
        TauCeti.hilbertSymbol (v.unitAtFinitePlace a) (v.unitAtFinitePlace b)) *
      ∏ w, TauCeti.hilbertSymbol ((TauCeti.unitAtRealPlace w) a) ((TauCeti.unitAtRealPlace w) b) =
    1
TauCeti.hilbertSymbol_productFormula.doc:
**Hilbert's product formula.** For `a, b ∈ Kˣ` in a number field `K`, the product of the
norm-equation Hilbert symbols `(a_v, b_v)_v` over the finite places and of the real Hilbert symbols
`(a_w, b_w)_w` over the real places of `K` is `1`.

TauCeti.hilbertSymbolForm.signature:
TauCeti.hilbertSymbolForm.{u_1} (K : Type u_1) [Field K] [ValuativeRel K] [TopologicalSpace K]
  [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K] [Invertible 2] :
  LinearMap.BilinForm (ZMod 2) (TauCeti.SquareClassGroup K)
TauCeti.hilbertSymbolForm.doc:
**The Hilbert symbol as a bilinear form over `𝔽₂`.** Over a nonarchimedean local field in which
`2` is invertible, the Hilbert symbol on square classes, read in `ZMod 2` through the dictionary
`+1 ↦ 0`, `-1 ↦ 1`, is a `ZMod 2`-bilinear form on `Kˣ/(Kˣ)²`. Its sign is the symbol
(`TauCeti.hilbertSign_hilbertSymbolForm`).

TauCeti.hilbertBasisOfWeightedMeasure.signature:
TauCeti.hilbertBasisOfWeightedMeasure.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {α : Type u_2}
  [MeasurableSpace α] (f : ℕ → α → ℝ) (w : α → ℝ) (c : ℕ → ℝ) {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure α}
  (hwnn : ∀ᵐ (x : α) ∂μ, 0 ≤ w x) (hwm : AEMeasurable w μ) (hc : ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < c n)
  (horth : ∀ (m n : ℕ), ∫ (x : α), f m x * f n x * w x ∂μ = if m = n then c n else 0)
  (hmem :
    ∀ (n : ℕ),
      MeasureTheory.MemLp (fun x => (algebraMap ℝ 𝕜) (f n x / √(c n))) 2
        (μ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (w x)))
  (hcomplete : (Submodule.span 𝕜 (Set.range (TauCeti.bareNormalizedLp f w c hmem)))ᗮ = ⊥) :
  HilbertBasis ℕ 𝕜 ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp 𝕜 2 (μ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (w x)))
TauCeti.hilbertBasisOfWeightedMeasure.doc:
**The weighted-measure basis.** The normalized bare functions, orthonormal by the
orthogonality relation and complete by hypothesis, form a Hilbert basis of `L²(w·μ)` — the textbook
statement that a family of orthogonal functions is an orthonormal basis of its own weighted `L²`
space.

TauCeti.hilbert90.signature:
TauCeti.hilbert90.{u_1} (K : Type u_1) [Field K] :
  CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero
    (continuousCohomology 1
      (TauCeti.ofDiscreteModule ℤ (TauCeti.AbsoluteGaloisGroup K) (TauCeti.UnitsCoeff K)))
TauCeti.hilbert90.doc:
**Hilbert 90 for the absolute Galois group**, stated for Mathlib's canonical continuous
cohomology: `H¹(G_K, (Kˢ)ˣ) = 0` (NSW (6.2.1)). This is the form in which the vanishing feeds
the canonical all-degree theory, where it makes the Kummer map `Kˣ → H¹(G_K, μₙ)` surjective for
`n` positive and invertible in `K`.

TauCeti.hermiteHilbertBasis.signature:
TauCeti.hermiteHilbertBasis.{u_1} (𝕜 : Type u_1) [RCLike 𝕜] :
  HilbertBasis ℕ 𝕜 ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp 𝕜 2 MeasureTheory.volume)
TauCeti.hermiteHilbertBasis.doc:
**The Hermite functions are a Hilbert basis of `L²(ℝ)`.** Orthonormality comes from the
weighted-measure machinery and completeness from moment determinacy
(`TauCeti.orthogonal_span_range_bareNormalizedLp_eq_bot`), applied to the exact-degree family
`Hₙ(x√2)` against the Gaussian weight `e^{-x²}`.

TauCeti.hermiteAnnihilationCLM_comp_herm.signature:
TauCeti.hermiteAnnihilationCLM_comp_hermiteCreationCLM_sub_hermiteCreationCLM_comp_hermiteAnnihilationCLM :
  TauCeti.hermiteAnnihilationCLM ∘SL TauCeti.hermiteCreationCLM -
      TauCeti.hermiteCreationCLM ∘SL TauCeti.hermiteAnnihilationCLM =
    ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (SchwartzMap ℝ ℝ)
TauCeti.hermiteAnnihilationCLM_comp_herm.doc:
**Canonical Commutation Relation (CCR) for the Hermite ladder operators.**
`[a, a†] = a ∘L a† - a† ∘L a = id`.

TauCeti.hausdorff_bernstein_widder.signature:
TauCeti.hausdorff_bernstein_widder (f : ℝ → ℝ) :
  TauCeti.IsContinuousCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi f ↔ ∃ μ, TauCeti.RepresentsLaplace μ f
TauCeti.hausdorff_bernstein_widder.doc:
**Hausdorff--Bernstein--Widder theorem**, finite-measure version on `ℝ≥0`.

A function is continuous on `[0, ∞)` and completely monotone on `(0, ∞)` if and only if it is
the Laplace transform of a finite positive measure on `ℝ≥0`.

TauCeti.hasSum_chebyshevT_expansion.signature:
TauCeti.hasSum_chebyshevT_expansion.{u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜]
  (f : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp 𝕜 2 Polynomial.Chebyshev.measureT)) :
  HasSum
    (fun n =>
      (∫ (x : ℝ),
          (algebraMap ℝ 𝕜) (TauCeti.normalizedChebyshevT n x) *
            ↑↑f x ∂Polynomial.Chebyshev.measureT) •
        TauCeti.normalizedChebyshevTLp 𝕜 n)
    f
TauCeti.hasSum_chebyshevT_expansion.doc:
**The Chebyshev expansion.** Every `f ∈ L²(measureT)` is the sum of its normalized
Chebyshev-polynomial series.

TauCeti.hasPrekopaLeindler_volume.doc:
The **Prékopa–Leindler inequality** on a finite-dimensional real inner product space, such as
`EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)`: its volume has the Prékopa–Leindler property at every weight
`0 ≤ θ ≤ 1`.

TauCeti.hasFoelnerSets_iff.signature:
TauCeti.hasFoelnerSets_iff.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] [DecidableEq G] :
  TauCeti.HasFoelnerSets G ↔
    ∀ (K : Finset G) (ε : ℝ),
      0 < ε → ∃ F, F.Nonempty ∧ ∀ g ∈ K, ↑(symmDiff (g • F) F).card < ε * ↑F.card
TauCeti.hasFoelnerSets_iff.doc:
A group has Følner sets exactly when for every finite `K ⊆ G` and every `ε > 0` there is a
finite nonempty `F ⊆ G` with `|gF △ F| < ε · |F|` for all `g ∈ K`.

TauCeti.harishChandraLinearIso.signature:
TauCeti.harishChandraLinearIso.{v} {K : Type} {L : Type v} [Field K] [CharZero K] [IsAlgClosed K]

TauCeti.harishChandraLinearIso.doc:
**The linear Harish-Chandra isomorphism** `Z(U(L)) ≃ₐ[K] S(H)^W`: the linear Harish-Chandra
projection `TauCeti.hcProjectionLinear b`, with its values in the Weyl invariants.

TauCeti.groupCohomologyOddEquivTorsionBy.signature:
TauCeti.groupCohomologyOddEquivTorsionBy (T : Type) [AddCommGroup T] (m : ℕ) [NeZero m] (i : ℕ)

TauCeti.groupCohomologyOddEquivTorsionBy.doc:
**Odd-degree cohomology of the trivial action.** When `C_m` acts trivially on `T`, its
cohomology in odd degree is the `m`-torsion `T[m]`: the class of a norm-zero element `x`
corresponds to `x` itself.

TauCeti.groupCohomology.averagingHomotop.signature:
TauCeti.groupCohomology.averagingHomotopy.{u} {k G : Type u} [CommRing k] [Group G] [Fintype G]

TauCeti.groupCohomology.averagingHomotop.doc:
**The averaging contraction.** The identity of the complex of inhomogeneous cochains is
homotopic to the averaging projection onto the invariants placed in degree `0`, through the
homotopy whose component from degree `n + 1` to degree `n` is `(-1)^(n+1)` times the average
over the last argument (`TauCeti.groupCohomology.averagingHomotopy_hom_succ`).

TauCeti.gradedLieHom.signature:
TauCeti.gradedLieHom.{u, v} (p : ℕ) {G : Type u} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]

TauCeti.gradedLieHom.doc:
**The graded Lie homomorphism of a continuous homomorphism** `f : G →* H`: the graded maps
`TauCeti.gradedMap p f hf k` of all degrees, assembled into a homomorphism of graded Lie algebras
`⨁ k, gr_k(G) →ₗ⁅ZMod p⁆ ⨁ k, gr_k(H)`. Its value on homogeneous elements is
`TauCeti.gradedLieHom_of`.

TauCeti.gradedIdempotentProjectiveBasis.signature:
TauCeti.gradedIdempotentProjectiveBasis.{uk, uA, uI} {k : Type uk} [Field k] {A : Type uA} [Ring A]

TauCeti.gradedIdempotentProjectiveBasis.doc:
**The graded projectives `A eᵢ` form a basis of `K₀^gr(proj A)`** over `ℤ[q,q⁻¹]`, for a
nonnegatively graded finite-dimensional algebra whose degree-zero piece is spanned by a complete
family of orthogonal nonzero idempotents `eᵢ`. Its basis vector at `i` is the class `[A eᵢ]`. This
is the projective counterpart of the head basis `TauCeti.gradedIdempotentHeadBasis`, and the case of
`TauCeti.gradedIdempotentProjectiveBasisOfPrimitive` where each `eᵢ` is primitive by
`TauCeti.isPrimitiveIdempotent_of_gradeZero_le_span` and the `A eᵢ` are pairwise nonisomorphic by
`TauCeti.isEmpty_linearEquiv_span_singleton_of_gradeZero_le_span`.

TauCeti.gradedCartanMatrix_zigzagAlgebra.{u, w} (k : Type w) [Field k] {V : Type u} [Finite V]

TauCeti.gradedCartanMatrix_zigzagAlgebra.doc:
The categorical graded Cartan map of the public algebra has matrix `(1 + q²) I + q A_G`
in the vertex-projective and vertex-head class bases, including isolated vertices.

TauCeti.gradedCartanMatrix_dualNumber.signature:
TauCeti.gradedCartanMatrix_dualNumber.{u} (k : Type u) [Field k] :
  TauCeti.gradedCartanMatrix (TauCeti.dualNumberIntegerGrade k)

    Matrix.of fun x x_1 => 1 + LaurentPolynomial.T 2
TauCeti.gradedCartanMatrix_dualNumber.doc:
**The graded Cartan matrix of the dual numbers is `1 + q²`**, with `ε` in degree two, in the
bases `[A]` and `[S]`: the regular module has the graded composition factors `S` and `S{2}`. At
`q = 1` this is the ungraded Cartan matrix `2` of `TauCeti.cartanMatrix_dualNumber`.

TauCeti.gradedCartanMatrix.signature:
TauCeti.gradedCartanMatrix.{uk, uA, uI, uJ} {k : Type uk} [CommRing k] {A : Type uA} [Ring A]
  [Algebra k A] (𝒜 : ℤ → Submodule k A) {I : Type uI} {J : Type uJ} [Fintype I] [Finite J]

TauCeti.gradedCartanMatrix.doc:
**The graded Cartan matrix** in a projective basis `bP` and a module basis `bM`: the matrix
of the Laurent-linear graded Cartan map.  Rows are indexed by `bM` and columns by `bP`.

TauCeti.gradedCartanEquiv.signature:
TauCeti.gradedCartanEquiv.{uk, uA} {k : Type uk} [CommRing k] {A : Type uA} [Ring A] [Algebra k A]

    TauCeti.LaurentK0 (TauCeti.gradedFiniteModulesExactStructure 𝒜)
TauCeti.gradedCartanEquiv.doc:
If every finite graded module admits a finite graded-projective resolution, the graded Cartan
map is an isomorphism of `ℤ[q,q⁻¹]`-modules.

TauCeti.globalDim_pivotalCategory_eq.signature:
TauCeti.globalDim_pivotalCategory_eq.{w, v, u} (C : Type u) [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C]

TauCeti.globalDim_pivotalCategory_eq.doc:
**The global dimension does not depend on the pivotal structure**: over an algebraically
closed field `k`, if the endomorphisms of each simple object are finite-dimensional, then any two
pivotal structures `P` and `Q` on `C` give the same global dimension.

TauCeti.globalDim_ne_zero.signature:
TauCeti.globalDim_ne_zero.{w', v, u} (k : Type w') [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] [CharZero k]
  (C : Type u) [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Abelian C]
  [CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory C] [CategoryTheory.MonoidalPreadditive C]
  [CategoryTheory.RigidCategory C] [TauCeti.PivotalCategory C] [CategoryTheory.Linear k C]

TauCeti.globalDim_ne_zero.doc:
**The global dimension of a pivotal fusion category over a field of characteristic zero is
nonzero** (Etingof–Nikshych–Ostrik). Here `C` is pivotal, `k`-linear abelian and finite semisimple
over an algebraically closed field `k` of characteristic zero, with finite-dimensional morphism
spaces, simple tensor unit, and finitely many simple classes.

TauCeti.germKernel_eq_ker.signature:
TauCeti.germKernel_eq_ker.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {H : Type u_3}
  {M : Type u_4} {G : Type u_5} [RCLike 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
  [TopologicalSpace H] {I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H} [I.Boundaryless] [TopologicalSpace M]
  [ChartedSpace H M] [Group G] [MulAction G M] [CompleteSpace E] [T2Space M] [PreconnectedSpace M]
  (hsmooth : ∀ (g : G), ContMDiff I I 1 fun x => g • x)
  (hG : ∀ (x : M), IsMulTorsion ↥(MulAction.stabilizer G x)) (x : M) :
  TauCeti.MulAction.germKernel G x = (MulAction.toPermHom G M).ker
TauCeti.germKernel_eq_ker.doc:
For a group with torsion stabilizers acting by `C¹` maps on a preconnected Hausdorff manifold
without boundary, the germ kernel at every point is the kernel of the action: an element acting as
the identity near one point acts as the identity everywhere.

TauCeti.genus_eq_of_isHomogeneous.signature:
TauCeti.genus_eq_of_isHomogeneous.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {k : Type u_1} [Field k] {F : Type u_2} [Field F]
  [Algebra k F] {K : Type u_3} [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K] [Algebra k K] {G : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) k}
  {d : ℕ} (hG : G.IsHomogeneous d)
  (hsm :
    ∀ (b : Fin 3 → K),
      b ≠ 0 →
        (MvPolynomial.aeval b) G = 0 → ∃ l, (MvPolynomial.aeval b) ((MvPolynomial.pderiv l) G) ≠ 0)
  {x y : F} (hx : Transcendental k x) (hgen : k⟮x, y⟯ = ⊤)
  (h : (MvPolynomial.aeval ![x, y, 1]) G = 0) : TauCeti.genus k F = (d - 1) * (d - 2) / 2
TauCeti.genus_eq_of_isHomogeneous.doc:
**The genus of a smooth projective plane curve** (Fulton, *Algebraic Curves*, Section 8.3): let
`G ∈ k[X₀, X₁, X₂]` be homogeneous of degree `d`, with every point of `G = 0` over an algebraically
closed extension `K` of `k` nonsingular. Let `F / k` be generated by a transcendental `x` and an
element `y` with `G(x, y, 1) = 0`. Then `F` has genus `(d - 1)(d - 2) / 2`.

Nonsingularity makes `G(X₀, X₁, 1)` irreducible over `K`, so `k` is the exact constant field of
`F` (`TauCeti.isIntegrallyClosedIn_of_irreducible_map`).

TauCeti.gelfandTsetlinGenerator.signature:
TauCeti.gelfandTsetlinGenerator.{u_1} (K : Type u_1) [CommRing K] {n k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ n) (r : ℕ) :
  UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra K (Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K)
TauCeti.gelfandTsetlinGenerator.doc:
The **Gelfand-Tsetlin generator** of degree `r` at level `k ≤ n`: the image in `U(gl (Fin n))`
of the Gelfand invariant `Cᵣ` of the upper-left corner `gl (Fin k)`.

TauCeti.gaussNorm_amiceRadius_le_amiceDu.signature:
TauCeti.gaussNorm_amiceRadius_le_amiceDualNorm.{u_1} {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)]

TauCeti.gaussNorm_amiceRadius_le_amiceDu.doc:
**`S_h ≤ D_h`.** The Gauss norm at the radius `r_h` is at most the dual stage norm at level
`h`, provided the latter is the supremum of a bounded family.

TauCeti.gamma0CuspOrbitEquiv.doc:
**The cusps of `Γ₀(N)`** are in bijection with the pairs `(g, x)` of a divisor `g` of `N`
and a unit `x` modulo `gcd(g, N / g)`. The cusp `γ • ∞` corresponds to the label of `γ`
(`gamma0CuspOrbitEquiv_cuspOrbitOfSL2Z`).

  [TopologicalSpace K] [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K] [Invertible 2] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
  [FiniteDimensional K L] [Invertible 2] (σ : L →ₐ[K] SeparableClosure K)
  (hfin : Module.finrank K L = 2) {x : L} {d : Kˣ} (hx : x ∉ Set.range ⇑(algebraMap K L))
  (hx2 : x ^ 2 = (algebraMap K L) ↑d) (a : Lˣ) {t : Kˣ} (ht : ↑t = (Algebra.trace K L) ↑a)
  {c e : Kˣ} (hce : TauCeti.hilbertSymbol c e = -1) :

    TauCeti.additiveIntUnitsAddEquiv
        (Additive.ofMul
          (TauCeti.hilbertSymbol t (-(d * (TauCeti.Algebra.normUnits K) a)) *
            TauCeti.hilbertSymbol (unitOfInvertible 2) d)) •
      (((TauCeti.trivialF2TopPairing (TauCeti.AbsoluteGaloisGroup K)).cup 1 1)
          (TauCeti.kummerClass c))
        (TauCeti.kummerClass e)
TauCeti.galoisEvens_kummerClass_eq_hilbe.doc:
**The Evens norm of a Kummer class over a local field, as an element of `H²(G_K, 𝔽₂)`**: if
`L` is generated over a local field `K` by a square root `x ∉ K` of `d`, and `a ∈ Lˣ` has nonzero
trace `t`, then `N^{Ev}((a)) = ε((t, −d · N a)_K · (2, d)_K) • ((c) ∪ (e))` for all `c, e` with
`(c, e)_K = -1`, where `ε` sends the signs `+1`, `-1` to `0`, `1`.

TauCeti.fusionCoeff.doc:
The **fusion coefficient** `N_{ST}^U` of three simple classes: the dimension over `k` of the
morphisms from the tensor product of the representatives of `S` and `T` to the representative of
`U`. Over an algebraically closed field, with finite-dimensional morphism spaces, it is the
multiplicity of `U` in `S ⊗ T` (`TauCeti.fusionCoeff_eq_simpleMultiplicities`).

TauCeti.frobeniusRootIdeal_eq_radical.signature:
TauCeti.frobeniusRootIdeal_eq_radical.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommSemiring R] {p : ℕ} [ExpChar R p]
  [PerfectRing R p] [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (f : R) :
  TauCeti.frobeniusRootIdeal R p f = (Ideal.span {f}).radical
TauCeti.frobeniusRootIdeal_eq_radical.doc:
**Frobenius-root ideals are radicals.** In a perfect ring, the Frobenius-root ideal of `f`
is the radical of the principal ideal `(f)`.

TauCeti.frobeniusPerronDim.signature:
TauCeti.frobeniusPerronDim.{w, w', v, u} (k : Type w') [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {C : Type u}
  [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Abelian C] [CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory C]

  [CategoryTheory.EssentiallySmall.{w, v, u} C] [Finite (TauCeti.SimpleClasses C)] (X : C) : ℝ
TauCeti.frobeniusPerronDim.doc:
The **Frobenius–Perron dimension** of an object of a fusion category: the value of the
Frobenius–Perron character `TauCeti.SplitK0.frobeniusPerronChar` at the class of the object.

TauCeti.freeProP.lcsDegreeOneBasis.signature:
TauCeti.freeProP.lcsDegreeOneBasis.{u} (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (X : Type u) [Fintype X]

TauCeti.freeProP.lcsDegreeOneBasis.doc:
**The `ℤ_p`-basis of `gr_1` of a free pro-`p` group of finite rank**, formed by the brackets
`[x_i, x_j]` of the generator classes for `i < j`
(`TauCeti.lcsGradedPiece_one_freeProP_bijective`).

TauCeti.freeProP.finrank_lcsGradedPiece_.signature:
TauCeti.freeProP.finrank_lcsGradedPiece_one.{u} (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (X : Type u)
  [Fintype X] :
  Module.finrank ℤ_[p] (TauCeti.lcsGradedPiece (TauCeti.freeProP p X) 1) = (Fintype.card X).choose 2
TauCeti.freeProP.finrank_lcsGradedPiece_.doc: `gr_1` of the free pro-`p` group on `X` has rank `#X choose 2` over `ℤ_p`.

TauCeti.freeProP.exteriorSquareEquivLcsG.signature:
TauCeti.freeProP.exteriorSquareEquivLcsGradedPieceOne.{u} (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (X : Type u)
  [Fintype X] :
  ↥(⋀[ℤ_[p]]^2 (TauCeti.lcsGradedPiece (TauCeti.freeProP p X) 0)) ≃ₗ[ℤ_[p]]
    TauCeti.lcsGradedPiece (TauCeti.freeProP p X) 1
TauCeti.freeProP.exteriorSquareEquivLcsG.doc:
**`gr_1` of a free pro-`p` group is the exterior square of `gr_0`.** For the free pro-`p` group
`F` on a finite type, the graded bracket induces an isomorphism of `ℤ_p`-modules
`⋀²gr_0(F) ≃ gr_1(F)`, `x ∧ y ↦ [x, y]` (`exteriorSquareEquivLcsGradedPieceOne_ιMulti`).

TauCeti.freeProP.exists_continuousMulEqu.signature:
TauCeti.freeProP.exists_continuousMulEquiv_apply_eq_of_range_basisModificationDelta_eq_top.{u}
  {p : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {X : Type u} [Finite X] [LinearOrder X]
  (r w : ↥(TauCeti.pLowerCentralSeries p (TauCeti.freeProP p X) 1))
  (h :
    TauCeti.gradedMk p (TauCeti.freeProP p X) 1 r = TauCeti.gradedMk p (TauCeti.freeProP p X) 1 w)
  (hspan :
    ∀ (m : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m),
      ((TauCeti.freeProP.basisModificationDelta p X hm)
            (TauCeti.gradedMk p (TauCeti.freeProP p X) 1 r)).range =
        ⊤) :
  ∃ e, e ↑r = ↑w
TauCeti.freeProP.exists_continuousMulEqu.doc:
**The unconstrained successive-approximation theorem.** Let `r, w ∈ λ_1(F)` be relators of
the free pro-`p` group `F` on a finite linearly ordered type with the same class `ρ ∈ gr_1(F)`, and
suppose the basis-modification map `δ_ρ` is onto `gr_{m+1}(F)` for every `m ≥ 1`. Then a continuous
automorphism of `F` carries `r` to `w`.

TauCeti.freeProP.continuousAutToGL_surje.signature:
TauCeti.freeProP.continuousAutToGL_surjective.{u} {p : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {X : Type u}
  [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] : Function.Surjective ⇑(TauCeti.freeProP.continuousAutToGL p X)
TauCeti.freeProP.continuousAutToGL_surje.doc:
**Every invertible matrix over `𝔽_p` comes from a continuous automorphism** of the free
pro-`p` group of finite rank: the automorphism of the Frattini quotient it defines lifts.

TauCeti.freeCumulant_fiberProd_eq_sum_pr.signature:
TauCeti.freeCumulant_fiberProd_eq_sum_prod.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2}
  {α : Type u_3} {β : Type u_4} [LinearOrder α] {s : Finset α} {f : α → β} [LinearOrder β]
  [CommRing R] [Monoid A] (φ : A → R) (a : α → A) (hf : MonotoneOn f ↑s) :
  TauCeti.freeCumulant φ (TauCeti.fiberProd a s f) (Finset.image f s) =
    ∑ π with π ⊔ (TauCeti.NoncrossingPartition.comap hf) ⊥ = ⊤,
      ∏ B ∈ (↑π).parts, TauCeti.freeCumulant φ a B
TauCeti.freeCumulant_fiberProd_eq_sum_pr.doc:
*Free cumulants with products as arguments*, in multiplicative form:
`κ(fiberProd a s f) = ∑_{π ⊔ σ_f = 1_s} ∏_{B ∈ π} κ_B(a)`, where `σ_f` is the partition of `s`
into the fibres of `f`.

TauCeti.freeCumulant_eq_sum_mu_mul_parti.doc:
The free cumulant of a word is the sum over the noncrossing partitions `π` of its block
moments weighted by the Möbius function, `κ_s(a) = ∑_{π ∈ NC(s)} μ(π, 1_s) φ_π(a)`.

TauCeti.freeCumulant.signature:

type.

`A` is finite-dimensional and nonnegatively graded, with semisimple degree-zero part. For an

TauCeti.exists_signInvariant_mcCallumPro.signature:
TauCeti.exists_signInvariant_mcCallumProjection_stackCells_not_signInvariant
  (polynomialGCD : NormalizedGCDMonoid (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℝ)) :
  ∃ f S,
    {f}.IsSquarefreeBasis {f} ∧
      TauCeti.IsSemialgebraic S ∧
        TauCeti.IsAnalyticSubmanifold 1 S ∧
          IsConnected S ∧
            (∀ x ∈ S, Polynomial.map (MvPolynomial.eval x) f ≠ 0) ∧
              (∀ q ∈ {f}.mcCallumProjection {f},
                  TauCeti.SignInvariant (fun x => (MvPolynomial.eval x) q) S) ∧
                (∃ q ∈ {f}.mcCallumProjection {f}, ∃ x ∈ S, ∃ y ∈ S, q.orderAt x ≠ q.orderAt y) ∧
                  ∀ (k : ℕ) (θ : Fin k → ↑S → ℝ),
                    (∀ (x : ↑S), StrictMono fun i => θ i x) →
                      ∃ E ∈ TauCeti.stackCells S θ,
                        ¬TauCeti.SignInvariant
                            (fun y =>
                              (MvPolynomial.eval y) ((MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv ℝ 2).symm f))
                            E
TauCeti.exists_signInvariant_mcCallumPro.doc:
**Sign-invariance of the McCallum projection does not suffice for lifting.** In
`Finset.IsSquarefreeBasis.exists_isSemialgebraicStack_signInvariant_of_mcCallumProjection`, the
hypothesis that the McCallum projection is order-invariant on the base cannot be weakened to
sign-invariance, even for a nonnullified squarefree basis over a connected semialgebraic
analytic submanifold. So a lower level of a CAD that is merely sign-invariant for the projection
cannot replace an order-invariant one.

Explicitly, let `f = (T - 1)² (T - 1 - x₀²) + x₁`, a monic cubic in the distinguished variable
`T` over `ℝ[x₀, x₁]`, and let `S ⊆ ℝ ^ 2` be the line `x₁ = 0`. As `f` is squarefree, it is its
own squarefree basis. Over `S` its coefficients `1`, `-(3 + x₀²)`, `3 + 2 x₀²` and `-(1 + x₀²)`
have constant signs, its content is `1`, and its discriminant vanishes, because each fibre
`(T - 1)² (T - 1 - x₀²)` has a double root. So the McCallum projection of `{f}` is sign-invariant
on `S`, and some member of it has nonconstant order on `S`; since the other members do not vanish
on `S`, this is the discriminant. But the fibre has the two roots `1` and `2` over `(1, 0)` and
the single root `1` over the origin. In the coordinates `(T, x₀, x₁)`, every cell of a stack over
`S` lies over all of `S`, so the cells through the zeros `(1, 1, 0)` and `(2, 1, 0)` of `f` would
both contain its only zero `(1, 0, 0)` over the origin, hence coincide, and then also contain
`(3 / 2, 1, 0)`, where `f` is negative. So no stack over `S`, given by pointwise strictly
increasing functions, continuous or not, has `f` sign-invariant on each cell.

  [IsContMDiffRiemannianBundle I 1 E fun x => TangentSpace I x] {f : M → ℝ} {x p : M}

  (hx : Set.Ici 0 ⊆ maximalIntegralCurveInterval (-TauCeti.Manifold.mgradient I f) x)
  (hconv :
    Filter.Tendsto (maximalIntegralCurve (-TauCeti.Manifold.mgradient I f) x) Filter.atTop (nhds p))

the Riemannian distance.** If the maximal integral curve `γ` of `-grad f` through `x` exists for
all positive time and converges to a nondegenerate critical point `p`, then the Riemannian
distance from `γ t` to `p` is at most `C * exp (-μ * t)` for some `μ, C > 0` and all large `t`.
This is the manifold counterpart, for an arbitrary `C¹` metric, of the vector-space theorem
`IsIntegralCurveOn.exists_norm_sub_le_mul_exp_atTop`.

TauCeti.exists_regular_lineDeriv_ofFun_apply_eq.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E}
  {Ω : TopologicalSpace.Opens E} {u : E → ℝ} [BorelSpace E]
  (hu : ∀ (K : Set E), IsCompact K → K ⊆ ↑Ω → ∃ U, K ⊆ ↑U ∧ TauCeti.totalVariationOn μ U u ≠ ⊤)
  (v : E) :

      ν₂.Regular ∧
        ∀ (φ : TestFunction Ω ℝ ⊤),
          (LineDeriv.lineDerivOp v (Distribution.ofFun Ω u μ ⊤)) φ =

TauCeti.exists_regular_lineDeriv_ofFun_a.doc:

measures.** If every compact `K ⊆ Ω` has an open neighbourhood `U` on which `u` has finite total
variation, then for every direction `v` there are regular measures `ν₁` and `ν₂` on `Ω` with
`∂_v u (φ) = ∫ φ dν₁ - ∫ φ dν₂` for every test function `φ`, where `∂_v u` is the derivative of
the distribution `Distribution.ofFun Ω u μ ⊤`. If `u` is locally integrable on `Ω`, this is the
distributional derivative of `u`, `∂_v u (φ) = -∫ ∂_v φ * u`; otherwise `Distribution.ofFun` is
zero by convention and the statement is trivial. The measures are finite on compact subsets of
`Ω` but need not be finite.

TauCeti.exists_polynomial_aeval_mem_rang.signature:
TauCeti.exists_polynomial_aeval_mem_range.{w, u_1, u_2} {F : Type u_1} [Field F] [PerfectField F]

extension of `F` also lie in `F`.

TauCeti.exists_polynomial_aeval_mem_crit.doc:
**Polynomial Belyification of algebraic numbers.** Every finite set `S` of elements algebraic
over `ℚ` in a field `K`, such as a finite subset of `AlgebraicClosure ℚ`, is carried into

every field of characteristic zero, lie in `{0, 1}`.

TauCeti.exists_pathCycleDecomposition.{u, v, w} {V : Type u} {Q : V → V → Type v} {K : Type w}

  {f : TauCeti.Assignment Q K} (H : AddSubgroup K) (hf : 0 ≤ f)
  (hH : ∀ ⦃x y : V⦄ (e : Q x y), f e ∈ H) :

      (∀ c ∈ D.cycles, c.weight ∈ H) ∧ D.paths.length + D.cycles.length ≤ {a | 0 < f a.snd.snd}.card
TauCeti.exists_pathCycleDecomposition.doc:
**Path–cycle decomposition.** Every nonnegative arrow assignment `f` on a finite arrow family
is a sum of positively weighted directed paths, each from a vertex of negative excess to a vertex
of positive excess, and positively weighted directed cycles. The number of components is at most
the number of arrows on which `f` is positive, and if the values of `f` lie in an additive subgroup
`H`, then so do all weights.

TauCeti.exists_nullified_mcCallumProject.signature:
TauCeti.exists_nullified_mcCallumProjection_orderAt_ne
  (polynomialGCD : NormalizedGCDMonoid (MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℝ)) :
  have this := polynomialGCD;
  ∃ f C,
    TauCeti.IsSemialgebraic C ∧
      TauCeti.IsAnalyticSubmanifold 1 C ∧
        IsConnected C ∧
          ∀ (B : Finset (Polynomial (MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℝ))),
            (Finset.map (MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv ℝ 3).toEmbedding {f}).IsIrreducibleBasis B →
              (∀
                  q ∈
                    (Finset.map (MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv ℝ 3).toEmbedding {f}).mcCallumProjection
                      B,
                  ∀ x ∈ C, ∀ y ∈ C, q.orderAt x = q.orderAt y) ∧
                (∀ b ∈ B, ∀ x ∈ C, Polynomial.map (MvPolynomial.eval x) b = 0) ∧
                  ∀ (k : ℕ) (θ : Fin k → ↑C → ℝ),
                    (∀ (x : ↑C), StrictMono fun i => θ i x) →
                      ∃ E ∈ TauCeti.stackCells C θ, ∃ y ∈ E, ∃ y' ∈ E, f.orderAt y ≠ f.orderAt y'
TauCeti.exists_nullified_mcCallumProject.doc:
**McCallum lifting fails over positive-dimensional nullifying cells.** The hypothesis of
`TauCeti.exists_isSemialgebraicStack_orderAt_eq_of_mcCallumProjection` that no basis member is
nullified over a cell with more than one point cannot be dropped, even over a connected
semialgebraic analytic submanifold on which the McCallum projection is order-invariant.

Explicitly, let `f = X₂ (X₀ + 1) + X₃ X₁`, a polynomial in the distinguished variable `X₀` and the
base coordinates `X₁, X₂, X₃`, and let `C ⊆ ℝ ^ 3` be the line of base points `x` with
`x₁ = x₂ = 0`. As a polynomial in `X₀`, `f` is linear with coprime coefficients `X₂` and
`X₂ + X₃ X₁`, each of which vanishes to order one at every point of `C`; its content and
discriminant are units. So for every irreducible basis `B` of `{f}`, every element of the McCallum
projection has constant order on `C`, while every member of `B` is nullified over `C`. But `f` has
order at least two at the point `(-1, 0, 0, 0)` above `C`, and order one at every point above
`C` where `X₀ ≠ -1` or `X₁ ≠ 0`. Since every cell of a stack over `C` lies over the whole of `C`,
no stack over `C`, given by pointwise strictly increasing functions, continuous or not, has `f`
order-invariant on each cell.

**Brenier's theorem.** Let `μ` and `ν` be probability measures on a finite-dimensional real
inner product space `E`, with `μ` absolutely continuous with respect to an additive Haar measure,
and suppose the optimal cost for `‖x - y‖ ^ 2 / 2` is finite, as it is for laws with finite second
moment (`TauCeti.transportCost_norm_sub_sq_div_two_ne_top`). Then there is a convex, lower
semicontinuous `u : E → EReal` that never takes the value `⊥`, is finite near `μ`-almost every
point and has differentiable real representative there, such that the gradient
`T = ∇ (fun x => (u x).toReal)`:

* is an optimal transport map from `μ` to `ν`, attaining the Kantorovich value;
* induces the unique optimal plan: a plan is optimal exactly when it is the graph plan of `T`;
* is the unique optimal transport map up to `μ`-almost everywhere equality.

variables has a cylindrical algebraic decomposition of `ℝ ^ n` into analytic submanifolds on
each cell of which every member has constant Lazard valuation, when the coordinates are read in
reverse order, from the coordinate added first by the cylindrical structure to the one added
last. Every member is also sign-invariant on each cell. No well-orientedness hypothesis is
imposed, and members may be nullified over base cells of positive dimension.

fixes `X ∩ quadraticSublevelUnionCell ε`. Both are restrictions of
`TauCeti.quadraticHandleRetraction ε` and `TauCeti.quadraticHandleDeformation ε`.

nondegenerate Killing form over a field of characteristic zero, `e` is the image of the raising
element `E₀₁` under an injective Lie algebra homomorphism `sl (Fin 2) K →ₗ⁅K⁆ L` if and only if

TauCeti.exists_injective_freeGroup_SL.doc:
**Free groups of countable rank are linear over `ℤ`.** Every free group on a countable basis
embeds in `SL(2, ℤ)`.

**Existence of weak solutions for linear parabolic equations.** Let `V ↪ H ↪ V*` be a Gelfand
triple: `V` a separable Hilbert space, `H` a Hilbert space and `ι : V →L[ℝ] H` with dense range.
Let `A(t) : V →L[ℝ] V*` be weakly measurable (`t ↦ A(t) u v` almost everywhere strongly
measurable on `(a, b)` for all `u, v`), bounded by `Λ` and satisfy **Gårding's inequality**
`α ‖v‖² - β ‖ι v‖² ≤ A(t) v v` with `α > 0`, for almost every `t ∈ (a, b)`. Then for every
`f ∈ L²(a, b; V*)` and `u₀ ∈ H` there is a weak solution of

`u' + A(t) u = f`, `u(a) = u₀`:

a `u ∈ L²(a, b; V)` such that `u' = f - A u ∈ L²(a, b; V*)` is the weak time derivative of
`ι.gelfandDual ∘ ι ∘ u` on `(a, b)`, and a representative `w` of `ι ∘ u` continuous on `[a, b]`
with `w a = u₀`. For `β ≥ 0` it is unique: see `TauCeti.HasWeakLineDerivOn.eqOn_of_gelfandDual`
and `TauCeti.HasWeakLineDerivOn.ae_eq_of_gelfandDual`.

**The Mihlin–Hörmander multiplier theorem on `Lᵖ`.** Let `V` be a real inner product space of
finite dimension `n ≥ 1`, let `2N > n` and `1 < p < ∞`. There is a constant `C` such that for
every symbol `m` of temperate growth satisfying Mihlin's condition of order `N` with constant `A`,

`‖D^k m ξ‖ ≤ A / ‖ξ‖ ^ k` for every `k ≤ N` and every `ξ ≠ 0`,

the Fourier multiplier `𝓕⁻ (m • 𝓕 f)` of the tempered distribution of any `f ∈ Lᵖ(V, F)` is an
`Lᵖ` function `g` with `‖g‖_p ≤ C A ‖f‖_p`.

TauCeti.exists_finset_card_smul_symmDiff.doc:

`∑_{g ∈ K} ∑_x |p (g⁻¹ • x) - p x| < ε · ∑_x p x`, then some finite nonempty set `F ⊆ X` satisfies
`|g • F ∆ F| < ε |F|` for every `g ∈ K`.

TauCeti.exists_equivariant_chart_target_.doc:
**The linear local model at a fixed point.** Let a finite group `G` act continuously on a
finite-dimensional real manifold without boundary, fixing `y`, by maps that are `C¹` at `y`.
Inside any neighbourhood `s` of `y` there is a chart `e` sending `y` to `0` whose domain is
`G`-invariant and preconnected and whose target is a positive strict sublevel set of a
`σ`-invariant inner product, in which `G` acts linearly through a continuous representation `σ`.
Every element of `G` is retained, including those acting trivially: `g` acts as the identity near
`y`, that is, lies in the germ kernel at `y`, exactly when `σ g = 1`, and exactly when `g` fixes
every point of the domain of `e`.

TauCeti.exists_eqOn_const_mul_add_iff_lo.doc:
**Rigidity of the pre-Schwarzian derivative.** Two holomorphic functions with nonvanishing
derivatives on a domain have equal pre-Schwarzian derivatives exactly when one is obtained from
the other by postcomposition with `w ↦ a * w + b` for a nonzero constant `a`.

TauCeti.exists_eLpNorm_iteratedFDeriv_tw.doc:
**The Calderón–Zygmund estimate `‖D²u‖_p ≤ C ‖Δu‖_p`.** Let `1 < p < ∞`, and let `V` be a
finite-dimensional real inner product space with its volume measure. There is a constant `C` with

`‖D²u‖_{Lᵖ} ≤ C ‖Δu‖_{Lᵖ}`

for every Schwartz function `u` on `V` with values in a complex Hilbert space, where `D²u` is the
second Fréchet derivative of `u`.

uncountable structures of the same cardinality: in every universe there are two dense linear
orders without endpoints of cardinality `ℵ₁` that are potentially isomorphic, and so
`L∞ω`-equivalent (`TauCeti.InfEquivW`), but not isomorphic. The witnesses are `ω₁ ×ₗ ℚ` and its
order dual.

TauCeti.exists_diffeomorph_sublevel.doc:
**Sublevels on either side of a band without critical points are diffeomorphic**
(Milnor, Theorem 3.1). If `f` is smooth, `a ≤ b`, and the band `f⁻¹[a, b]` is compact and contains
no critical point of `f`, then there is a diffeomorphism `Φ` of `M` carrying the sublevel
`{f ≤ b}` onto `{f ≤ a}` and the level `f⁻¹(b)` onto `f⁻¹(a)`.

TauCeti.exists_diffeomorph_eventually_co.doc:
**Darboux's theorem.** A closed `C^r` two-form `ω` (`r ≥ 1`) on an open subset of a
finite-dimensional real normed space, nondegenerate at `x₀`, is constant in suitable coordinates
near `x₀`: there is a `C^r` diffeomorphism `ψ` of the space fixing `x₀` such that the pullback
`ψ^* ω` equals the constant form `ω(x₀)` on a neighbourhood of `x₀`.

**Carathéodory's continuity theorem, as a characterization.** A holomorphic injection of a disc
onto a bounded region extends continuously to the closed disc if and only if the boundary of the
region is locally connected.

TauCeti.exists_complete_self_stabilizati.doc:
A countable structure stabilizes below `ω₁`. Only its tuples are counted; the language
may be uncountable.

TauCeti.exists_card_aroots_eq.doc:
**Local constancy of the root count.** For a monic `f` over `𝒪[K]` that is separable over
`K`, there is a threshold `T > 0` such that every monic `g` over `𝒪[K]` with
`g.coeff i - f.coeff i ∈ 𝓂[K] ^ T` for all `i` has as many roots as `f`, counted with
multiplicity, in every finite intermediate field of `Ω / K`. The threshold depends only on `f`.

**The prime ends of a Jordan domain are the points of the circle.** Let `Ω` be a bounded
domain whose frontier is a Jordan curve. There is a holomorphic bijection `g` of the unit disc onto
`Ω` that is continuous and injective on the closed disc, and the map of prime ends it induces sends
the radial prime ends of the disc at the points of the unit circle bijectively onto the prime ends
of `Ω`.

TauCeti.exists_bijOn_const_mul_schwarzCh.doc:
**The Schwarz--Christoffel theorem for an unbounded polygonal Jordan domain.**  Let `U` be a
connected open set whose frontier, together with the point at infinity, is a Jordan curve
of the Riemann sphere.  Suppose that `U` coincides near each frontier point other than the
distinct vertices `v i` with an open half-plane, near the vertex `v i` with the open sector of
opening `(e i + 1) * π` at `v i`, where `e i ∈ (-1, 1)`, and far from a point `c` with the open
sector `{|arg ((z - c) / b)| < β * π / 2}` of opening `β * π`, where `0 < β < 2`: so `U` has a
further vertex at infinity.  Then there are distinct real prevertices `a i` and constants `A ≠ 0`
and `B` such that `z ↦ A * F z + B` maps the upper half-plane bijectively onto `U`, where `F` is
the normalized Schwarz--Christoffel primitive for the prevertices `a` and the turning exponents
`e`, and such that the Schwarz--Christoffel vertex at `a i`, the limit of `F` at `a i`, is sent to
`v i`.  The prevertex of the vertex at infinity is the point at infinity of the half-plane.

bounded, connected open set whose frontier is a Jordan curve.  Suppose that `U` coincides
near each frontier point other than the distinct vertices `v i` with an open half-plane, and near

`z ↦ A * F z + B` maps the upper half-plane bijectively onto `U`, where `F` is the normalized
Schwarz--Christoffel primitive for the prevertices `a` and the turning exponents `e`, and such that
the Schwarz--Christoffel vertex at `a i`, the limit of `F` at `a i`, is sent to `v i`.

TauCeti.exists_analytic_delineation_of_o.doc:
**Analytic delineability from constant discriminant order.** A polynomial with nonzero
fibers of constant degree over a preconnected analytic submanifold, whose nonzero formal
discriminant has constant ambient order on the base, has a global delineation with intrinsically
analytic root functions. Each root function is represented by an ambient function whose values
off the base are immaterial. Along each root section, the polynomial, viewed as a polynomial in
all `n + 1` variables, has constant ambient order of vanishing.

No preservation of the formal degree or nonvanishing of the discriminant values is required.
Multiple roots are allowed, and their fiber multiplicities are constant.

TauCeti.existsUnique_transitiveGroupLabe.doc:
A transitive subgroup of the symmetric group on five points carries exactly one label, one of
`5T1`, …, `5T5`.

TauCeti.existsUnique_isPos_reflection_sm.doc:
**A cover of `W / W_λ` has a unique positive root label.** If `y` is covered by `x` in the
Bruhat order of the minimal coset representatives of the stabilizer of the dominant weight `λ`,
there is exactly one positive root `β` with `y λ = s_β (x λ)`.

TauCeti.existsUnique_eq_smul_lazardCocyc.doc:
**The symmetric 2-cocycle lemma**, with uniqueness: for `n ≥ 2`, a homogeneous symmetric
additive 2-cocycle of degree `n` over any commutative ring is `r • C_n` for a unique `r`.

form a `C^n` manifold of dimension the index `d`, with a `C^n` immersion into `M` whose tangent
spaces are the kernels of the linearizations in the `M` direction.

TauCeti.eventuallyConst_separatingSpace.doc:
**Sinclair's stability lemma.** Let `E n` and `F` be Banach spaces, let
`R n : E (n + 1) → E n` be continuous linear maps, and let `T n : E n →ₗ F` be linear maps, not
assumed continuous, with `T (n + 1) = T n ∘ R n`, so that `T n = T 0 ∘ R 0 ∘ ⋯ ∘ R (n - 1)`.
Then the decreasing sequence of separating spaces of the `T n` is eventually constant.

A sphere of radius `r > 0` in an `n`-dimensional real inner product space has
`(n - 1)`-dimensional Hausdorff measure `n ω_n r ^ (n - 1)`, where `ω_n` is the volume of the
unit ball.

TauCeti.eq_zero_of_two_eq_zero_of_aeval_X_X_eq_zero.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (h2 : 2 = 0)

homogeneous symmetric additive 2-cocycle `f` of degree `2ᵏ` over `R` with zero diagonal

TauCeti.enoughInjectives_smoothModules.doc:
For a directed family `J` of left ideals of `A : Type u`, the smooth `A`-modules in universe
`max u w` have enough injectives: every smooth module embeds, through the unit of the coinduction
adjunction along `ℤ →+* A`, into the coinduction of an injective abelian group.

TauCeti.elementarilyEquivalent_int_sumLe.doc: `ℤ` and `ℤ ⊕ₗ ℤ` satisfy the same first-order sentences in the language of orders.

TauCeti.eisensteinSet.signature: TauCeti.eisensteinSet.{u_1} (K : Type u_1) [Field K] [ValuativeRel K] (n : ℕ) : Set (Fin n → K)
TauCeti.eisensteinSet.doc:
The Eisenstein region in the space `Fin n → K` of coefficient vectors of monic polynomials of
degree `n`: every coefficient has valuation below `1`, and the constant term of `monicOfCoeff a`
has valuation at least that of every element of valuation below `1`. For `0 < n` the constant term
is `a 0`, which then has the valuation of a uniformizer; for `n = 0` it is `1`, and the region is
the whole one-point space. When `𝒪[K]` is a discrete valuation ring,
`TauCeti.mem_eisensteinSet_iff_exists_isEisensteinAt` identifies these with the coefficient vectors
of the polynomials over `𝒪[K]` that are Eisenstein at `𝓂[K]`.

TauCeti.eLpNorm_le_totalVariationOn.signature:
TauCeti.eLpNorm_le_totalVariationOn.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure E} [μ.IsAddHaarMeasure] {p : NNReal} {u : E → ℝ}
  (hu : MeasureTheory.Integrable u μ) (hp : (↑(Module.finrank ℝ E)).HolderConjugate p) :
  MeasureTheory.eLpNorm u (↑p) μ ≤
    ↑(MeasureTheory.eLpNormLESNormFDerivOneConst μ ↑p) * TauCeti.totalVariationOn μ ⊤ u
TauCeti.eLpNorm_le_totalVariationOn.doc:
**The Sobolev inequality for functions of bounded variation.** Let `E` have dimension
`n ≥ 2` and let `p = n / (n - 1)`. Every integrable `u : E → ℝ` satisfies `‖u‖_p ≤ C |Du|(E)`,
where `|Du|(E)` is the total variation of `u` on the whole space, finite or infinite, and `C` is
the constant `MeasureTheory.eLpNormLESNormFDerivOneConst μ p` of the `C¹` Gagliardo–Nirenberg–
Sobolev inequality `MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_le_eLpNorm_fderiv_one`.

TauCeti.doubleCosetCongr.doc:
Transport of a double-coset space along a change of reference family. The subgroups on the
right are the images of those on the left under `restrictedProductCongr`, not the integral
subgroups of the new family; see `exists_map_integralSubgroup_ne`.

  (Π₀ (j : κ), TensorProduct k (S j) (S j →ₗ[A] M)) ≃ₗ[A] M
TauCeti.directSumIsotypicTensorEquiv.doc:
**The isotypic decomposition of a semisimple module.** Let `S j` be pairwise non-isomorphic
simple modules, finite-dimensional over the algebraically closed field `k`, such that every simple
submodule of the semisimple module `M` is isomorphic to one of them. Then evaluation
`s ⊗ f ↦ f s` is an isomorphism `⨁ⱼ S j ⊗[k] (S j →ₗ[A] M) ≃ M` of `A`-modules.

TauCeti.differentiable_intervalIntegral_.doc:
**Truncated Laplace transforms are entire.** If `f` is interval integrable on `[a, b]`, then
`z ↦ ∫ t in a..b, f t * exp (-z t)` is complex differentiable everywhere.

TauCeti.differentiableOn_schwarzReflecti.signature:
TauCeti.differentiableOn_schwarzReflection_of_symmetric {f : ℂ → ℂ} {Ω : Set ℂ} (hΩopen : IsOpen Ω)
  (hΩ : Set.MapsTo (⇑(starRingEnd ℂ)) Ω Ω) (hcont : ContinuousOn f (Ω ∩ {z | 0 ≤ z.im}))
  (hholo : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (Ω ∩ {z | 0 < z.im})) (hreal : ∀ z ∈ Ω, z.im = 0 → (f z).im = 0) :
  DifferentiableOn ℂ (TauCeti.schwarzReflection f) Ω
TauCeti.differentiableOn_schwarzReflecti.doc:
**Schwarz reflection principle (real axis).** On a conjugation-symmetric open set `Ω`, if `f`
is continuous on the closed upper part, holomorphic on the open upper part, and real-valued on
the real axis of `Ω`, then the explicit reflection extension `schwarzReflection f` is holomorphic
on all of `Ω` — in particular across the real axis.

The gluing calculus (continuity everywhere, holomorphy off the axis, the conjugation symmetry) is
`Reflection/Basic.lean`; the missing holomorphy at the axis is Painlevé removability,
`differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_im_ne_zero`.

TauCeti.differentiableOn_integral_mul_ce.doc:
**Holomorphy of the Laplace transform.** If `f` is bounded on `[0, ∞)`, its Laplace transform
`z ↦ ∫ t in Ici 0, f t * exp (-z t)` is complex differentiable on the half-plane `0 < re z`.

TauCeti.dgYonedaEquiv.signature:
TauCeti.dgYonedaEquiv.{v, u} {R : Type v} [CommRing R] {C : Type u} [TauCeti.DGCategory R C] (X : C)
  (F :
    CategoryTheory.EnrichedFunctor (CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) Cᵒᵖ
      (CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ)) :
  TauCeti.DGNatTrans (TauCeti.dgRepresentable R X) F ≃
    ↥(ModuleCat.Hom.hom ((F.obj (Opposite.op X)).d 0 1)).ker
TauCeti.dgYonedaEquiv.doc:
**The Yoneda lemma for right DG modules**: DG natural transformations `Hom(-, X) ⟶ F` are the
closed degree-zero elements of `F(X)`.  A transformation goes to the image of the identity of `X`
under its component at `X` (`TauCeti.dgYonedaEquiv_apply_coe`), and a closed element `x` goes to
the transformation sending `g : Y ⟶ X` to `F(g)(x)` (`TauCeti.dgApp_dgYonedaEquiv_symm_v`).

TauCeti.dense_setOf_stabilizer_eq_ker_of.doc:
**The principal part of a finite smooth action.** For a finite group acting by `C¹` maps on a
preconnected Hausdorff manifold without boundary, the points whose stabilizer is the kernel of the
action form a dense set. The action need not be faithful: elements acting trivially are retained
in every stabilizer, and generically they are the only ones. The set is also open, by
`TauCeti.isOpen_setOf_stabilizer_eq_ker`.

TauCeti.dense_setOf_stabilizer_eq_ker.signature:
TauCeti.dense_setOf_stabilizer_eq_ker.{u_1, u_3, u_4} {G : Type u_1} [Group G] (R : Type u_3)
  {V : Type u_4} [Ring R] [TopologicalSpace R] [(nhdsWithin 0 {r | IsUnit r}).NeBot]
  [AddCommGroup V] [_root_.Module R V] [TopologicalSpace V] [ContinuousAdd V] [ContinuousSMul R V]
  [DistribMulAction G V] [SMulCommClass G R V] [T2Space V] [ContinuousConstSMul G V] [Finite G] :
  Dense {v | MulAction.stabilizer G v = (MulAction.toPermHom G V).ker}
TauCeti.dense_setOf_stabilizer_eq_ker.doc:
**Generic stabilizer of a finite linear action.** For a finite group acting linearly and
continuously on a Hausdorff topological module over a ring in which `0` is a limit of units, for
instance a finite-dimensional real vector space, the points whose stabilizer is the kernel of the
action form a dense set. The action need not be faithful. The set is also open, by
`TauCeti.isOpen_setOf_stabilizer_eq_ker`.

TauCeti.dense_setOf_exists_norm_apply_eq.doc:
**The Bishop–Phelps theorem.** The continuous linear functionals on a Banach space which
attain their norm on the closed unit ball are norm dense in the dual.

  {U V : TopologicalSpace.Opens M} {ρ : ↥(U ⊔ V) → ℝ}
  (hρ : ContMDiff I (modelWithCornersSelf ℝ ℝ) (↑⊤) ρ) (hρV : tsupport ρ ⊆ {x | ↑x ∈ V})
  (hρU : (tsupport fun x => 1 - ρ x) ⊆ {x | ↑x ∈ U}) (φ : ↥(TauCeti.closedForms I (↥(U ⊓ V)) k))

    ↑↑σ =
      TauCeti.RoughForm.extendByZero (U ⊔ V)

TauCeti.deRhamCohomology.mayerVietorisδ_.doc:
**The Mayer–Vietoris connecting map through a cut-off function.** Let `ρ` be a smooth function
on `U ⊔ V` supported in `V` such that `1 - ρ` is supported in `U`, and let `φ` be a closed form on
`U ⊓ V`. If `σ` is the closed form on `U ⊔ V` extending `d(ρ φ)` by zero
(`TauCeti.exists_closedForms_coe_eq_extendByZero_mextDeriv`), then the connecting map sends the
class of `φ` to the class of `σ`.

TauCeti.deRhamCohomology.map_eq_of_homot.doc:
**Homotopy invariance of de Rham cohomology.** If `F : M × [0, 1] → M'` is a smooth
homotopy from `f` to `g`, then `f` and `g` induce the same map on de Rham cohomology. The source
`M` may have boundary or corners.

TauCeti.cyclicTwoCohomPolynomialEquiv.signature:
TauCeti.cyclicTwoCohomPolynomialEquiv.{u} (G : Type u) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
  [IsTopologicalGroup G] [DiscreteTopology G] (hG : Nat.card G = 2) :
  Polynomial (ZMod 2) ≃ₐ[ZMod 2] TauCeti.gradedCohomF2 G
TauCeti.cyclicTwoCohomPolynomialEquiv.doc:
The canonical graded mod-two cohomology algebra of an order-two discrete group is a
polynomial algebra, with `X` sent to its nontrivial character in degree one.

TauCeti.cyclicModuleRootPowProjectiveRes.signature:
TauCeti.cyclicModuleRootPowProjectiveResolution.{u} (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (n i : ℕ) :
  CategoryTheory.ProjectiveResolution
    ↧((AdjoinRoot (Polynomial.X ^ n))ᵐᵒᵖ ⧸
        Ideal.span {MulOpposite.op (AdjoinRoot.root (Polynomial.X ^ n) ^ i)})
TauCeti.cyclicModuleRootPowProjectiveRes.doc:
**The periodic free resolution of `M_i` over `R[X]/(X ^ n)`.** With `x` the class of `X`
and `M_i = A ⧸ (x ^ i)`, the complex
`⋯ ⟶ A --x^(n-i)--> A --x^i--> A --x^(n-i)--> A --x^i--> A ⟶ M_i ⟶ 0` is a projective
resolution of `M_i`.

TauCeti.cyclicConnectingEquiv.doc:
**The connecting isomorphism `H¹(C_m, T) ≃ H²(C_m, Λ)`.** When multiplication by `m` is
bijective on `E`, for instance when `E` is a real vector space, the cohomology of `E` vanishes in
positive degrees and the connecting homomorphism of `0 → Λ → E → T → 0` is an isomorphism.

TauCeti.cyclicCohomology.selfEquiv.signature:
TauCeti.cyclicCohomology.selfEquiv.{u, u_1} (R : Type u) (M : Type u_1) [CommRing R]
  [AddCommGroup M] [_root_.Module R M] {n : ℕ} (hn : Even n) (h2 : IsSMulRegular M 2) :
  M ≃ₗ[R] ↑(TauCeti.cyclicCohomology R R M n)
TauCeti.cyclicCohomology.selfEquiv.doc:
If multiplication by `2` is injective on `M`, then `HCⁿ(R; M) ≅ M` in every even degree `n`,
by the class of the product cochain. In particular `HC²ᵏ(ℂ) ≅ ℂ`.

TauCeti.cyclicCohomology.oddPairing_matr.doc:
**Stabilization of the odd pairing**: enlarging an invertible matrix `u` to the block diagonal
matrix `u ⊕ 1` does not change its odd pairing.

TauCeti.cyclicCohomology.oddPairing.signature:
TauCeti.cyclicCohomology.oddPairing.{u_1, u_2} {A : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [Ring A] [Algebra ℂ A]
  [AddCommGroup M] [_root_.Module ℂ M] (u : Aˣ) (m : ℕ) :

TauCeti.cyclicCohomology.oddPairing.doc:
**Connes' odd pairing** `⟨[u], [φ]⟩ = (1 + i)⁻¹ 2⁻ⁿ Γ(n/2 + 1)⁻¹ φ(u⁻¹ - 1, u - 1, …, u - 1)`
of an invertible `u` with cyclic cohomology classes of odd degree `n = 2m + 1`.

TauCeti.cyclicCohomology.matrixExtension.{u_4, u_5, u_6, u_7} {R : Type u_4} {A : Type u_5}
  (M : Type u_6) [AddCommGroup M] (ι : Type u_7) [Fintype ι] (n : ℕ) [CommRing R]

TauCeti.cyclicCohomology.matrixExtension.doc:
The map `HCⁿ(A; M) → HCⁿ(Matrix ι ι A; M)` on cyclic cohomology induced by matrix extension of
cyclic cocycles.

TauCeti.cyclicCohomology.evenPairing_uni.signature:
TauCeti.cyclicCohomology.evenPairing_units_conj.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2}
  {M : Type u_3} [Field R] [CharZero R] [Ring A] [Algebra R A] [AddCommGroup M] [_root_.Module R M]
  (u : Aˣ) {e : A} (he : IsIdempotentElem e) (hue : IsIdempotentElem (↑u * e * ↑u⁻¹)) (m : ℕ) :

    TauCeti.cyclicCohomology.evenPairing e he m
TauCeti.cyclicCohomology.evenPairing_uni.doc:
**Conjugation invariance of the even pairing.** Conjugating an idempotent by a unit does not
change its even pairing with cyclic cohomology.

TauCeti.cycleCocycle.doc: The character of a cycle, as a cyclic cocycle.

TauCeti.cwComplexPreimage.signature:
TauCeti.cwComplexPreimage.{u} {E B : Type u} [TopologicalSpace B] {p : E → B} (C : Set B)
  [TopologicalSpace E] [Topology.CWComplex C] [T2Space B] (hp : IsCoveringMap p) :
  Topology.CWComplex (p ⁻¹' C)
TauCeti.cwComplexPreimage.doc:
**A CW structure lifts along a covering map.** If `C` is a CW complex in the Hausdorff space
`B` and `p : E → B` is a covering map, then `p ⁻¹' C` is a CW complex in `E`. Its `n`-cells are the
pairs of an `n`-cell of `C` and a point of `E` over the centre of that cell
(`TauCeti.cellPreimageEquiv`); the characteristic map of such a pair is the lift of the
characteristic map of the cell through `p` sending the centre to the chosen point.

TauCeti.cup_kummerClass_eq_hilbertSymbol.signature:
TauCeti.cup_kummerClass_eq_hilbertSymbol_smul.{u} {K : Type u} [Field K] [ValuativeRel K]

  (((TauCeti.trivialF2TopPairing (TauCeti.AbsoluteGaloisGroup K)).cup 1 1) (TauCeti.kummerClass a))
      (TauCeti.kummerClass b) =
    TauCeti.additiveIntUnitsAddEquiv (Additive.ofMul (TauCeti.hilbertSymbol a b)) •

          (TauCeti.kummerClass c))
        (TauCeti.kummerClass e)
TauCeti.cup_kummerClass_eq_hilbertSymbol.doc:
**A Kummer cup over a local field is its Hilbert symbol times a fixed nonzero cup**: if
`(c, e)_K = -1`, then `(a) ∪ (b) = ε • ((c) ∪ (e))`, where `ε ∈ ZMod 2` is `0` if `(a, b)_K = 1`
and `1` if `(a, b)_K = -1`.

TauCeti.criticalHessian.signature:
TauCeti.criticalHessian.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {E : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [TopologicalSpace H] [TopologicalSpace M]
  [ChartedSpace H M] (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H) (f : M → ℝ) (x : M) :
  TangentSpace I x →L[ℝ] TangentSpace I x →L[ℝ] ℝ
TauCeti.criticalHessian.doc:
The **critical Hessian** of a real function `f` at a point `x` of a manifold: the second
derivative at `extChartAt I x x` of the coordinate expression of `f` in the preferred extended
chart, as a bilinear form on the tangent space at `x`.

Like `TauCeti.manifoldMorseIndex`, the definition makes sense at every point and carries no
regularity hypotheses. At a critical point of a `C²` function on a manifold without boundary it is
intrinsic: `TauCeti.criticalHessian_apply_eq_of_mem_maximalAtlas` computes it in an arbitrary chart
there. At a noncritical point it depends on the preferred chart, and on a manifold with boundary
or corners it may also depend on the chart inverse outside `range I`.

TauCeti.countable_infEquivAt_nat_iff_iso.doc:
**Karp's theorem for countable structures.** Countable structures in a relational language are
isomorphic exactly when they satisfy the same `L_{ω₁ω}` sentences, the infinitary sentences whose
conjunctions and disjunctions are indexed by `ℕ`.

TauCeti.convexSection.signature:
TauCeti.convexSection.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [AddCommGroup E] [_root_.Module ℝ E] (Ω : Set E)
  (u : E → ℝ) (x : E) (ℓ : E →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (h : ℝ) : Set E
TauCeti.convexSection.doc: The section of `u` on `Ω` at `x`, with slope `ℓ` and strict height `h`.

  Continuous ⇑(TauCeti.restrictedProductSum U hT₁ hT₂).symm
TauCeti.continuous_restrictedProductSum_.doc:
For a principal filter on `ι₁ ⊕ ι₂` the inverse of the splitting is continuous for every
reference family, so that the splitting is a homeomorphism: the target is a principal stage,
whose topology is induced from the product.

TauCeti.continuous_rationalDiagonal.signature:
TauCeti.continuous_rationalDiagonal.{u, v, w} {ι : Type u} {G : ι → Type v} [(i : ι) → Group (G i)]
  {Γ : Type w} [MulOneClass Γ] [TopologicalSpace Γ] [(i : ι) → TopologicalSpace (G i)]
  (φ : (i : ι) → Γ →* G i) (U : (i : ι) → Subgroup (G i))
  (h : ∀ (γ : Γ), ∀ᶠ (i : ι) in Filter.cofinite, (φ i) γ ∈ U i)
  (hcont : ∀ (i : ι), Continuous ⇑(φ i)) (S : Set ι) (hS : S ∈ Filter.cofinite)
  (huniform : ∀ (γ : Γ), ∀ i ∈ S, (φ i) γ ∈ U i) : Continuous ⇑(TauCeti.rationalDiagonal φ U h)
TauCeti.continuous_rationalDiagonal.doc:
The diagonal is continuous when the coordinate maps are continuous and there is one cofinite
set of indices at which every `γ` is integral. Pointwise eventual integrality alone builds the
map but is not enough for continuity, because the restricted-product topology is finer than the
topology induced from the full product.

TauCeti.continuous_outerAction.signature:
TauCeti.continuous_outerAction.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [Group E] [TopologicalSpace E] {N : Subgroup E}
  [N.Normal] [IsTopologicalGroup E] [CompactSpace ↥N] : Continuous ⇑(TauCeti.outerAction N)
TauCeti.continuous_outerAction.doc:
For compact `N`, the outer action `E ⧸ N → ContinuousOut N` is continuous for the quotient
topologies.

TauCeti.continuous_eval_and_not_continuo.signature:
TauCeti.continuous_eval_and_not_continuous_rationalDiagonal_range_coeMonoidHom.{u, v} {ι : Type u}
  {G : ι → Type v} [(i : ι) → Group (G i)] [(i : ι) → TopologicalSpace (G i)]

discrete groups with trivial reference subgroups, infinitely many of them nontrivial, and for `Γ`

continuous and every element of `Γ` is eventually integral (it is the coercion of an element of

it would make the restricted-product topology the one induced from the full product,
contradicting `not_isInducing_coe_bot`.

`s * ∫_{1}^{∞} (∑_{N(I) ≤ t} χ(I)) t ^ (-(s + 1)) dt`.

For free properly discontinuous actions by `C^n` maps on `C^n` manifolds and `m ≤ n`, a
`C^m` map carrying one action to the other along `σ` induces a `C^m` map of orbit spaces.

TauCeti.contMDiff_iff_mdifferentiable.doc:
A map between complex manifolds is `C^n`, for any `n ≠ 0`, if and only if it is
holomorphic.

For a boundaryless model on a finite-dimensional complex space, the `C^m` and `C^n` groupoids
agree whenever `m` and `n` are nonzero.

in `ℂ^N`: a line belongs to it when every polynomial of the family vanishes at every vector of
the line. The line of `L` is `L.submodule`, which is the underlying submodule of
`Projectivization.equivSubmodule ℂ (Fin N → ℂ) L`.

TauCeti.compactlySupportedDeRhamCohomolo.doc:
Integration `H^n_c(M) → ℝ` over an oriented boundaryless manifold, induced by integrating
compactly supported closed top forms.

The map on compactly supported de Rham cohomology induced by extension by zero along an
inclusion `U ≤ W` of open subsets of a Hausdorff manifold.

supported de Rham complex.

the coextension of scalars `Hom_R(A, V)`, which is the module of continuous `R`-linear maps

(`TauCeti.mem_smoothPart_coextendScalars_iff_continuous`).

the singular homology `Hₙ(BG; k)` of Milnor's classifying space with coefficients in a
commutative ring `k` is Mathlib's group homology `Hₙ(G, k)` of the trivial representation. It
comes from the free resolution of `k` by the singular chains of `universalGSpace G`.

TauCeti.classifyingSpaceSingularCohomolo.doc:
**The singular cohomology of the classifying space is group cohomology**: for every group
`G`, the singular cohomology `Hⁿ(BG; M)` of Milnor's classifying space with coefficients in a
module `M` over a commutative ring `k` is Mathlib's group cohomology `Hⁿ(G, M)` of the trivial
representation `M`. It comes from the free resolution of `k` by the singular chains of
`universalGSpace G`.

`orthonormal_normalizedChebyshevTLp`; completeness is
`orthogonal_span_normalizedChebyshevTLp_eq_bot`.

TauCeti.chebyshevTEnvelopeHilbertBasis.signature:
