TauCeti.Multiquadratic.genusCharFunNarro.doc:
**The genus character on the narrow class group.**

For a factor `t` of a prime-discriminant factorization, this is the homomorphism
`Cl⁺(K) → ℤˣ` obtained by evaluating a coprime integral representative. Its definition is
independent of the representative by `genusCharFunCoprimeIdealHom_eq_of_mk0_eq`.

TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_adjoin_ra.doc:
**Degree of a multiquadratic field over a finite index.** If no nonempty subset product of
the radicands `d i` is a square in `K`, then `[K(rootᵢ : i) : K] = 2^|ι|`.

TauCeti.Multiquadratic.candidateGenusFie.doc:
**The candidate genus field is cut out of the cyclotomic field by the genus characters.** For
squarefree `d` with fundamental discriminant `D` and a cyclotomic subfield `K ⊆ ℂ` of level `|D|`,
the candidate genus field of `ℚ(√d)` is the image in `ℂ` of the intermediate field of `K` that the
character correspondence attaches to the genus character group of `D`. The correspondence is
taken for the abelian Galois structure of the cyclotomic extension.

TauCeti.Multiquadratic.autCandidateGenus.doc:
**The genus-field isomorphism `Gal(K_gen/K) ≅ Cl⁺(K)/Cl⁺(K)²`.** For a squarefree integer `d`
that is not a rational square, the Galois group of the candidate genus field over its embedded
quadratic base `K = ℚ(√d)` is isomorphic to the maximal elementary-`2` quotient of the narrow class
group of `K`. Both are the space of even-parity sign patterns on the prime discriminants dividing
`disc K`: the Galois group by its sign patterns, the class group by its genus characters.

The map is pinned down coordinate for coordinate on those prime discriminants: it sends an
automorphism `σ` to the unique narrow class modulo squares whose genus characters are the signs
that `σ` puts on the chosen square roots
(`autCandidateGenusFieldEquivNarrowElementaryTwoQuotient_apply` together with
`narrowElementaryTwoQuotientEquivRelativeSign_apply_coe`). Its identification with the inverse
Artin map of `K_gen / K` is not proved here; see the module docstring.

TauCeti.ModularSymbols.periodMap_injecti.doc:
**Periods determine a cusp form.** For a finite-index subgroup of `SL(2, ℤ)` and weight
`k = w + 2 ≥ 2`, the period map into the dual of the modular symbols over `R` is injective.
In particular this applies to the integral modular symbols (`R = ℤ`).

  (hk : k = ↑w + 2) :

TauCeti.ModularSymbols.periodMap.doc:
The **period map** `S_k(Γ) →ₗ[ℂ] (𝕄_w(Γ; R) →ₗ[R] ℂ)` for `k = w + 2`: a cusp form `f` on
`Γ` is sent to the `R`-linear functional on the modular symbols induced by its raw period
pairing, so that `{α, β} ⊗ P ↦ ∫_β^α f(z) P(z, 1) dz`. For `R = ℤ` this is
the pairing of cusp forms with the integral modular symbols.

TauCeti.ModularSymbols.signature:
TauCeti.ModularSymbols.{u_1} (R : Type u_1) [CommRing R]

The **module of modular symbols** `𝕄_w(Γ; R) = (Div⁰(ℙ¹(ℚ)) ⊗_R Sym^w(R²))_Γ` of weight
`w + 2` for a subgroup `Γ ≤ SL(2, ℤ)`, with coefficients in `R`: the `Γ`-coinvariants of the
degree-zero divisors on the cusps tensored with the binary forms of degree `w`.

This is an abbreviation for the coinvariants, so that their universal property
(`Representation.Coinvariants.lift`, `Representation.Coinvariants.hom_ext`) applies directly.

The normalized modular invariant identifies the compactified level-one modular quotient
biholomorphically with the Riemann sphere.

TauCeti.ModularForm.valence_formula_fini.doc:
**The valence formula at general level**: for a nonzero weight-`k` form on a finite-index
`Γ ≤ SL(2, ℤ)`, the interior orders — weighted by `2 / |Stab_Γ P|` — together with the orders
indexed by the cusp translation orbits add up to `k · [SL(2, ℤ) : Γ] / 12`.

This is `valence_formula_finiteIndex_norm` with its cusp term, an order at `∞` on the norm,
distributed over the cusps of `Γ`.

TauCeti.ModularForm.siegelFunction.doc:
**The Siegel function** `g_r(τ)` attached to `r = (r₁, r₂) ∈ ℝ²`:
`g_r(τ) = -e^{π i B₂(r₁) τ} e^{π i r₂ (r₁ - 1)} (1 - w) ∏_{n ≥ 1} (1 - qⁿ w) (1 - qⁿ w⁻¹)`
with `q = e^{2π i τ}`, `w = e^{2π i (r₁ τ + r₂)}` and `B₂ = bernoulliFun 2` the second Bernoulli
polynomial `x² - x + 1/6`. The product converges for `τ` in the upper half-plane, where `g_r` is
holomorphic; elsewhere the value is a junk value.

TauCeti.MetricMeasureSpace.MeasureContra.signature:
TauCeti.MetricMeasureSpace.MeasureContraction.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} [MetricSpace X]

  (M : TauCeti.MetricMeasureSpace X) (K N : ℝ) : Prop
TauCeti.MetricMeasureSpace.MeasureContra.doc:
The **measure-contraction property** `MCP(K, N)` of Ohta and Sturm, in the form of
Cavalletti–Mondino: for every point `o` of the support of the reference measure `m` and every
measurable `A` with `0 < m(A) < ∞`, some dynamic plan `η` concentrated on geodesics has law
`m[|A] = m(A)⁻¹ m|_A` at time `0` and law `δ_o` at time `1`, and for every time `t` the law at
time `t` of `η` weighted by `τ_{K,N}^{(1-t)}(d(γ₀, γ₁))^N` is at most `m(A)⁻¹ m`.

Such a plan is automatically optimal, since `m[|A]` and `δ_o` have only one coupling.

Gaussian decay and automatically for compactly supported measures.

The endpoint map of a mapping-path replacement is a Hurewicz fibration, for test spaces in
every universe.

A reference path `α` from `f b` to `k` makes the fibre of the source projection over `b`
homotopy equivalent to the loop space `Ω K k`. A path `γ` from `f b` to `k` is sent to the loop

**The first variation of the Levi-Civita connection.** Let `g_s` be a family of smooth
nondegenerate metrics, jointly `C²` in `(s, y)` at `(t, x)`, with parameter derivative
`h = ∂ₛ g_s` at `s = t`, and let `∇ˢ` be a Levi-Civita connection of `g_s` for every `s`. Then for
every vector field `Y` which is differentiable at `x` and all `v, w ∈ T_x M`,

`2 g_t((∂ₜ∇)_v Y, w) = (∇ᵗ_v h)(Y, w) + (∇ᵗ_Y h)(v, w) - (∇ᵗ_w h)(v, Y)`,

where `(∂ₜ∇)_v Y` is the derivative at `t` of `s ↦ ∇ˢ_v Y` and `∇ᵗh` is the covariant derivative
`CovariantDerivative.derivBilinearTensor` of `h` along `∇ᵗ`.

TauCeti.Manifold.tfae_expDomain_eq_univ.doc:
**The Hopf–Rinow theorem.**  For a point `p` of a Riemannian manifold `M` whose distance is
the Riemannian distance, the following are equivalent:
the exponential map at `p` is defined on all of `T_p M`; `M` is proper; `M` is complete;
every maximal geodesic of `M` is defined for all time; and `M` has an increasing exhaustion by
compact sets `K n` such that `dist p (q n) → ∞` whenever `q n ∉ K n` for every `n`.

**The variational characterization of geodesics.** On a boundaryless `C^n` manifold with
`2 ≤ n ≤ ∞`, a curve which is `C^n` near every point of `[a, b]` is a critical point of the energy

the open interval between `a` and `b`.  For `n = ∞`: a smooth curve is critical among smooth
variations exactly when it is a geodesic.

compact manifold, a family of metrics of positive scalar curvature indexed by a compact space, whose
chart metrics have Gram matrices, first and second derivatives in the basis `b` depending
continuously on the parameter and the chart point, has scalar curvature bounded below by a common
positive constant.

TauCeti.Manifold.ContMDiffNondegenerateM.doc:
A smooth family, parametrized by `P`, of symmetric nondegenerate real bilinear forms on the
tangent bundle of `M`.

The family is a native smooth section over `P × M` of the pullback of the tangent
bilinear-form bundle of `M` along the projection `P × M → M`; its value at `(p, x)` is a bilinear
form on `T_x M`. As for a single metric, no positivity or signature is imposed.

The Levi-Civita connection of a smooth symmetric nondegenerate metric. It is chosen to
vanish on vector fields that are not differentiable at the evaluation point.

subextension can be chosen with trivial upper ramification groups at every later index, so the
specified break is its last break. Its local-field structures are the canonical ones induced
from the base field.

**Every invariant bilinear form on a Lie algebra is a multiple of the Killing form**, for a
finite-dimensional Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field whose adjoint module is
irreducible and whose Killing form is nondegenerate, such as a simple Lie algebra in
characteristic zero.

class of the Killing form.** Here `L` is a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over an algebraically
closed field of characteristic zero whose adjoint module is irreducible and whose Killing form is

`smul_twoCochainOfBilinear_mem_range_d₁₂_iff`, this says that the second cohomology of
`loopAlgebra K ℤ L` with trivial coefficients is one-dimensional.

TauCeti.LazardRing.gradedLift.signature:
TauCeti.LazardRing.gradedLift.{u_1, u_5} {A : Type u_1} [CommRing A] {σ : Type u_5} [SetLike σ A]

        ∀ (d : Fin 2 →₀ ℕ),
          (MvPowerSeries.coeff d) F.toPowerSeries ∈ 𝒜 (2 * (Finsupp.degree d - 1)) } ≃

TauCeti.LazardRing.gradedLift.doc:
**The graded universal property of the Lazard ring**: for a commutative ring `A` graded by
`𝒜`, graded ring homomorphisms `L →+*ᵍ A` correspond to commutative formal group laws over `A`
whose coefficient of every monomial `X^(d 0) Y^(d 1)` lies in `𝒜 (2 (d 0 + d 1 - 1))`, that is,
whose coefficient `aᵢⱼ` lies in `𝒜 (2 (i + j - 1))` for all `i, j ≥ 1`. A formal group law
corresponds to the homomorphism `TauCeti.LazardRing.lift` classifying it.

TauCeti.LazardRing.cotangentBasis.doc:
**Lazard's computation of the indecomposables of the Lazard ring.** The `ℤ`-module
`I ⧸ I²` of indecomposables of `L`, for `I` the augmentation ideal, is free with basis the classes
of the generators `xₙ ∈ L₂ₙ`, `n ≥ 1`.

TauCeti.LazardRing.coproduct_coassoc.doc:
**Coassociativity** `(Δ ⊗ id) Δ = (id ⊗ Δ) Δ` of the coproduct: composition of strict
isomorphisms is associative. Both sides take values in the triple tensor product
`Γ ⊗_L Γ ⊗_L Γ = MvPolynomial ℕ+ (Γ ⊗_L Γ)`, the pushout of `Γ ⊗_L Γ` along the target of its right
factor and of `Γ` along `η_L`, whose three factors are `C ∘ C`, `C ∘ MvPolynomial.map η_R` and
`MvPolynomial.map (MvPolynomial.map η_R ∘ η_R)`. In it, `Δ ⊗ id` is `tensorLift (C ∘ Δ, ι₃)` with
`ι₃` the third factor, and `id ⊗ Δ` is `tensorLift (C ∘ C, ι₂₃ ∘ Δ)` with
`ι₂₃ = MvPolynomial.map (MvPolynomial.map η_R)` the inclusion of the last two factors.

TauCeti.LazardRing.coordinateChangeLift.doc:
**Strict coordinate changes of commutative formal group laws are representable**: pairs of a
commutative formal group law `F` and a strict coordinate `φ` over `R` correspond to ring
homomorphisms `L[b₁, b₂, …] →+* R`. The homomorphism attached to `(F, φ)` restricts to the
homomorphism `L →+* R` classifying `F` and sends `bᵢ` to the coefficient of `X^(i + 1)` in `φ`.

series `φ` of zero constant coefficient multiplies the residue of `f dX` by `φ.order.toNat`, in all
characteristics: `Res(f(φ) Dφ dX) = φ.order.toNat • Res(f dX)`.

TauCeti.LaurentSeries.Level.algEquivOfFi.doc:
**Finite extensions of `K⸨X⸩`.** If `K` is algebraically closed of characteristic zero, then
every extension `L` of `K⸨X⸩` of degree `e` is isomorphic over `K⸨X⸩` to the ramified level
`K⸨u⸩`, `u ^ e = X`. The isomorphism is a chosen one: it is built from a chosen embedding of `L`
into the Puiseux field, whose image is the level-`e` subfield.

  (hF : ∀ (s : ℂ), 1 < s.re → LSeriesHasSum (fun n => ↑(a n)) s (F s))
  (hG : ContinuousOn G {s | 1 ≤ s.re}) (hGF : ∀ (s : ℂ), 1 < s.re → G s = F s - ↑κ / (s - 1)) :

TauCeti.LSeries.wienerIkehara.doc:
**The Wiener--Ikehara theorem.** Let `a n ≥ 0` have Dirichlet series with sum `F s` on
`Re s > 1`, and let `G` be continuous on `Re s ≥ 1` with `G s = F s - κ / (s - 1)` on `Re s > 1`.
Then `x⁻¹ ∑_{1 ≤ n ≤ x} a n → κ` as `x → ∞`.

TauCeti.LSeries.tendsto_integral_newmanD.signature:
TauCeti.LSeries.tendsto_integral_newmanDetour_mul_kernel {R δ : ℝ} {G : ℂ → ℂ} (hR : 0 < R)

on the detour `newmanDetour R δ` with `R, δ > 0`, then the detour integral of `G` against Newman's
kernel `exp (T z) (1 + z² / R²) / z` tends to `0` as `T → ∞`.

TauCeti.LSeries.stepCorrection_zero.doc: **The step correction at `0`:** `stepCorrection a 0 = ∑' n, a n (log (1 + 1 / n) - 1 / n)`.

TauCeti.LSeries.newmanLaplace_tendsto_in.signature:
TauCeti.LSeries.newmanLaplace_tendsto_integral {f : ℝ → ℂ} {G : ℂ → ℂ} {M : ℝ} {Ω : Set ℂ}
  (hf : MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable f (MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.Ici 0)))
  (hbound : ∀ t ∈ Set.Ici 0, ‖f t‖ ≤ M) (hΩ : IsOpen Ω) (hcover : {z | 0 ≤ z.re} ⊆ Ω)
  (hG : DifferentiableOn ℂ G Ω)
  (hLaplace : ∀ (z : ℂ), 0 < z.re → G z = ∫ (t : ℝ) in Set.Ici 0, f t * Complex.exp (-z * ↑t)) :
  Filter.Tendsto (fun T => ∫ (t : ℝ) in 0..T, f t) Filter.atTop (nhds (G 0))
TauCeti.LSeries.newmanLaplace_tendsto_in.doc:
**Newman's Tauberian theorem.** Let `f : ℝ → ℂ` be measurable and bounded on `[0, ∞)`, and
let `G` be holomorphic on an open set `Ω` containing the closed half-plane `0 ≤ re z`, agreeing
with the Laplace transform `∫ t in Ici 0, f t * exp (-z t)` on the open half-plane `0 < re z`.
Then `∫ t in 0..T, f t` converges to `G 0` as `T → ∞`.

TauCeti.LSeries.newmanDetour.doc:
**Newman's left detour.** The parabolic arc `s ↦ -δ (1 - s²) - R s I`, which on `[-1, 1]`
runs from `R * I` to `-R * I`; for `R, δ ≥ 0` it stays in the strip `-δ ≤ re z ≤ 0`,
`|im z| ≤ R`.

TauCeti.LSeries.integral_right_semicircl.signature:
TauCeti.LSeries.integral_right_semicircle_add_integral_newmanDetour_mul_kernel {f : ℝ → ℂ}
  {G : ℂ → ℂ} {T R δ : ℝ} {U : Set ℂ} (hf : IntervalIntegrable f MeasureTheory.volume 0 T)
  (hR : 0 < R) (hδ : 0 < δ) (hU : IsOpen U) (hconv : Convex ℝ U) (hG : DifferentiableOn ℂ G U)
  (hcirc : ∀ θ ∈ Set.Icc (-Real.pi / 2) (Real.pi / 2), circleMap 0 R θ ∈ U)
  (hdet : ∀ s ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, TauCeti.LSeries.newmanDetour R δ s ∈ U) :
  (∫ (θ : ℝ) in -Real.pi / 2..Real.pi / 2,
        circleMap 0 R θ * Complex.I *
          ((G (circleMap 0 R θ) - ∫ (t : ℝ) in 0..T, f t * Complex.exp (-circleMap 0 R θ * ↑t)) *
                Complex.exp (↑T * circleMap 0 R θ) *
              (1 + circleMap 0 R θ ^ 2 / ↑R ^ 2) /
            circleMap 0 R θ)) +
      ∫ (s : ℝ) in -1..1,
        deriv (TauCeti.LSeries.newmanDetour R δ) s *
          (G (TauCeti.LSeries.newmanDetour R δ s) *
                Complex.exp (↑T * TauCeti.LSeries.newmanDetour R δ s) *
              (1 + TauCeti.LSeries.newmanDetour R δ s ^ 2 / ↑R ^ 2) /
            TauCeti.LSeries.newmanDetour R δ s) =
    2 * ↑Real.pi * Complex.I * (G 0 - ∫ (t : ℝ) in 0..T, f t) +
      ∫ (θ : ℝ) in Real.pi / 2..3 * Real.pi / 2,
        circleMap 0 R θ * Complex.I *
          ((∫ (t : ℝ) in 0..T, f t * Complex.exp (-circleMap 0 R θ * ↑t)) *

              (1 + circleMap 0 R θ ^ 2 / ↑R ^ 2) /
            circleMap 0 R θ)
TauCeti.LSeries.integral_right_semicircl.doc:
**Newman's contour identity.** Let `G` be holomorphic on an open convex set `U` containing
the right semicircle of radius `R > 0` and the detour `newmanDetour R δ` with `δ > 0`, and let
`G_T z = ∫ t in 0..T, f t * exp (-z t)`. Against Newman's kernel
`k_T z = exp (T z) (1 + z² / R²) / z`, the right semicircle integral of `(G - G_T) k_T`
(counterclockwise from `-R * I` to `R * I`) plus the detour integral of `G k_T` (from `R * I`
back to `-R * I`) equals `2πi (G 0 - ∫ t in 0..T, f t)` plus the left semicircle integral of
`G_T k_T` (counterclockwise from `R * I` to `-R * I`). All integrals include the velocity of
their parametrization.

  (hcover : {z | 0 ≤ z.re} ⊆ Ω) (hR : 0 ≤ R) :
  ∃ δ > 0,
    ∃ U ⊆ Ω,
      IsOpen U ∧
        Convex ℝ U ∧
          (∀ θ ∈ Set.Icc (-Real.pi / 2) (Real.pi / 2), circleMap 0 R θ ∈ U) ∧

TauCeti.LSeries.exists_convex_newmanDeto.doc:
**The detour inside the continuation domain.** If `Ω` is open and contains the closed
half-plane `0 ≤ re z`, then for some `δ > 0` the right semicircle of radius `R` and the detour
`newmanDetour R δ` lie in a common open convex subset of `Ω`.

  (hG : DifferentiableOn ℂ G Ω)
  (hLaplace : ∀ (z : ℂ), 0 < z.re → G z = ∫ (t : ℝ) in Set.Ici 0, f t * Complex.exp (-z * ↑t))

TauCeti.LSeries.eventually_norm_sub_inte.doc:
**Newman's estimate at a fixed radius.** Let `f` be measurable and bounded by `M` on
`[0, ∞)`, and let `G` be holomorphic on an open set `Ω` containing the closed half-plane
`0 ≤ re z` and equal to the Laplace transform of `f` on `0 < re z`. For every `R > 0` and
`ε > 0`, eventually in `T`, `‖G 0 - ∫ t in 0..T, f t‖ ≤ 2 M / R + ε`.

TauCeti.LSeries.differentiableOn_stepCor.doc:
**Holomorphy of the step correction.** For coefficients bounded from `n = 1` on, the step
correction is holomorphic on the half-plane `-1 < re z`: near `z₀`, the terms are bounded
uniformly by a multiple of the summable `n ^ (-1 - ε)` for `ε = (re z₀ + 1) / 2`.

TauCeti.LFunctions.primeIdealVonMangoldt.signature:

TauCeti.LFunctions.primeIdealVonMangoldt.doc:
**Boundary data for all primes of a number field.** The von Mangoldt series of all primes of
`K` sums to `-ζ_K'(s)/ζ_K(s)` on `Re s > 1`, and `-ζ_K'(s)/ζ_K(s) - 1/(s - 1)` extends continuously
to `Re s ≥ 1` (`TauCeti.exists_continuousOn_eq_neg_deriv_dedekindZeta_div_sub`).

TauCeti.Khovanov.quantumGrading.{u} (R : Type u) [CommRing R] :

TauCeti.Khovanov.quantumGrading.doc:
The **quantum grading** of the Khovanov Frobenius algebra `R[ε]`: the basis vector `1` spans
degree `1`, the basis vector `ε` spans degree `-1`, and every other degree is zero. It is the
grading of the free module on the basis `1, ε` by `TauCeti.Khovanov.quantumDegree`, transported
to `R[ε]`.

TauCeti.Khovanov.isFrobenius.{u_1} (R : Type u_1) [CommSemiring R] :
  Coalgebra.IsFrobenius R (DualNumber R)
TauCeti.Khovanov.isFrobenius.doc: The dual numbers with the Khovanov comultiplication satisfy the Frobenius equation.

TauCeti.Khovanov.fiberwiseSplit.doc:
The split map along `f`, adjoint to multiplication along its fibres. It maps the tensor
on `τ` to the tensor on `σ`; a two-element fibre splits that circle.

TauCeti.Khovanov.CircleTensor.signature:

  Type (max u u_1)
TauCeti.Khovanov.CircleTensor.doc:
The **circle tensor** of a finite set `ι` of circles: the tensor product of one copy of the
Khovanov Frobenius algebra `R[ε]` for each circle. It is a commutative `R`-algebra.

TauCeti.Iwasawa.ker_levelCoordinate.doc:
**The kernel of the level coordinate** is the principal ideal generated by
`ω_n = (1 + T) ^ pⁿ - 1`.

**The level coordinates separate points**: over a noetherian `O`, the product
`O⟦T⟧ → ∏ₙ O[ℤ/pⁿ]` of the level maps is injective.

TauCeti.Isogeny.zetaFunction_eq.doc:
**Isogenous curves over a finite field have the same zeta function**
`Z(W/F, T) = exp (∑_{n ≥ 1} #W(𝔽_{qⁿ}) Tⁿ / n)`.

**The `φ`-descent sequence is exact at `H¹(G_K, E₁[φ])`**: the kernel of
`H¹(G_K, E₁[φ]) → H¹(G_K, E₁)[φ]` is the image of `E₂(K) ⧸ φ(E₁(K))` under the Kummer map.
Together with `TauCeti.Isogeny.kummerClassMap_injective` and
`TauCeti.Isogeny.kerCoeffInclH1_surjective` this is the short exact sequence
`0 → E₂(K) ⧸ φ(E₁(K)) → H¹(G_K, E₁[φ]) → H¹(G_K, E₁)[φ] → 0`.

TauCeti.IsSolidTorusNeighborhood.framing.doc:
The **framing number** of the solid torus neighbourhood `Φ`: the longitude of `Φ` is
homologous in the knot complement to `framingNumber` times the meridian. Equivalently, the
longitude of `Φ` is `λ₀ + n · μ` for the preferred longitude `λ₀`
(`TauCeti.IsSolidTorusNeighborhood.preferredFramedBoundaryTorus_basis_one`). For a knot in `S³`
it is the linking number of the longitude of `Φ` with the knot.

TauCeti.IsSemianalytic.preimage.signature:
TauCeti.IsSemianalytic.preimage.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E]

TauCeti.IsSemianalytic.preimage.doc:
**Analytic preimages.** The preimage of a semianalytic set under a real analytic map is
semianalytic.

TauCeti.IsSemianalytic.signature:
TauCeti.IsSemianalytic.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] (s : Set E) :
  Prop
TauCeti.IsSemianalytic.doc:
A set `s ⊆ E` is *semianalytic* if it is semianalytic at every point of `E`: near every point,
it agrees with a finite Boolean combination of zero sets and positivity sets of real analytic
functions defined near that point.

TauCeti.IsSemialgebraic.isSemianalytic.signature:

TauCeti.IsSemialgebraic.isSemianalytic.doc:
A semialgebraic subset of `σ → ℝ`, for a finite type `σ`, is semianalytic: polynomial
functions are analytic.

TauCeti.IsRepresentativeSet.tsum_one_div.signature:
TauCeti.IsRepresentativeSet.tsum_one_div_natCard_algEquiv_mul_natCard_residueField_pow_wildExponent_eq_one_iff.{u_1}

  ∑' (M : ↑R),

          (↑(Nat.card Gal(↥↑M/K)) *
            ↑(Nat.card (IsLocalRing.ResidueField ↥(ValuativeRel.valuation K).integer)) ^
              (↑M).wildExponent) =

    ∑' (L : ↑(TauCeti.totallyRamifiedOfDegree K n)),

For `0 < n`, Serre's mass formula over a set of representatives,
`∑_{M ∈ R} 1 / (#Aut_K(M) · q ^ c(M)) = 1`, is equivalent to the mass formula over `σ_K(n)`,
`∑_{L ∈ σ_K(n)} q ^ (-c(L)) = n`.

TauCeti.IsRegularLocalRing.isRegular_pai.doc:
Over a two-dimensional regular local ring, every pair generating the maximal ideal is
regular on any finite injective normal local algebra, considered as a module over the base.

TauCeti.IsRegularLocalRing.isCohenMacaul.signature:

TauCeti.IsRegularLocalRing.isCohenMacaul.doc: **A regular local ring is Cohen–Macaulay.** Stacks, Lemma 10.106.3 (00NQ).

TauCeti.IsProP.range_pi_mapQuotient_ker_.signature:
TauCeti.IsProP.range_pi_mapQuotient_ker_proPFrattini.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G]
  [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] [CompactSpace G] [TotallyDisconnectedSpace G] {p : ℕ}
  [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (hG : TauCeti.IsProP p G)
  (hfg : TauCeti.IsTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated G) :
  (Set.range fun φ N => (TauCeti.ContinuousAut.mapQuotient ⋯) ↑φ) =
    {σ |
      (∀
          (N :
            { N //
              TauCeti.IsTopCharacteristic G ↑N.toOpenSubgroup ∧
                ↑N.toOpenSubgroup ≤ TauCeti.proPFrattini p G }),
          σ N ∈ (MulAut.mapQuotient (frattini (G ⧸ ↑(↑N).toOpenSubgroup))).ker) ∧
        ∀
          ⦃N M :
            { N //
              TauCeti.IsTopCharacteristic G ↑N.toOpenSubgroup ∧
                ↑N.toOpenSubgroup ≤ TauCeti.proPFrattini p G }⦄
          (hle : ↑N ≤ ↑M) (q : G ⧸ ↑(↑N).toOpenSubgroup),
          (TauCeti.QuotientGroup.mapOfLE hle) ((σ N) q) =
            (σ M) ((TauCeti.QuotientGroup.mapOfLE hle) q)}
TauCeti.IsProP.range_pi_mapQuotient_ker_.doc:
**The kernel on the Frattini quotient is the inverse limit of the finite kernels.** For a
topologically finitely generated pro-`p` group `G`, the coordinates on the quotients `G ⧸ N` by the
topologically characteristic open normal subgroups `N ≤ proPFrattini p G` identify the kernel of
`ContinuousAut G →* MulAut (G ⧸ proPFrattini p G)` with the families of automorphisms `σ N` of
the finite `p`-groups `G ⧸ N` that act trivially on the Frattini quotients of `G ⧸ N` and are
compatible with the quotient maps `G ⧸ N → G ⧸ M` for `N ≤ M`. The coordinate map is injective
and a topological embedding by `ContinuousAut.isEmbedding_pi_mapQuotient_ker_proPFrattini`.

TauCeti.IsProP.isProP_ker_mapQuotient_pr.signature:
TauCeti.IsProP.isProP_ker_mapQuotient_proPFrattini.{u_1} {G : Type u_1} [Group G]
  [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] [CompactSpace G] {p : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime p)]
  (hG : TauCeti.IsProP p G) : TauCeti.IsProP p ↥(TauCeti.ContinuousAut.mapQuotient ⋯).ker
TauCeti.IsProP.isProP_ker_mapQuotient_pr.doc:
**The continuous automorphisms of a pro-`p` group acting trivially on its Frattini quotient
form a pro-`p` group.** For a compact pro-`p` group `G`, the kernel of
`ContinuousAut G →* MulAut (G ⧸ proPFrattini p G)` is pro-`p` for the congruence topology.

TauCeti.IsProP.gradedLieAlgebra.signature:
TauCeti.IsProP.gradedLieAlgebra.{u} (p : ℕ) {G : Type u} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
  [IsTopologicalGroup G] {ℓ : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime ℓ)] [CompactSpace G] [TotallyDisconnectedSpace G]
  (hG : TauCeti.IsProP ℓ G) : LieAlgebra ℤ_[ℓ] (DirectSum ℕ fun k => TauCeti.gradedPiece p G k)
TauCeti.IsProP.gradedLieAlgebra.doc:
**The `ℤ_ℓ`-Lie algebra of a pro-`ℓ` group.** For a pro-`ℓ` group `G`, the graded Lie ring
`⨁ k, gr_k(G)` of the lower `p`-series is a Lie algebra over `ℤ_ℓ`, for the `ℤ_ℓ`-module structure
which in each degree is `TauCeti.IsProP.gradedPieceModule`: the graded bracket is `ℤ_ℓ`-bilinear.
For `p = 0` this is the `ℤ_ℓ`-Lie algebra of the closed lower central series.

TauCeti.IsProP.cohomologicalDimensionAt_.signature:
TauCeti.IsProP.cohomologicalDimensionAt_le_one_iff_exists_convergesToOne_continuousMulEquiv_presentation.{u}
  {p : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {G : Type u} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G]
  [CompactSpace G] [TotallyDisconnectedSpace G] (hG : TauCeti.IsProP p G) :
  TauCeti.cohomologicalDimensionAt p G ≤ 1 ↔
    ∃ s, TauCeti.ConvergesToOne s ∧ ∃ e, ⇑e = ⇑(hG.presentation s)
TauCeti.IsProP.cohomologicalDimensionAt_.doc:
**Serre's theorem at arbitrary rank, as an equivalence.** A pro-`p` group `G` has `cd_p G ≤ 1`
if and only if it is free pro-`p` on a pointed profinite space: some subset `s` of `G` converging to
`1` has a presentation `F_p(insert 1 s, 1) → G` that is a topological isomorphism.

TauCeti.IsPolynomiallyConvex.exists_subs.signature:

TauCeti.IsPolynomiallyConvex.exists_subs.doc:
A compact polynomially convex set `K ⊆ ℂⁿ` lies in the interior of a polynomial polyhedron
contained in any given open neighbourhood `U` of `K`.

TauCeti.IsNondegenerateCriticalPoint.exi.signature:
TauCeti.IsNondegenerateCriticalPoint.exists_stableSet_isManifold.{u_1} {E : Type u_1}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {f : E → ℝ} {x : E}

        Subtype.val
TauCeti.IsNondegenerateCriticalPoint.exi.doc:
The global stable set of a Morse critical point of a globally `C^(n+1)` function has a `C^n`
manifold structure modelled on the stable Hessian subspace, with its subspace topology and a
`C^n` inclusion into the ambient space. The dimension of the model plus the Morse index equals
the ambient dimension.

TauCeti.IsMorse.exists_tendsto_maximalIn.signature:
TauCeti.IsMorse.exists_tendsto_maximalIntegralCurve_neg_mgradient.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {E : Type u_1}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {H : Type u_2}
  [TopologicalSpace H] {I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H} {M : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace M]
  [ChartedSpace H M] [T2Space M] [IsManifold I 2 M] [BoundarylessManifold I M]
  [Bundle.RiemannianBundle fun x => TangentSpace I x]
  [IsContMDiffRiemannianBundle I 1 E fun x => TangentSpace I x] {f : M → ℝ} [I.Boundaryless]
  (hf : TauCeti.IsMorse I f) (hp : IsProperMap f) (hbdd : BddBelow (Set.range f)) (x : M) :
  ∃ p ∈ TauCeti.criticalPoints I f,
    Filter.Tendsto (maximalIntegralCurve (-TauCeti.Manifold.mgradient I f) x) Filter.atTop (nhds p)
TauCeti.IsMorse.exists_tendsto_maximalIn.doc:
**Negative gradient trajectories of a proper Morse function converge.** If `f` is a proper
Morse function bounded below, the maximal integral curve of `-grad f` through any point converges
to a critical point of `f`, for any `C¹` Riemannian metric.

TauCeti.IsMorse.exists_admissible_morseC.signature:
TauCeti.IsMorse.exists_admissible_morseCharts.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {E : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2}
  {M : Type u_3} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [TopologicalSpace H] {I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H} [I.Boundaryless] [TopologicalSpace M]
  [ChartedSpace H M] [IsManifold I (↑⊤) M] {f : M → ℝ} [T2Space M] (hf : TauCeti.IsMorse I f)
  {c δ : ℝ} (hδ : 0 < δ) (hcompact : IsCompact (f ⁻¹' Set.Icc (c - δ) (c + δ))) {U : M → Set M}
  (hU : ∀ x ∈ TauCeti.criticalPoints I f ∩ f ⁻¹' {c}, U x ∈ nhds x) :
  ∃ ε,
    0 < ε ∧
      ε ≤ δ ∧
        TauCeti.criticalPoints I f ∩ f ⁻¹' Set.Icc (c - ε) (c + ε) ⊆ f ⁻¹' {c} ∧
          ∃ ψ,
            Pairwise (Function.onFun Disjoint fun p => (ψ p).source) ∧
              ∀ (p : ↑(TauCeti.criticalPoints I f ∩ f ⁻¹' {c})),
                ↑p ∈ (ψ p).source ∧
                  (ψ p).source ⊆ U ↑p ∧
                    ↑(ψ p).toPartialEquiv ↑p = 0 ∧
                      Metric.closedBall 0 √(2 * ε) ⊆ (ψ p).target ∧
                        ∀ y ∈ (ψ p).source,
                          f y =
                            c +
                              ∑ i,
                                (if ↑i < TauCeti.manifoldMorseIndex I f ↑p then -1 else 1) *
                                  (↑(ψ p).toPartialEquiv y).ofLp i ^ 2
TauCeti.IsMorse.exists_admissible_morseC.doc:
**Admissible Morse charts at a critical level.** Let `f` be a Morse function on a Hausdorff
manifold whose band `f⁻¹[c - δ, c + δ]` is compact, for some `0 < δ`. Then there are a width
`0 < ε ≤ δ` and normalized Morse charts `ψ p`, indexed by the critical points `p` on the level
`f⁻¹(c)`, such that

* the only critical points in the band `f⁻¹[c - ε, c + ε]` are those on the level `f⁻¹(c)`;
* the chart sources are pairwise disjoint, and each lies in a prescribed neighbourhood `U p`;
* `ψ p p = 0`, and `f = c - Σ_{i < λ} (ψ p)ᵢ² + Σ_{i ≥ λ} (ψ p)ᵢ²` on the source of `ψ p`, where
  `λ` is the Morse index of `f` at `p`;
* the target of each chart contains the closed ball of radius `√(2ε)` about `0`.

The last condition places Milnor's ellipsoid `‖u‖² + 2‖v‖² ≤ 2ε` inside every chart. All of these
conditions persist when `ε` is decreased.

TauCeti.IsMonomialEquivalent.hammingMinD.doc: Monomially equivalent codes have the same minimum distance.

TauCeti.IsMcCallumWellOriented.signature:
TauCeti.IsMcCallumWellOriented

TauCeti.IsMcCallumWellOriented.doc:
A finite family `F` of real polynomials in `n` variables is *well-oriented* in McCallum's
sense if, when `n` is positive, singling out the distinguished variable `X 0` gives a family with
a squarefree basis `B` such that each member of `B` is nullified at only finitely many points of
`ℝ ^ (n - 1)`, and the McCallum projection of the family with respect to `B` is again
well-oriented. Every family of constants is well-oriented.

TauCeti.IsManifoldStronglyPseudoconvexAt.doc:
**The index bound for strongly `q`-pseudoconvex functions on a complex manifold.** At a
critical point `x` of a function `f` which is `C²` at `x` and strongly `q`-pseudoconvex at `x`, the
Morse index of `f` is at most `dim_ℂ E + q`.

function `f` which is smooth near `x`, on a manifold with a boundaryless model, there is a partial
diffeomorphism `ψ` onto an open subset of `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)`, `m = dim M`, with
`ψ x = 0` and

`f y = f x - Σ_{i < λ} (ψ y)ᵢ² + Σ_{i ≥ λ} (ψ y)ᵢ²`

on its whole source, where `λ` is the manifold Morse index of `f` at `x`.

TauCeti.IsLocalTiling.signature:

  [TopologicalSpace X] (P : Set X) (N : X → Set G) : Prop
TauCeti.IsLocalTiling.doc:
A **local tiling** by a closed path-connected tile `P`: for each `x ∈ P`, `N x` is a set of
local neighbours, the elements `h` such that `h • P` is one of the tiles around `x`. The
identity is a neighbour, `x ∈ h • P` for each neighbour `h`, the neighbours of `x` seen from the
tile `h • P` are the translates `h⁻¹ • N x`, and each point of `P` lies in a tiling chart made of
its own neighbours.

TauCeti.IsLiouvilleDomain.exists_isRestr.doc:
**The boundary of a Liouville domain is of restricted contact type.** On a finite-dimensional
manifold without boundary, a Liouville domain `W` is the sublevel set `{f ≤ c}` of a function `f`,
`C¹` along the level `f⁻¹(c)`, of which `c` is a regular value; the frontier of `W` is exactly the
level; and the level, with its atlas `TauCeti.regularLevelChartedSpace`, is a hypersurface
of restricted contact type for the primitive `α`.

TauCeti.IsLiouvilleDomain.doc:
A subset `W` of a manifold `M` is a **Liouville domain** for the smooth two-form `ω`, with
primitive `α`, when `ω` is nondegenerate, `dα = ω`, `W` is compact and lies in the interior of
`M`, and the Liouville field of `α` points strictly outwards along the boundary of `W`: some smooth
vector field `Z` with `ι_Z ω = α` and some continuous function `f` and value `c` satisfy
`W = {f ≤ c}`, with `f` smooth and `df(Z) > 0` at every point of the level `f⁻¹(c)`. The
nondegeneracy of `ω` makes `Z` unique, and the condition along `f⁻¹(c)` makes `c` a regular value
of `f`, so that `W` is a compact domain with smooth boundary `f⁻¹(c)`.

TauCeti.IsJordanCurve.not_isPreconnected.doc:
**The Jordan separation theorem.** The complement of a Jordan curve in the plane is not
preconnected.

TauCeti.IsJordanCurve.frontier_connected.signature:
TauCeti.IsJordanCurve.frontier_connectedComponentIn {C : Set ℂ} (h : TauCeti.IsJordanCurve C)
  {x : ℂ} (hx : x ∉ C) : frontier (connectedComponentIn Cᶜ x) = C
TauCeti.IsJordanCurve.frontier_connected.doc:
**The frontier of a complementary component of a Jordan curve is the whole curve**: for
`x ∉ C`, the component of `Cᶜ` containing `x` has frontier `C`.

TauCeti.IsGoodCycle.apply_self_eq_zero_o.doc: An image occurring with multiplicity at least two has square zero.

TauCeti.IsGoodCycle.signature:
TauCeti.IsGoodCycle.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {H : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} {P : Type u_3} [AddCommGroup H]
  [Fintype ι] [Fintype P] (B : LinearMap.BilinForm ℤ H) (κ e : H) (C : ι → H) (m δ : ι → ℕ)

TauCeti.IsGoodCycle.doc:
The numerical properties of a positive cycle `∑ m i • C i` of distinct simple
pseudoholomorphic images in a good class `e` of a symplectic four-manifold with canonical class
`κ`, passing through generic points indexed by `P`, read in the intersection form `B` on
integral homology. The image `C i` has singularity number `δ i` and contains the points `pts i`.
The fields say: the multiplicities are positive; distinct images meet nonnegatively; the number
of points on an image is at most half the index `d(C i) - 2 δ i` of simple curves in its class,
where `d(x) = x · x - κ · x`; the good class `e` is at least `-1` on every image of negative
square; the cycle represents `e`; every point lies on some image; and the number of points is
half the virtual dimension of `e`. The square `-1` of an image of negative square, which
adjunction forces for an exceptional sphere, then follows (`IsGoodCycle.apply_self_eq_neg_one`).

TauCeti.IsFreelyIndependent.eqOn_iSup.doc:
Freeness determines the joint distribution from the individual ones: two normalised
functionals for which `B` is free and which agree on each `B i` agree on the subalgebra
generated by the `B i`.

TauCeti.IsFreelyIndependent.signature:
TauCeti.IsFreelyIndependent.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2} {ι : Type u_4}

TauCeti.IsFreelyIndependent.doc:
Subalgebras `B i` of `A` are *freely independent* with respect to a linear functional `φ` if
`φ (a₁ * ⋯ * aₙ) = 0` for every nonempty word `[(i₁, a₁), …, (iₙ, aₙ)]` whose consecutive labels
are distinct and whose letters satisfy `aⱼ ∈ B iⱼ` and `φ aⱼ = 0`. Labels that are not adjacent
may coincide.

TauCeti.IsFiniteEtaleSplit.of_henselianL.signature:
TauCeti.IsFiniteEtaleSplit.of_henselianLocalRing.{u} (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
  [HenselianLocalRing R] [IsSepClosed (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R)] : TauCeti.IsFiniteEtaleSplit R
TauCeti.IsFiniteEtaleSplit.of_henselianL.doc:
A Henselian local ring with separably closed residue field, that is, a strictly Henselian local
ring, has no nonsplit finite étale covers: a faithfully flat finite étale algebra has a point over
the separably closed residue field, which lifts to a section.

TauCeti.IsFiniteEtaleSplit.doc:
A ring `R` *has no nonsplit finite étale covers* if every finite étale `R`-algebra is totally
split. This is the conclusion of Scholze's Lemma 15.3 for the perfectoid tower `A_∞`.

TauCeti.IsDemushkin.openSubgroup.doc:
**An open subgroup of an infinite Demushkin group is Demushkin** (Serre's exposé, §9.2). The
subgroup is pro-`p` and topologically finitely generated with `G`; its `H²(U, 𝔽_p)` is
one-dimensional by `TauCeti.IsDemushkin.finrank_cohomFp_two_openSubgroup`; and its cup product is
nondegenerate because a nonzero class of `H¹(U, 𝔽_p) ≅ H¹(G, Coind_U^G 𝔽_p)` is paired
nontrivially by Tate's duality map `α₁` of `G`, a pairing which is the corestriction of a cup
product of `U`.

TauCeti.IsDemushkin.nonempty_continuousM.doc:
**The isomorphism type of an open subgroup of a Demushkin group**: an open subgroup `U` of an
infinite Demushkin group `G` is topologically isomorphic to a Demushkin group `H` if and only if
`H` has rank `2 + [G : U] (n(G) - 2)` and the canonical character of `H` has image `χ(U)`, where
`χ` is the canonical character of `G`.

TauCeti.IsDemushkin.nonempty_continuousM.doc:
**Uniqueness of the dyadic Demushkin groups of even rank with image `{±1} × U^(f)`** (Labute,
Theorem 6). Two Demushkin groups at `p = 2` of the same even rank `n ≥ 4` whose canonical
characters have the same image `V^(f) = {±1} × U^(f)`, `f ≥ 2` finite, are topologically
isomorphic.

TauCeti.IsDemushkin.nonempty_continuousM.doc:
**The classification of Demushkin groups** (Labute): two Demushkin groups are topologically
isomorphic if and only if they have the same rank and their canonical characters have the same
image. The forward direction is the invariance of both invariants under isomorphism; the
converse is `TauCeti.IsDemushkin.nonempty_continuousMulEquiv_of_range_demushkinCharacter_eq`.

TauCeti.IsDemushkin.dualityMap1_zModTwis.doc:
**Tate's duality map `α₁` of an infinite Demushkin group with coefficients `I(χ)/pⁱ` is
bijective** on every finite discrete `G`-module `M` killed by `pⁱ`:
`H¹(G, M) × H¹(G, Hom(M, I(χ)/pⁱ)) → H²(G, I(χ)/pⁱ)` is a perfect pairing.

TauCeti.IsDemushkin.cohomologicalDimensi.signature:
TauCeti.IsDemushkin.cohomologicalDimensionAt_eq_two.{u} {p : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {G : Type u}
  [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] [CompactSpace G]

  TauCeti.cohomologicalDimensionAt p G = 2
TauCeti.IsDemushkin.cohomologicalDimensi.doc:
**Tate's theorem: an infinite Demushkin group has `p`-cohomological dimension exactly `2`.**
The lower bound is `H²(G, 𝔽_p) ≠ 0`; the upper bound is the right exactness of `H²` on the finite
`𝔽_p[G]`-modules, which Tate's perfect duality provides.

TauCeti.IsDemushkin.signature:
TauCeti.IsDemushkin.{u} (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (G : Type u) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
  [IsTopologicalGroup G] : Prop
TauCeti.IsDemushkin.doc:
**The Demushkin predicate** (Labute, p. 106), for a prime `p` and a topological group `G`: a
pro-`p` group whose `H¹(G, 𝔽_p)` is finite-dimensional, whose `H²(G, 𝔽_p)` is one-dimensional, and
on which the cup product `H¹(G, 𝔽_p) × H¹(G, 𝔽_p) → H²(G, 𝔽_p)` is nondegenerate on both sides.
The primality of `p` is a hypothesis of the predicate. Profiniteness is not: no field mentions
`CompactSpace G` or `TotallyDisconnectedSpace G`, so Lean leaves those section instances out of
the structure, and the predicate is also defined for topological groups that are not profinite.
The presentation results below assume both; on profinite groups, its intended mathematical
domain, this is Labute's notion. The pro-`p` hypothesis is a field, so that no theorem about
Demushkin groups applies to a group that satisfies only the cohomological clauses. Finite
generation is a consequence, `IsDemushkin.isTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated`, and is not assumed.

TauCeti.IsCAD.exists_isCAD_lazardValuati.doc:
**CAD lifting by Lazard delineations in a reordered base.** Suppose every cell `C` of a
cylindrical algebraic decomposition of `ℝ ^ n` is an analytic submanifold, and its reordering
`(· ∘ e.symm) ⁻¹' C` by a permutation `e` of the base coordinates carries a Lazard delineation
of a fixed polynomial family. Then the stacks of those delineations, pulled back to the
original cells, form a cylindrical algebraic decomposition of `ℝ ^ (n + 1)` with the original
decomposition as its projection.

Every lifted cell is an analytic submanifold. On it, every family member has constant Lazard
valuation when the base coordinates are read through `e` and the new coordinate is read last.

TauCeti.IsAspherical.exists_homotopyEqui.signature:
TauCeti.IsAspherical.exists_homotopyEquiv.{u} {X Y : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X]
  [TopologicalSpace Y] [TauCeti.CWType X] [TauCeti.CWType Y] {x : X} {y : Y}
  (hX : TauCeti.IsAspherical X x) (hY : TauCeti.IsAspherical Y y)
  (φ : FundamentalGroup X x ≃* FundamentalGroup Y y) :

    ∀ (a : FundamentalGroup X x),
      (FundamentalGroup.fundamentalGroupMulEquivOfPath γ) ((FundamentalGroup.map e.toFun x) a) = φ a
TauCeti.IsAspherical.exists_homotopyEqui.doc:
**Uniqueness of aspherical spaces of CW type.** Two aspherical spaces of CW type are homotopy
equivalent by a homotopy equivalence realizing any prescribed isomorphism `φ` of their fundamental
groups: there is a homotopy equivalence `e` and a path `γ` from `e x` to `y` such that the map
induced by `e` on fundamental groups, followed by basepoint change along `γ`, is `φ`.

The hypothesis of CW type on both spaces cannot be dropped: a point and the Warsaw circle are
aspherical with trivial fundamental groups, but they are not homotopy equivalent.

TauCeti.IsAlgebraicBelyiPair.of_mapRingE.doc:
**The Galois conjugate of an algebraic Belyi pair is an algebraic Belyi pair**: if `F` is an
algebraic Belyi pair over `k`, and `τ : F ≃+* F'` carries `k(t)` onto `k'(t)` by the coefficient
map of `σ : k ≃+* k'`, then `F'` is an algebraic Belyi pair over `k'`.

Taking `F' = F` with its structure maps precomposed with `σ⁻¹` and `τ` the identity, this is the
conjugation of a Belyi pair by an automorphism `σ` of the constants.

TauCeti.IsAlgebraicBelyiPair.signature:
TauCeti.IsAlgebraicBelyiPair.{u_1, u_2} (k : Type u_1) (F : Type u_2) [Field k] [CharZero k]

  [FiniteDimensional (RatFunc k) F] : Prop
TauCeti.IsAlgebraicBelyiPair.doc:
An **algebraic Belyi pair** over a field `k` of characteristic zero: a function field `F / k`
with exact constant field `k`, finite over the rational function field `k(t)` through the given
`Algebra (RatFunc k) F` structure, in which every place lying over a place of `k(t)` other than
`t = 0`, `t = 1` and `t = ∞` has ramification index `1`.

The branch locus is only required to be contained in the three marked places. The base field is
pinned to characteristic zero, where `F / k(t)` is automatically separable; in characteristic `p`
the power map `t ↦ t ^ p` is inseparable and `4t(1 - t)` is constant in characteristic `2`.

TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.toContinuousAl.doc:
**Equivalence of complete affinoid norms.** An algebra isomorphism between completely normed
affinoid algebras is a homeomorphism, whatever complete ultrametric algebra norms they carry.
Applied to two such norms on one algebra, this says that they define the same topology.

TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.supSeminorm_eq.signature:

**The supremum seminorm is the spectral value of the minimal polynomial.** Let `B` be an
affinoid algebra which is integral and torsion-free over an integrally closed domain `A`. For
`f : B` with minimal polynomial `X ^ d + ∑_{i < d} aᵢ X ^ i` over `A`,
`|f|sup = max_{i < d} |aᵢ|sup ^ (1 / (d - i))`.

TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.isRestricted_s.doc:
**Restricted series over an affinoid algebra form an affinoid algebra.** For an affinoid
algebra `A` with a complete ultrametric algebra norm, the Gauss-normed algebra `A⟨X₁, …, Xₘ⟩` of
unit-radius restricted series is affinoid: a Tate presentation `K⟨Y₁, …, Yₙ⟩ → A` induces a
presentation `K⟨X₁, …, Xₘ, Y₁, …, Yₙ⟩ → A⟨X₁, …, Xₘ⟩`.

TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.height_eq_ring.signature:
TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.height_eq_ringKrullDim_of_isDomain.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1}
  [NormedField K] [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K] {A : Type u_2} [CommRing A] [Algebra K A]
  [IsDomain A] (hA : TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra K A) (m : Ideal A) [m.IsMaximal] :
  ↑m.height = ringKrullDim A
TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.height_eq_ring.doc:
**Heights of maximal ideals of affinoid domains.** Every maximal ideal of an affinoid domain
`A` has height `dim A`.

TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.exists_pointNo.signature:
TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.exists_pointNorm_eq_supSeminorm.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1}
  [NontriviallyNormedField K] [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K] {A : Type u_2} [CommRing A]
  [Algebra K A] [Nontrivial A] (hA : TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra K A) (f : A) :
  ∃ x, TauCeti.pointNorm K x f = TauCeti.supSeminorm K f
TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.exists_pointNo.doc:
**The maximum modulus principle.** On a nonzero affinoid algebra the supremum seminorm is
attained at a classical point: for every `f : A` there is a maximal ideal `x` of `A` with
`|f(x)| = |f|sup`.

TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.exists_finite_.signature:
TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.exists_finite_injective.{u, u_1} {K : Type u} [NormedField K]
  [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K] {A : Type u_1} [CommRing A] [Algebra K A] [Nontrivial A]
  (hA : TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra K A) : ∃ n g, Function.Injective ⇑g ∧ g.Finite
TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.exists_finite_.doc:
**Affinoid Noether normalisation.** Every nonzero affinoid algebra over a complete
ultrametric field is finite over an injectively embedded finite-variable Tate algebra.
Finiteness uses the algebra structure induced by the displayed map.

TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.existsUnique_a.doc:
**The universal property of restricted series over an affinoid algebra.** Let `A` and `B` be
affinoid algebras with complete ultrametric algebra norms. A `K`-algebra map `φ : A → B` and
power-bounded `b₁, …, bₖ ∈ B` extend to exactly one `K`-algebra map `A⟨X₁, …, Xₖ⟩ → B` sending
each `Xᵢ` to `bᵢ`, namely `TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.restrictedLift`. It is continuous, as is every
algebra map between such algebras (`TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.continuous_algHom`).

TauCeti.IsAffinoidAlgebra.continuous_alg.doc:
Every homomorphism from a noetherian ultrametric Banach algebra to a completely normed
affinoid algebra is continuous. The affinoid presentation is purely algebraic.

TauCeti.InternalGrading.exists_isInterna.signature:
TauCeti.InternalGrading.exists_isInternal_span_singleton.{u, u_1} {k : Type u_1} {M : Type u}
  [Field k] [AddCommGroup M] [_root_.Module k M] [_root_.Module (Polynomial k) M]
  [IsScalarTower k (Polynomial k) M] {G : TauCeti.InternalGrading k M ℤ} {d : ℕ}
  [Module.Finite (Polynomial k) M] (hd : d ≠ 0)
  (hX : ∀ ⦃p : ℤ⦄ ⦃x : M⦄, x ∈ G.piece ℤ p → Polynomial.X • x ∈ G.piece ℤ (p - ↑d)) :
  ∃ ι κ,
    ∃ (_ : Finite ι) (_ : Finite κ),
      ∃ t deg m,
        (∀ (i : ι ⊕ κ), t i ∈ G.piece ℤ (deg i)) ∧
          (∀ (i : ι), Ideal.torsionOf (Polynomial k) M (t (Sum.inl i)) = ⊥) ∧
            (∀ (j : κ), m j ≠ 0) ∧
              (∀ (j : κ),
                  Ideal.torsionOf (Polynomial k) M (t (Sum.inr j)) =
                    Ideal.span {Polynomial.X ^ m j}) ∧
                DirectSum.IsInternal fun i => Polynomial k ∙ t i
TauCeti.InternalGrading.exists_isInterna.doc:
**The structure theorem for finitely generated graded `k[X]`-modules.** Let `X` lower degree
by `d ≠ 0` in a finitely generated graded `k[X]`-module `M` over a field. Then `M` is the internal
direct sum of cyclic submodules `k[X] ∙ t i` generated by homogeneous elements `t i`, indexed by
the disjoint union of two finite types: for `i` in the first, `t i` has zero annihilator, so
`k[X] ∙ t i` is a free `X`-tower; for `j` in the second, `t j` has annihilator `(X ^ m j)` with
`m j ≠ 0`, so `k[X] ∙ t j ≅ k[X] ⧸ (X ^ m j)`.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.weylGroup_typeE₈.doc:
**The reflections in the 240 roots generate the isometry group of the E₈ lattice**: its Weyl
group is the whole of `O(E₈)`.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.typeE₈IsometryD8.doc:
**The `E₈` root lattice is isometric to the spinor glue lattice `D₈⁺`.**

The underlying rational equivalence sends the `i`-th simple root of `E₈` to the `i`-th vector of
Bourbaki's plate VII in Conway--Sloane coordinates.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.nonempty_isometr.doc:
**`E₈ ⊕ E₈ ⊕ U ≅ D₁₆⁺ ⊕ U`.** Adding the hyperbolic plane `U` makes the two non-isometric even
unimodular lattices of rank sixteen isometric.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.isLeast_form_sel.signature:
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.isLeast_form_self_typeADiscriminantGroupEquiv {n : ℕ} (a : ZMod (n + 1)) :
  IsLeast
    {q |
      ∃ x,
        Submodule.Quotient.mk x = (TauCeti.IntegralLattice.typeADiscriminantGroupEquiv n) a ∧
          ((TauCeti.IntegralLattice.typeARootLattice n).form ↑x) ↑x = q}
    (↑a.val * (↑n + 1 - ↑a.val) / (↑n + 1))
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.isLeast_form_sel.doc:
**The minimum norm of the discriminant class labelled `a : ZMod (n + 1)`.**  The class
`typeADiscriminantGroupEquiv n a = a.val • ω₁` of `Aₙ` has minimum norm
`a.val (n + 1 - a.val) / (n + 1)`, the shortest norm of the Conway–Sloane glue label `[a]` of an
`Aₙ` component.

Attained least norms in two discriminant cosets add to the attained least norm of the
corresponding coset of the orthogonal sum.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.infinite_isometr.signature:
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.infinite_isometry_of_isIndefinite.{u_1} {V : Type u_1} [AddCommGroup V]
  [_root_.Module ℚ V] {L : TauCeti.IntegralLattice V} [L.IsNondegenerate]
  (hrank : 3 ≤ Module.finrank ℤ ↥L.carrier) (hL : L.IsIndefinite) : Infinite (L.Isometry L)
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.infinite_isometr.doc:
**Indefinite lattices have infinite isometry groups.** A nondegenerate indefinite integral
lattice of rank at least three has infinitely many isometries.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.evenIntermediate.doc:
**Even overlattices correspond to quadratic-isotropic subgroups.** For an even lattice, the
intermediate-carrier order isomorphism restricts to the even carriers on one side and the
quadratic-isotropic subgroups of the discriminant group on the other.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.discriminantQuad.signature:
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.discriminantQuadraticModule.{u} {V : Type u} [AddCommGroup V]
  [_root_.Module ℚ V] (L : TauCeti.IntegralLattice V) [L.IsNondegenerate] (hL : L.IsEven) :
  TauCeti.FiniteQuadraticModule
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.discriminantQuad.doc:
The discriminant group of an even nondegenerate integral lattice, equipped with its canonical
half-norm quadratic map and discriminant polar pairing.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.classNumber.signature:
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.classNumber.{u} {V : Type u} [AddCommGroup V] [_root_.Module ℚ V]
  (L : TauCeti.IntegralLattice V) : ℕ
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.classNumber.doc:
The class number `h(L)`: the number of isometry classes in the genus of `L`. It is `0` when
the genus contains infinitely many classes.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.checkerboardDisc.signature:
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.checkerboardDiscriminantQuadraticIsometry (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (hn : Even n) :
  (TauCeti.IntegralLattice.checkerboardStandardQuadraticModule n hn).Isometry
    ((TauCeti.IntegralLattice.checkerboardLattice n).discriminantQuadraticModule ⋯)
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.checkerboardDisc.doc:
**The standard model is isometric to the discriminant quadratic module of an even-rank
checkerboard lattice**, by the identification carrying `(1, 0)` to the vector class and `(0, 1)`
to the spinor class.

This is the `Dₙ` row of the ADE table for even `n`: not only is the discriminant group `(ℤ/2)²`,
its quadratic form is the displayed one.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.IsPosDef.unitNor.signature:
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.IsPosDef.unitNormDecomposition.{u} {V : Type u} [AddCommGroup V]
  [_root_.Module ℚ V] {L : TauCeti.IntegralLattice V} (hL : L.IsPosDef) :
  ((TauCeti.IntegralLattice.unitLattice (Fin (Module.finrank ℤ ↥L.unitNormSubmodule))).orthogonalSum
        L.unitNormComplement).Isometry
    L
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.IsPosDef.unitNor.doc:
**A positive definite lattice is `I_k` plus a lattice without vectors of norm one.** The
standard lattice `I_k` is carried onto the unit-norm sublattice, with `k` its rank, and the second
summand is the complement `unitNormComplement L`.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.IsPosDef.nonempt.signature:
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.IsPosDef.nonempty_isometry_typeE₈RootLattice_of_isEven.{u} {V : Type u}
  [AddCommGroup V] [_root_.Module ℚ V] {L : TauCeti.IntegralLattice V} (hL : L.IsPosDef)
  (hU : L.IsUnimodular) (he : L.IsEven) (hn : Module.finrank ℤ ↥L.carrier = 8) :
  Nonempty (TauCeti.IntegralLattice.typeE₈RootLattice.Isometry L)
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.IsPosDef.nonempt.doc: **`E₈` is the unique even unimodular positive definite lattice of rank eight.**

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.IsPosDef.nonempt.signature:
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.IsPosDef.nonempty_isometry_of_isUnimodular_of_finrank_le_nine.{u}
  {V : Type u} [AddCommGroup V] [_root_.Module ℚ V] {L : TauCeti.IntegralLattice V}
  (hL : L.IsPosDef) (hU : L.IsUnimodular) (hn : Module.finrank ℤ ↥L.carrier ≤ 9) :
  Nonempty ((TauCeti.IntegralLattice.unitLattice (Fin (Module.finrank ℤ ↥L.carrier))).Isometry L) ∨
    Nonempty (TauCeti.IntegralLattice.typeE₈RootLattice.Isometry L) ∨

              TauCeti.IntegralLattice.typeE₈RootLattice).Isometry
          L)
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.IsPosDef.nonempt.doc:
**Positive definite unimodular lattices of rank at most nine.** Such a lattice is the
standard lattice `Iₙ`, the root lattice `E₈`, or `I₁ ⊕ E₈`.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.IsPosDef.minimum.signature:
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.IsPosDef.minimum_le_rpow_mul_determinant_rpow.{u} {V : Type u}
  [AddCommGroup V] [_root_.Module ℚ V] {L : TauCeti.IntegralLattice V} (hL : L.IsPosDef) :
  ↑L.minimum ≤
    (4 / 3) ^ ((↑(Module.finrank ℤ ↥L.carrier) - 1) / 2) *
      ↑L.determinant ^ (1 / ↑(Module.finrank ℤ ↥L.carrier))
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.IsPosDef.minimum.doc:
**Hermite's inequality for the minimum.** A positive definite integral lattice of rank `n`
satisfies `min L ≤ (4 / 3) ^ ((n - 1) / 2) · (det L) ^ (1 / n)`.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.IsPosDef.finite_.signature:
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.IsPosDef.finite_genusClasses.{u} {V : Type u} [AddCommGroup V]
  [_root_.Module ℚ V] {L : TauCeti.IntegralLattice V} (hL : L.IsPosDef) : L.genusClasses.Finite
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.IsPosDef.finite_.doc:
**A positive definite genus contains finitely many classes.** The lattices of the genus all
have the rank and determinant of `L`, so this is the finiteness of positive definite classes of
given rank and bounded determinant.

TauCeti.IntegralLattice.signature: TauCeti.IntegralLattice.{u} (V : Type u) [AddCommGroup V] [_root_.Module ℚ V] : Type u
TauCeti.IntegralLattice.doc:
An integral symmetric lattice in a rational vector space.

The field `le_dual` says exactly that the form takes integer values on pairs of vectors in
`carrier`.

TauCeti.InjectiveTensor.signature:
TauCeti.InjectiveTensor.{u_1, u_2, u_3} (𝕜 : Type u_1) (E : Type u_2) (F : Type u_3)
  [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
  [SeminormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F] : Type (max u_2 u_3)
TauCeti.InjectiveTensor.doc:
The algebraic tensor product `E ⊗[𝕜] F` carrying the injective seminorm.

This wrapper distinguishes the injective seminorm from other norms on the same algebraic tensor
product, such as the projective norm or the Hilbert-space norm of inner product spaces.

TauCeti.InfiniteTypeAHeckeAlgebra.stage.signature:
TauCeti.InfiniteTypeAHeckeAlgebra.stage.{u_1} (R : Type u_1) [CommRing R] (q : Rˣ) (n : ℕ) :
  Subalgebra R (TauCeti.InfiniteTypeAHeckeAlgebra R q)
TauCeti.InfiniteTypeAHeckeAlgebra.stage.doc:
The stage of the first `n` strands: the subalgebra generated by the generators
`T 0, …, T (n - 2)` that cross two of the strands `0, …, n - 1`. It is the image of the type-A
Hecke algebra on `n` strands.

TauCeti.InfiniteTypeAHeckeAlgebra.shift.signature:
TauCeti.InfiniteTypeAHeckeAlgebra.shift.{u_1} (R : Type u_1) [CommRing R] (q : Rˣ) (k : ℕ) :
  TauCeti.InfiniteTypeAHeckeAlgebra R q →ₐ[R] TauCeti.InfiniteTypeAHeckeAlgebra R q
TauCeti.InfiniteTypeAHeckeAlgebra.shift.doc:
The strand shift by `k`: the algebra endomorphism `T i ↦ T (i + k)` that moves every braid
`k` strands to the right.

TauCeti.InfiniteTypeAHeckeAlgebra.blockI.signature:
TauCeti.InfiniteTypeAHeckeAlgebra.blockIncl.{u_1} (R : Type u_1) [CommRing R] (q : Rˣ) (a b : ℕ) :
  TensorProduct R ↥(TauCeti.InfiniteTypeAHeckeAlgebra.stage R q a)
      ↥(TauCeti.InfiniteTypeAHeckeAlgebra.stage R q b) →ₐ[R]
    ↥(TauCeti.InfiniteTypeAHeckeAlgebra.stage R q (a + b))
TauCeti.InfiniteTypeAHeckeAlgebra.blockI.doc:
The disjoint block map: the algebra map from the tensor product of the stages `a` and `b` to
the stage `a + b` that places the first factor on the first `a` strands and the second factor,
shifted by `a`, on the next `b` strands. Its injectivity, which would make it an embedding,
needs the basis theorem and is not proved here.

TauCeti.InfiniteTypeAHeckeAlgebra.signature: TauCeti.InfiniteTypeAHeckeAlgebra.{u_1} (R : Type u_1) [CommRing R] (q : Rˣ) : Type u_1
TauCeti.InfiniteTypeAHeckeAlgebra.doc:
The infinite type-A Hecke algebra over `R` with parameter `q`: the free `R`-algebra on `ℕ`
modulo `TauCeti.InfiniteTypeAHeckeAlgebra.Rel`. It is the union of its finite stages
`TauCeti.InfiniteTypeAHeckeAlgebra.stage R q n`; see the module docstring for what is proved about
them.

TauCeti.Hyperfunction.oneDimBoundaryPres.doc:
**The presheaf of one-dimensional hyperfunctions is separated**: a section that vanishes on
the members of an open cover vanishes.

TauCeti.Hyperfunction.OneDimBoundaryQuot.doc:
The space `O(ℂ ∖ ℝ) / O(W(U))` of one-dimensional hyperfunctions on an open set `U ⊆ ℝ`,
represented by holomorphic functions on `ℂ ∖ ℝ` modulo those extending holomorphically across
`U`.

TauCeti.Huber.tensorTopology.signature:
TauCeti.Huber.tensorTopology.{u_1, u_2, u_3} (A : Type u_1) (B : Type u_2) (C : Type u_3)
  [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C] [Algebra A B] [Algebra A C] [TopologicalSpace A]
  [TopologicalSpace B] [TopologicalSpace C] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsTopologicalRing B]
  [IsTopologicalRing C] [TauCeti.Huber.IsAdicHom (algebraMap A B)]
  [TauCeti.Huber.IsAdicHom (algebraMap A C)] : TopologicalSpace (TensorProduct A B C)
TauCeti.Huber.tensorTopology.doc:
**The tensor topology** on `B ⊗[A] C`, for adic structure maps `A → B` and `A → C`: for any
compatible pairs of definition `(A₀, I)`, `(B₀, I B₀)` and `(C₀, I C₀)`, its neighbourhoods of
zero are generated by the images of `Iⁿ F`, where `F` is the image of `B₀ ⊗[A₀] C₀`
(`TauCeti.Huber.hasBasis_tensorTopology`). It is not an instance, since `B ⊗[A] C` may carry
other topologies.

TauCeti.Huber.isTopologicallyFiniteType_.doc:
**Affinoid algebras are the algebras topologically of finite type.** A complete ultrametric
normed `K`-algebra `B` is topologically of finite type over `K` in Huber's sense (Wedhorn,
Definition 5.57) exactly when it is a quotient of a Tate algebra `K⟨X₁, …, Xₙ⟩` as a
`K`-algebra.

TauCeti.Huber.isSheafyRing_of_isStrongly.signature:
TauCeti.Huber.isSheafyRing_of_isStronglyNoetherian.{v} {A : Type v} [CommRing A] [UniformSpace A]
  [IsUniformAddGroup A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing A]
  [TauCeti.Huber.IsStronglyNoetherian A] : TauCeti.Huber.IsSheafyRing A
TauCeti.Huber.isSheafyRing_of_isStrongly.doc:
**Every strongly noetherian Tate ring is sheafy** in the sense of Wedhorn's Definition 8.26
(`TauCeti.Huber.IsSheafyRing`). This is Wedhorn's Theorem 8.28(b); `A` need not be complete or
Hausdorff. The identity of `Â` is topologically of finite type, so this is the case `B = Â` of
`TauCeti.Huber.isStablySheafyRing_of_isStronglyNoetherian`.

TauCeti.Huber.exists_tateSeminorm.signature:
TauCeti.Huber.exists_tateSeminorm.{u_1} {A : Type u_1} [CommRing A] {A₀ : Subring A} {ϖ : Aˣ}
  {a : ℝ} [TopologicalSpace A]
  (hb : (nhds 0).HasBasis (fun x => True) fun n => {x | ↑(ϖ ^ (-↑n)) * x ∈ A₀})
  [SeparatelyContinuousMul A] (ha : 1 < a) (hϖ : ↑ϖ ∈ A₀) :
  ∃ α,
    (∀ (x : A), α x = TauCeti.Huber.tateGauge A₀ ϖ a x) ∧
      IsNonarchimedean ⇑α ∧ (nhds 0).HasBasis (fun ε => 0 < ε) fun ε => {x | α x < ε}
TauCeti.Huber.exists_tateSeminorm.doc:
A ring with separately continuous multiplication in which the sets `ϖ ^ n A₀`, `n ≥ 0`, form
a neighbourhood basis of zero carries an ultrametric ring seminorm, equal to the Tate gauge, whose
open balls about zero form a neighbourhood basis of zero.

TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.ofTensorP.signature:
TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.ofTensorProduct_bijective.{u_1, u_2} {A : Type u_1} [CommRing A]
  [UniformSpace A] [IsUniformAddGroup A] [IsTopologicalRing A] {M : Type u_2} [AddCommGroup M]
  [_root_.Module A M] [Module.Finite A M] [UniformSpace M] [IsUniformAddGroup M]
  [IsModuleTopology A M] [UniformContinuousConstSMul A M] (P : TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition A)
  [IsNoetherianRing ↥P.ringOfDefinition] :
  Function.Bijective ⇑(UniformSpace.Completion.ofTensorProduct A M)
TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.ofTensorP.doc:
**Completion of a finite module is base change to the completed ring** (Huber, Lemma
2.3(iii)). If `A` is a Huber ring with a noetherian ring of definition and `M` is a finitely
generated `A`-module with its natural topology, the canonical map `Â ⊗[A] M → M̂` is bijective.

TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.isStrictM.doc:
**Linear maps of finite modules over a Huber ring with a noetherian ring of definition are
strict** (Huber, Lemma 2.3(i)). If `A₀` is noetherian, every `A`-linear map between finitely
generated `A`-modules with their natural topologies is continuous and open onto its image.

TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.isClosed_.signature:
TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.isClosed_of_isNoetherianRing.{u_1, u_2} {A : Type u_1} [CommRing A]
  {M : Type u_2} [AddCommGroup M] [_root_.Module A M] [UniformSpace A] [IsUniformAddGroup A]
  [CompleteSpace A] [T0Space A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [Module.Finite A M] [TopologicalSpace M]
  [IsModuleTopology A M] (P : TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition A)
  [IsNoetherianRing ↥P.ringOfDefinition] (N : Submodule A M) : IsClosed ↑N
TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.isClosed_.doc:
**Submodules of finite modules over a complete Huber ring with a noetherian ring of definition
are closed** (Huber, Lemma 2.3(ii)). If `A` is complete and Hausdorff with a noetherian ring of
definition, every `A`-submodule of a finite `A`-module is closed in its natural topology.

TauCeti.Huber.Pair.finiteAlgebra.homEqui.signature:
TauCeti.Huber.Pair.finiteAlgebra.homEquiv.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {A : Type u_1} [CommRing A]

  {S : TauCeti.Huber.Pair A} {B : Type u_2} [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Module.Finite A B]

  {D : Type u_3} [CommRing D] [TopologicalSpace D] [IsTopologicalRing D]

TauCeti.Huber.Pair.finiteAlgebra.homEqui.doc:
**Morphisms out of the Huber pair of a finite algebra.** Morphisms of Huber pairs
`(B, B⁺) → (D, D⁺)` under `(A, A⁺)` are exactly the `A`-algebra maps `B → D`.

TauCeti.Huber.NoetherianCech.filtration.signature:
TauCeti.Huber.NoetherianCech.filtration.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {B : Type u_1} [CommRing B] {ι : Type u_2}

  (N : Set M) (p i : ℕ) : AddSubgroup (TauCeti.cechLocalizationTerm M f p)
TauCeti.Huber.NoetherianCech.filtration.doc:
**Huber's filtration** `K_i^p` of the term of degree `p`: for a set `N ⊆ M`, the product over
the faces `S`, `|S| = p + 1`, of the subgroups `Iⁱ · C[F_p / f_S] · N` of `M_{f_S}`.

TauCeti.Huber.NoetherianCech.completedTe.signature:
TauCeti.Huber.NoetherianCech.completedTerm.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {B : Type u_1} [CommRing B]

  (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤) (p : ℕ) : Type (max (max u_2 u_3) u_1)
TauCeti.Huber.NoetherianCech.completedTe.doc:
The separated completion of the degree-`p` term of the rational-localization Čech complex,
for the product of the natural module topologies on its faces.

TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.of_isModuleTopo.signature:
TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.of_isModuleTopology.{u_1, u_2} {A : Type u_1} [CommRing A]
  [TopologicalSpace A] {B : Type u_2} [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [IsTopologicalRing A]

  TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing B
TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.of_isModuleTopo.doc:
**A finite algebra over a Tate ring is a Tate ring.** If `B` is a commutative `A`-algebra,
finite as an `A`-module and carrying its natural topology, then `B` is a Tate ring; the image of a
pseudouniformiser of `A` is a pseudouniformiser of `B`.

TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoCoherentOver.signature:
TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoCoherentOver.{u, v} (R : Type u) (M : Type v) [Ring R] [AddCommGroup M]
  [_root_.Module R M] (m : ℕ∞) : Prop
TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoCoherentOver.doc:
`M` is *`m`-pseudocoherent* over `R`: it has a resolution `⋯ → F₁ → F₀ → M → 0` by finite free
modules `Fᵢ = Fin (n i) → R`, with augmentation `ε` and differentials `d i : Fᵢ₊₁ → Fᵢ`, which is
exact at `M, F₀, …, F_{m-1}`. Thus `0`-pseudocoherent means finitely generated,
`1`-pseudocoherent means finitely presented, and for `m = ⊤` the whole resolution is exact
(Kedlaya–Liu II, Definition 1.1.1; Stacks, Tag 064T, with the index negated).

TauCeti.Huber.IsNoetherianType.signature:
TauCeti.Huber.IsNoetherianType.{u_1} (A : Type u_1) [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A]
  [IsTopologicalRing A] [TauCeti.Huber.IsHuberRing A] : Prop
TauCeti.Huber.IsNoetherianType.doc:
A Huber ring is **of noetherian type** if it has a noetherian ring of definition, or if it is
a strongly noetherian Tate ring.

TauCeti.Huber.IsHuberRing.subring.signature:
TauCeti.Huber.IsHuberRing.subring.{u_2} {A : Type u_2} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A]
  [IsTopologicalRing A] [TauCeti.Huber.IsHuberRing A] {C : Subring A} (hC : IsOpen ↑C) :
  TauCeti.Huber.IsHuberRing ↥C
TauCeti.Huber.IsHuberRing.subring.doc:
**Wedhorn Corollary 6.4(2).** An open subring of a Huber ring, with the subspace topology, is
a Huber ring.

TauCeti.HopfIdeal.IsParabolic.signature:
TauCeti.HopfIdeal.IsParabolic.{u, v} (k : Type u) [Field k] (H : CommHopfAlgCat k)
  [Algebra.FiniteType k ↑H] (I : TauCeti.HopfIdeal k ↑H) : Prop
TauCeti.HopfIdeal.IsParabolic.doc:
A Hopf ideal defines a **parabolic subgroup** when its base change to an algebraic closure
defines a smooth closed subgroup of the geometric fibre containing a Borel subgroup.

The order is contravariant: `I ≤ J` says that the subgroup cut out by `I` contains the subgroup
cut out by `J`.

TauCeti.HopfIdeal.IsBorelOverAlgClosed.e.signature:
TauCeti.HopfIdeal.IsBorelOverAlgClosed.exists_conjugate_eq.{u} {k : Type u} [Field k]
  [IsAlgClosed k] {H : TauCeti.FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat k} {I J : TauCeti.HopfIdeal k ↑H.obj}
  (hI : TauCeti.HopfIdeal.IsBorelOverAlgClosed k H I)
  (hJ : TauCeti.HopfIdeal.IsBorelOverAlgClosed k H J) : ∃ g, I.conjugate g = J
TauCeti.HopfIdeal.IsBorelOverAlgClosed.e.doc:
**Borel conjugacy.** Any two Borel subgroups of a finite-type affine group over an
algebraically closed field are conjugate by a rational point. The ambient group need not
be smooth, reduced, or connected.

TauCeti.Homologous.homotopyEquiv.doc:
**Homologous twisting cocycles give homotopy equivalent twisted complexes**: for every
differential graded right module `(ℳ, dM)`, the twisted complexes of `mP` and `mQ` are
homotopy equivalent.

TauCeti.Hodge.exists_isCompl_of_isPolari.doc:
**Semisimplicity of polarizable rational Hodge structures.** Every rational Hodge substructure
of a polarizable pure Hodge structure has a complement, both over `ℚ` and after complexification,
orthogonal to it for some polarization.

TauCeti.Hodge.Polarization.exists_comp_t.signature:

        P.toDualHom.comp g = c • TauCeti.Hodge.HodgeStructure.Hom.id hs.dualTateTwist ∧

TauCeti.Hodge.Polarization.exists_comp_t.doc:
**Self-duality is invertible up to a nonzero integer.** For a polarization of `V`, there is a
Hodge morphism `g : V^*(-n) → V` such that composing it with self-duality, in either order, is
multiplication by a nonzero natural number `c`. Over `ℚ`, `c⁻¹ • g` is the inverse of
self-duality.

TauCeti.Hodge.Polarization.Q.signature:
TauCeti.Hodge.Polarization.Q.{u, v} {V : Type u} {Vℂ : Type v} [AddCommGroup V] [AddCommGroup Vℂ]

  LinearMap.BilinForm ℂ Vℂ
TauCeti.Hodge.Polarization.Q.doc: The complex bilinear form of a polarization, derived by complexifying the integral form.

TauCeti.Hodge.PolarizableHodgeStructureC.signature:
TauCeti.Hodge.PolarizableHodgeStructureCat.exists_iso_biproduct_simple.{u'} {n : ℤ}
  (X : TauCeti.Hodge.PolarizableHodgeStructureCat n) :

      Nonempty ((⨁ fun U => X.ofSubstructure ↑U) ≅ X)
TauCeti.Hodge.PolarizableHodgeStructureC.doc:
**Categorical semisimplicity of polarizable rational Hodge structures.** Every object is
isomorphic to a finite biproduct of simple objects induced by rational Hodge substructures.

The category of finite-dimensional polarizable rational Hodge structures of weight `n`, with
integral, rational, and complex models in `Type u`.

The integral model is a finitely generated free lattice and determines the conjugation on the
complexification. The rational model is the carrier on which morphisms are defined. Polarizability
is retained only as a property, so no particular polarizing form is part of an object.

TauCeti.Hodge.MixedHodgeStructureCat.abe.doc: Mixed Hodge structures, with rational Hodge morphisms, form an abelian category.

TauCeti.Hodge.MixedHodgeStructure.map_la.signature:

TauCeti.Hodge.MixedHodgeStructure.map_la.doc:
**Deligne's fine conjugation relation.** Conjugation exchanges `I^{p,q}` and `I^{q,p}`
modulo the sum of the components `I^{r,s}` with `r < q` and `s < p`.

TauCeti.Hodge.MixedHodgeStructure.isInte.doc:
**Deligne's theorem.** The pieces `I^{p,q}` of Deligne's bigrading form an internal direct sum
of the complex vector space underlying a mixed Hodge structure.

TauCeti.Hodge.MixedHodgeStructure.Hom.ra.doc:
**Strictness of a morphism of mixed Hodge structures for the Hodge filtration.** A complex
vector lying both in the image of `f` and in the target's Hodge step `F^p` is the image of a
vector of the source's `F^p`.

The two filtration steps are the sums of the bigrading pieces of first index at least `p`, and `f`
respects the bigrading, so a preimage may be truncated to its components of first index at least
`p` without changing its image.

TauCeti.Hodge.IsPolarization.doc:
The **Hodge–Riemann bilinear relations** for a fixed integral bilinear form `Q` on the lattice
of a weight-`n` Hodge structure.

The form is `(-1)^n`-symmetric and nondegenerate; its complexification annihilates
`F p × F (n + 1 - p)`; and `i^(p-q) Q x (conj x)` is a positive real number for every nonzero `x`
in the Hodge component `H^{p,q}`, where `q = n - p`.

TauCeti.Hodge.IsPolarizable.internalHom.doc:
**Polarizable pure Hodge structures are closed under internal homs.** The internal hom of
weights `n₁` and `n₂` is polarizable of weight `n₂ - n₁`.

TauCeti.Hodge.IsPolarizable.dual.doc: **The dual of a polarizable pure Hodge structure is polarizable.**

TauCeti.Hodge.HodgeStructureOn.isInterna.doc:
**The Hodge decomposition.** The Hodge components `H^{p,n-p}` form an internal direct sum of
the ambient complex vector space.

TauCeti.Hodge.HodgeStructureOn.finsum_ho.signature:
TauCeti.Hodge.HodgeStructureOn.finsum_hodgeNumber_eq_finrank.{u} {W : Type u} [AddCommGroup W]
  [_root_.Module ℂ W] {ω : TauCeti.Hodge.Conjugation W} {n : ℤ}
  (hs : TauCeti.Hodge.HodgeStructureOn W ω n) [FiniteDimensional ℂ W] :
  ∑ᶠ (p : ℤ), hs.hodgeNumber p = Module.finrank ℂ W
TauCeti.Hodge.HodgeStructureOn.finsum_ho.doc:
**The Hodge numbers partition the dimension**: the Hodge numbers of a weight-`n` Hodge
structure on a finite-dimensional complex vector space sum to its dimension.

TauCeti.Hodge.HodgeStructureOn.signature:
TauCeti.Hodge.HodgeStructureOn.{u} (W : Type u) [AddCommGroup W] [_root_.Module ℂ W]
  (ω : TauCeti.Hodge.Conjugation W) (n : ℤ) : Type u
TauCeti.Hodge.HodgeStructureOn.doc:
A pure Hodge structure of weight `n` on a complex vector space with conjugation `ω`.

The decreasing filtration `F` is bounded and `n`-opposed to its conjugate: for every `p`,
`F p` is complementary to the conjugate of `F (n + 1 - p)`.

TauCeti.Henselization.henselian.signature:
TauCeti.Henselization.henselian.{u} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) :
  HenselianRing (↑(TauCeti.Henselization.algebra I)) (TauCeti.Henselization.extended I)
TauCeti.Henselization.henselian.doc:
**The henselization of a pair is henselian.** The pair formed by the henselization of
`(R, I)` and the extended ideal is a henselian pair, with no hypothesis on `R` or `I`.

TauCeti.Henselization.existsUnique_lift.signature:

TauCeti.Henselization.existsUnique_lift.doc:
**The universal property of the henselization.** For a henselian pair `(S, J)` receiving a
map of pairs from `(R, I)`, there is a unique `R`-algebra map from the henselization of
`(R, I)` to `S` carrying the extended ideal into `J`.

TauCeti.Henselization.existsUnique_isLoc.signature:
TauCeti.Henselization.existsUnique_isLocalHom.{u, v} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
  {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [HenselianLocalRing S] [Algebra R S] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] :
  ∃! f, IsLocalHom f
TauCeti.Henselization.existsUnique_isLoc.doc:
**The universal property of the henselization of a local ring.** Every local homomorphism
from a local ring `R` to a henselian local ring `S` factors through a unique local
`R`-algebra map from the henselization of `R` along its maximal ideal. Every `R`-algebra map
from the henselization to `S` is in fact local and equal to this one (`eq_lift`).

TauCeti.HeisenbergDGA.minimalModel_m_thr.signature:
TauCeti.HeisenbergDGA.minimalModel_m_three.{u_1} (R : Type u_1) [CommRing R] :
  ((TauCeti.HeisenbergDGA.minimalModel R).m 3)

        (TauCeti.HeisenbergDGA.aInfinityAlgebra R).cohomologyClass ⋯,
        (TauCeti.HeisenbergDGA.aInfinityAlgebra R).cohomologyClass ⋯] =
    (TauCeti.HeisenbergDGA.aInfinityAlgebra R).cohomologyClass ⋯
TauCeti.HeisenbergDGA.minimalModel_m_thr.doc:
**The transferred ternary operation on `([a], [a], [b])`**: `m₃^H ([a], [a], [b]) = [a c]`.
Of the Kontsevich--Soibelman/Merkulov tree sum only the term
`-p m₂ (i (τ [a]), h m₂ (i [a], i [b]))` survives, with `h (a b) = c` and the Koszul twist
`τ [a] = -[a]`.

TauCeti.HeegaardRegionSystem.hatDifferen.signature:
TauCeti.HeegaardRegionSystem.hatDifferential.{u, v, w} {n : ℕ} {Point : Type u} {Region : Type v}
  {Basepoint : Type w} (H : TauCeti.HeegaardRegionSystem n Point Region Basepoint) [Fintype Point]

  (H.Generator →₀ ZMod 2) →ₗ[ZMod 2] H.Generator →₀ ZMod 2
TauCeti.HeegaardRegionSystem.hatDifferen.doc:
The hat differential of a Heegaard diagram with region Euler characteristics `χ`: the
`ZMod 2`-linear endomorphism of the free module on generators whose coefficient from `x` to `y`
is the number, modulo two, of nonnegative domains of Maslov index one from `x` to `y` avoiding
the basepoints (`TauCeti.HeegaardRegionSystem.hatCoefficient`).

TauCeti.HeegaardRegionSystem.IsNice.doc:
A pointed Heegaard diagram, with region Euler characteristics `χ`, is *nice* when every
region containing no basepoint is a bigon or a square: a disk, of Euler characteristic one, with
two or four corners.

TauCeti.HasNodalReduction.of_genus_eq_ze.signature:

TauCeti.HasNodalReduction.of_genus_eq_ze.doc:
**A curve of genus zero with a divisor of degree one has nodal reduction.** Let `C` be a
regular proper curve over the fraction field `K` of a discrete valuation ring `R`, with `K`
integrally closed in `K(C)`. If `dim_K H¹(C, 𝒪_C) = 0` and some divisor on `C` has degree one,
then `C` has a proper at-worst-nodal model over `R`; indeed `C ≅ ℙ¹_K`, which has the smooth proper
model `ℙ¹_R`.

TauCeti.HasGaloisLabel.signature:
TauCeti.HasGaloisLabel.{u} {F : Type u} [Field F] (f : Polynomial F) {n : ℕ}
  (j : TauCeti.TransitiveGroupIndex n) : Prop
TauCeti.HasGaloisLabel.doc:
The Galois group of `f` carries the transitive-group label `j` of degree `n`: `f` is
separable of degree `n`, and some numbering of its roots in the splitting field by `Fin n` carries
the image of the Galois action on the roots to a conjugate of the reference subgroup
`referenceSubgroup n j`. By `TauCeti.hasGaloisLabel_iff_forall`, every numbering then does.

TauCeti.HasApproximationProperty.signature:
TauCeti.HasApproximationProperty.{u_1, u_2} (𝕜 : Type u_1) (E : Type u_2)
  [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] : Prop
TauCeti.HasApproximationProperty.doc:
The identity can be approximated uniformly on every norm-compact set by bounded operators
with finite-dimensional range.

TauCeti.HaagerupZsido.integral_norm_reci.doc: **The exact mass of the Haagerup–Zsidó kernel.** `∫_ℝ ‖k(t)‖ dt = π / 2`.

TauCeti.GroupPresentation.homEquiv.signature:
TauCeti.GroupPresentation.homEquiv.{u_1} (P : TauCeti.GroupPresentation) {G : Type u_1} [Group G] :

TauCeti.GroupPresentation.homEquiv.doc:
Homomorphisms from a finite presentation correspond to generator assignments satisfying
its transcribed relators. No generation or injectivity condition is imposed on the assignment.

TauCeti.GroupAlgGeom.zariskiTopology.signature:

TauCeti.GroupAlgGeom.zariskiTopology.doc: The Zariski topology generated by the complements of algebraic sets over `G`.

TauCeti.GroupAlgGeom.isEquationallyNoeth.doc:
**Linear groups are equationally Noetherian.** Over a commutative Noetherian ring `R`, the
general linear group `GL n R` is equationally Noetherian over any coefficients: every system of
equations in finitely many variables has a finite subsystem with the same solutions in
`GL n R`.

TauCeti.GroupAlgGeom.IsGDomain.of_isCSA.signature:

TauCeti.GroupAlgGeom.IsGDomain.of_isCSA.doc:
**CSA groups are domains** (Baumslag–Myasnikov–Remeslennikov, Proposition 1). A CSA group in
which the images of two coefficients do not commute is a domain over these coefficients.

TauCeti.GroupAlgGeom.CoordGroup.signature:
TauCeti.GroupAlgGeom.CoordGroup.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {G : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} {X : Type u_3}

TauCeti.GromovWassersteinSpace.signature:
TauCeti.GromovWassersteinSpace.{u, v} (p : ENNReal) (Z : Type v) [MetricSpace Z] [Fact (1 ≤ p)] :
  Type (max (u + 1) v)
TauCeti.GromovWassersteinSpace.doc:
Finite-size standard Borel measured kernels modulo weak isomorphism, with the full
Gromov–Wasserstein metric. The carrier universe is fixed, but is independent of the target.

TauCeti.GridLink.unknottingNumber.doc:
The unknotting number of a grid link: the least number of crossing changes turning it into
the unknot, or `⊤` if no sequence of crossing changes does.

TauCeti.GridDiagram.unblockedHomologyCom.doc:
**The commutation map on `GH⁻` preserves the class of the `X`-marking state.** Under the
condition of `commutationMap_single_X`, the induced map on unblocked grid homology sends the
class of the `X`-marking state of `G` to that of the commuted diagram.

The homotopy equation `∂ ∘ H + H ∘ ∂ = 1 + Ψ ∘ Φ` of a column commutation, over any
commutative semiring of characteristic two: the hexagon-counting map `H` is a chain homotopy
between the identity of `GC⁻(G)` and the round trip through the commuted diagram.

TauCeti.GridDiagram.two_mul_tau_torusLin.doc:
**`τ` of a torus knot grid**: on the standard grid of the `(p + 1, q + 1)` torus knot,
`2 τ = -p q`.
