**Stabilization invariance of `GH⁻`.** The map `GH⁻(G') → GH⁻(G)` induced by the
stabilization chain map is bijective.

TauCeti.GridDiagram.commutationMap_comp_.signature:
TauCeti.GridDiagram.commutationMap_comp_unblockedDifferential.{u_1} {n : ℕ}
  (G : TauCeti.GridDiagram n) (C : TauCeti.GridDiagram.ColumnTurn n) (R : Type u_1) [CommSemiring R]
  [CharP R 2] :
  G.commutationMap R C ∘ₛₗ G.unblockedDifferential R =
    (TauCeti.GridDiagram.swapColumns C.column ((finRotate n) C.column) G).unblockedDifferential
        R ∘ₛₗ
      G.commutationMap R C
TauCeti.GridDiagram.commutationMap_comp_.doc:
**The commutation map is a chain map.** Over a commutative semiring of characteristic two,
counting empty pentagons turning on either side of the replaced grid line intertwines the unblocked
differentials of a grid diagram and of the diagram with the two columns of the turn exchanged.
This holds at every column turn: the two marking segments need not be non-interleaving.

TauCeti.GridDiagram.commutationBidegree_.signature:
TauCeti.GridDiagram.commutationBidegree_eq_of_notMem_columnArc {n : ℕ} {G : TauCeti.GridDiagram n}
  (C : TauCeti.GridDiagram.ColumnTurn n)
  (h : G.ColumnsInterleaving C.column ((finRotate n) C.column))
  (hO : G.O.toPerm C.column ∉ G.columnArc ((finRotate n) C.column))
  (hs : C.turnRow = G.X.toPerm C.column) : G.commutationBidegree C = (-2, -1)
TauCeti.GridDiagram.commutationBidegree_.doc:
**A chain map of bidegree `(-2, -1)` across a crossing change.** If the segments of the two
columns of the column turn `C` interleave and the `O`-marking of the first column does not lie on
the arc of the second, then the commutation map turning in the row of the `X`-marking of the
first column has bidegree `(-2, -1)`, the bidegree of multiplication by `U`.

TauCeti.GridDiagram.IsKnot.tau.signature:
TauCeti.GridDiagram.IsKnot.tau.{u_1} {n : ℕ} {G : TauCeti.GridDiagram n} (hG : G.IsKnot)
  (K : Type u_1) [CommRing K] [CharP K 2] : ℤ
TauCeti.GridDiagram.IsKnot.tau.doc:
**The invariant `τ` of a knot grid diagram**: minus the largest Alexander degree of a
homogeneous element of the unblocked grid homology `GH⁻(G)` that is not `K[U]`-torsion.

Over a Noetherian `K`, the supremum is attained as soon as `GH⁻(G)` is not a torsion module
(`isGreatest_nonTorsionDegrees_neg_tau`); if `GH⁻(G)` is torsion the value is `0`, the supremum
of the empty set. It is an invariant of the presented knot: knot grids connected by grid moves
have the same `τ` (`tau_eq_of_movesTo`, in `Homology/Invariance.lean`). This is the grid
definition of the concordance invariant `τ` of Ozsváth--Stipsicz--Szabó.

TauCeti.Green.green_ac_winding.signature:
TauCeti.Green.green_ac_winding {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {U : Set ℂ} {P Q : ℂ → ℝ} (hab : a < b)
  (hγ : AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval γ a b) (hclosed : γ a = γ b) (hU : IsOpen U)
  (htrace : γ '' Set.uIcc a b ⊆ U) (hP : ContDiffOn ℝ 1 P U) (hQ : ContDiffOn ℝ 1 Q U)
  (hindex : ∀ z ∉ U, TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber γ a b z = 0) :
  IntervalIntegrable (TauCeti.Green.circulationFun P Q γ) MeasureTheory.volume a b ∧
    MeasureTheory.IntegrableOn
        (fun z => TauCeti.Green.windingWeight γ a b z * TauCeti.Green.curl P Q z) U
        MeasureTheory.volume ∧
      ∫ (t : ℝ) in a..b, TauCeti.Green.circulationFun P Q γ t =
        ∫ (z : ℂ) in U, TauCeti.Green.windingWeight γ a b z * TauCeti.Green.curl P Q z
TauCeti.Green.green_ac_winding.doc:
Green's theorem for a closed absolutely continuous curve with index vanishing outside
the open field domain. The winding numbers may be unbounded and the curve may intersect itself.

TauCeti.GraphTwistedIndex.steinberg_eq_g.doc:
**The Steinberg endomorphism is the graph automorphism composed with the Frobenius**,
uniformly in the thirteen ordinary and graph-twisted families. On the nine untwisted ones the
graph factor is trivial and the composite is the Frobenius itself, which is
`TauCeti.GraphTwistedIndex.steinberg_eq_frobenius`.

TauCeti.GradedProjectiveResolution.IsLin.doc:
A graded projective resolution is **linear** if its term in homological degree `n` is
generated by its homogeneous piece of internal degree `n`.

TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.rayClassIdeal.signature:
TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.rayClassIdealCount.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [NumberField K]
  (𝔪 : TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.Modulus K) :
  ∃ δ,
    0 < δ ∧
      ∀ (c : TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.RayClassGroup 𝔪),
        (fun x =>
            ↑(TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.rayClassIdealCountingFunction 𝔪 c x) -
              TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.rayClassIdealMainTerm 𝔪 * x) =O[Filter.atTop]
          fun x => x ^ (1 - δ)
TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.rayClassIdeal.doc:
**The ray class ideal count.**  For every modulus `𝔪` there is a power saving `δ > 0` such
that, in each ray class `c` of `𝔪`, the number of nonzero integral ideals prime to `𝔪` of norm at
most `x` is `rayClassIdealMainTerm 𝔪 * x + O(x ^ (1 - δ))`.  One can take `δ = 1 / [K : ℚ]`;
for that explicit exponent, use `isBigO_rayClassIdealCountingFunction_sub` instead.

TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.ratModulusEqu.signature:
TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.ratModulusEquivGal.{u_1} (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (F : Type u_1) [Field F]
  [NumberField F] [IsCyclotomicExtension {n} ℚ F] :
  TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.RayClassGroup (TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.ratModulus n ⋯) ≃* Gal(F/ℚ)
TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.ratModulusEqu.doc:
**The ray class group of `ℚ` modulo `(n)·∞` is the Galois group of `ℚ(ζ_n)`.** The
composite of `ratModulusEquivZMod` with the inverse of Mathlib's `galEquivZMod`: a ray class with
residue `a ∈ (ZMod n)ˣ` goes to the automorphism acting on the `n`-th roots of unity by
`ζ ↦ ζ ^ a`. It sends the ray class of a prime `p ∤ n` to the arithmetic Frobenius at `p`
(`isArithFrobAt_iff_eq_ratModulusEquivGal_idealClass`).

TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.normOneProdEq.signature:
TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.normOneProdEquiv.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [NumberField K]
  (w : NumberField.InfinitePlace K) :
  NumberField.IdeleClassGroup (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K ≃ₜ*
    ↥(TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.IdeleClassGroup.normOne K) × NNRealˣ
TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.normOneProdEq.doc:
**The idele class group splits as `C_K¹ × ℝ>0`.** The infinite place `w` determines the
isomorphism of topological groups sending an idele class `c` to its norm-one part
`c · s(‖c‖)⁻¹` and its norm `‖c‖`, where `s = ideleClassNormSection K w`.

TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.adeleBaseChan.signature:
TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.adeleBaseChangeEquiv_tower.{u_1, u_2, u_3} (K : Type u_1) (L : Type u_2)
  [Field K] [NumberField K] [Field L] [NumberField L] [Algebra K L]
  [TopologicalSpace (TensorProduct K (NumberField.AdeleRing (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K) L)]
  [IsModuleTopology (NumberField.AdeleRing (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K)
      (TensorProduct K (NumberField.AdeleRing (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K) L)]
  (M : Type u_3) [Field M] [NumberField M] [Algebra K M] [Algebra L M] [IsScalarTower K L M]
  [TopologicalSpace (TensorProduct K (NumberField.AdeleRing (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K) M)]
  [IsModuleTopology (NumberField.AdeleRing (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K)
      (TensorProduct K (NumberField.AdeleRing (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K) M)]
  [TopologicalSpace (TensorProduct L (NumberField.AdeleRing (NumberField.RingOfIntegers L) L) M)]
  [IsModuleTopology (NumberField.AdeleRing (NumberField.RingOfIntegers L) L)
      (TensorProduct L (NumberField.AdeleRing (NumberField.RingOfIntegers L) L) M)]
  (a : NumberField.AdeleRing (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K) (z : M) :
  (TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.adeleBaseChangeEquiv K M) (a ⊗ₜ[K] z) =
    (TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.adeleBaseChangeEquiv L M)
      ((TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.adeleBaseChangeEquiv K L) (a ⊗ₜ[K] 1) ⊗ₜ[L] z)
TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.adeleBaseChan.doc:
**Base change of adeles in a tower** `K ⊆ L ⊆ M`: the comparison for `M/K` factors through
the comparison for `L/K`, followed by the comparison for `M/L`.

TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.NumberFieldOr.signature:
TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.NumberFieldOrder.mem_ker_rayClassToPic.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K]
  [NumberField K] (O : TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.NumberFieldOrder K)
  {c : TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.RayClassGroup O.conductorModulus} :
  c ∈ O.rayClassToPic.ker ↔
    ∃ J,
      (TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.idealClass O.conductorModulus) J = c ∧
        ∃ β ∈ O.toRingOfIntegers, ↑J = Ideal.span {β}
TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.NumberFieldOr.doc:
**The congruence description of the Picard group.** A ray class of the conductor maps to the
trivial Picard class exactly when it is the ray class of an ideal of `𝓞 K` generated by an element
of the order.

TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.NumberFieldOr.signature:
TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.NumberFieldOrder.mem_ker_rayClassToNarrowPic.{u_1} {K : Type u_1}
  [Field K] [NumberField K] (O : TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.NumberFieldOrder K)
  {c : TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.RayClassGroup O.narrowConductorModulus} :
  c ∈ O.rayClassToNarrowPic.ker ↔
    ∃ J,
      (TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.idealClass O.narrowConductorModulus) J = c ∧
        ∃ β ∈ O.toRingOfIntegers, NumberField.IsTotallyPositive ↑β ∧ ↑J = Ideal.span {β}
TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.NumberFieldOr.doc:
**The congruence description of the narrow Picard group.** A ray class of the narrow conductor
modulus maps to the trivial narrow Picard class exactly when it is the ray class of an ideal of
`𝓞 K` generated by a totally positive element of the order.

TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.NumberFieldOr.signature:
TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.NumberFieldOrder.isGorenstein_iff_forall_isUnit.{u} {K : Type u}
  [Field K] [NumberField K] (O : TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.NumberFieldOrder K) :
  O.IsGorenstein ↔
    ∀ (I : FractionalIdeal (nonZeroDivisors ↥O.toSubalgebra) K),
      O.IsProperFractionalIdeal I → IsUnit I
TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.NumberFieldOr.doc: **An order is Gorenstein exactly when all of its proper fractional ideals are invertible.**

TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.HeckeCharacte.doc:
**The infinite part of the conductor is the set of real signs.** A real place `w` divides the
conductor of a finite-order Hecke character exactly when its real parity at `w` is one, that is,
when the character is nontrivial on the negative elements of `K_w`.

**Finite-order Hecke characters are exactly the ray class characters**: a Hecke character has
finite order exactly when it is the pullback of a ray class character of some modulus.

TauCeti.GTopology.isSheaf_iff.signature:
TauCeti.GTopology.isSheaf_iff.{u, v, w} {X : Type u} {B : Type v} [SemilatticeInf B] [OrderTop B]
  {ι : B ↪o Set X} (G : TauCeti.GTopology ι) (P : CategoryTheory.Functor Bᵒᵖ (Type w)) :
  CategoryTheory.Presieve.IsSheaf G.grothendieckTopology P ↔
    ∀ (U : B) (S : Set B),
      G.Covers U S → CategoryTheory.Presieve.IsSheafFor P (TauCeti.GTopology.coverPresieve U S)
TauCeti.GTopology.isSheaf_iff.doc:
The site sheaf condition is precisely unique gluing of matching families on all admissible
covers. `Presieve.IsSheafFor` is Mathlib's existence-and-uniqueness condition for amalgamations.

TauCeti.GTopology.signature:
TauCeti.GTopology.{u, v} {X : Type u} {B : Type v} [SemilatticeInf B] [OrderTop B]
  (ι : B ↪o Set X) : Type v
TauCeti.GTopology.doc:
Admissible covers on a family of subsets closed under finite intersections and containing
the whole space. The family is represented by an order embedding `ι`, preserving intersections
and the largest open. Covering families are sets, so repetitions and indexing choices carry
no additional data.

TauCeti.FundamentalGroupoid.isColimitCec.doc:
**The groupoid van Kampen theorem.** For an open cover of `X`, the fundamental groupoid of
`X` is the colimit of the fundamental groupoids of the nonempty finite intersections of members
of the cover.

TauCeti.FormalGroupIso.signature: TauCeti.FormalGroupIso.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (F G : FormalGroup R) : Type u_1
TauCeti.FormalGroupIso.doc:
An isomorphism of formal group laws with specified mutually inverse homomorphisms.
The inverse laws are equations of substitution operators on one-variable power series.

TauCeti.FormalGroupHom.signature: TauCeti.FormalGroupHom.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (F G : FormalGroup R) : Type u_1
TauCeti.FormalGroupHom.doc:
A homomorphism of formal group laws is a series `f` with zero constant term such that
`f(F(X,Y)) = G(f(X),f(Y))`.

TauCeti.FormalCoordinate.jetLimitEquiv.signature:
TauCeti.FormalCoordinate.jetLimitEquiv.{u_1} (R : Type u_1) [CommRing R] :
  TauCeti.FormalCoordinate R ≃ₜ* ↥(TauCeti.FormalCoordinate.jetLimit R)
TauCeti.FormalCoordinate.jetLimitEquiv.doc:
The formal coordinates are the inverse limit of their jet groups: passing to all jets is an
isomorphism of topological groups onto the compatible families of jets.

TauCeti.FormalCoordinate.signature: TauCeti.FormalCoordinate.{u_1} (R : Type u_1) [CommRing R] : Type u_1
TauCeti.FormalCoordinate.doc:
A formal coordinate over `R`: a power series `φ = u X + ⋯` with zero constant coefficient
and unit linear coefficient `u`. These are the changes of formal parameter `X ↦ φ`.

TauCeti.Foliation.eulerClass.doc:
The Euler class `Hᵏ(TF, TF₀) ⟶ Hᵏ(M)` of the tangent field of a foliation of rank `k`:
`TauCeti.eulerClass`, restriction to the total space followed by pullback along the zero
section, read in degree `k`.

TauCeti.Flow.exists_val_eq_arrowSum.signature:
TauCeti.Flow.exists_val_eq_arrowSum.{u, v, w} {V : Type u} {Q : V → V → Type v} {K : Type w}
  [Fintype V] [(v w : V) → Fintype (Q v w)] [AddCommGroup K] [LinearOrder K] [IsOrderedAddMonoid K]
  {cap : TauCeti.Assignment Q K} {s t : V} [DecidableEq V] (hst : s ≠ t) (hcap : 0 ≤ cap) :
  ∃ f S, s ∈ S ∧ t ∉ S ∧ f.val = TauCeti.arrowSum cap S Sᶜ
TauCeti.Flow.exists_val_eq_arrowSum.doc:
**Max-flow/min-cut theorem.** For nonnegative capacities and distinct terminals, some ordinary
flow has value equal to the capacity of the arrows leaving some vertex set containing `s` but not
`t`. By weak duality (`TauCeti.Flow.val_le_arrowSum`) this flow is maximum and this cut is
minimum.

TauCeti.Flow.exists_isMaximum_mem.signature:
TauCeti.Flow.exists_isMaximum_mem.{u, v, w} {V : Type u} {Q : V → V → Type v} {K : Type w}
  [Fintype V] [(v w : V) → Fintype (Q v w)] [AddCommGroup K] [LinearOrder K] [IsOrderedAddMonoid K]
  {cap : TauCeti.Assignment Q K} {s t : V} (hcap : 0 ≤ cap) (H : AddSubgroup K)
  (hcapH : ∀ ⦃v w : V⦄ (e : Q v w), cap e ∈ H) :
  ∃ f, f.IsMaximum ∧ ∀ ⦃v w : V⦄ (e : Q v w), f.toFun e ∈ H
TauCeti.Flow.exists_isMaximum_mem.doc:
**Integrality of maximum flows.** For nonnegative capacities in an additive subgroup `H`, some
maximum ordinary flow takes values in `H`. For distinct terminals, its value is the capacity of
some cut by `TauCeti.Flow.IsMaximum.exists_val_eq_arrowSum`.

TauCeti.Flow.exists_isAcyclic.signature:
TauCeti.Flow.exists_isAcyclic.{u, v, w} {V : Type u} {Q : V → V → Type v} {K : Type w} [Fintype V]
  [(x y : V) → Fintype (Q x y)] [AddCommGroup K] [LinearOrder K] [IsOrderedAddMonoid K]
  {cap : TauCeti.Assignment Q K} {s t : V} (f : TauCeti.Flow cap s t) :
  ∃ g, g.toFun.IsAcyclic ∧ g.val = f.val ∧ g.toFun ≤ f.toFun
TauCeti.Flow.exists_isAcyclic.doc:
**Acyclic flows.** Every ordinary `s`–`t` flow `f` has an acyclic ordinary `s`–`t` flow of the
same value that is arrowwise at most `f`.

TauCeti.Floer.periodGroupComparison_sing.signature:
TauCeti.Floer.periodGroupComparison_single_eq_iff.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2}
  [AddCommGroup S] (ω : S →+ ℝ) (c : S →+ ℤ) [Semiring R] {r : R} (hr : r ≠ 0) (A B : S) :
  (TauCeti.Floer.periodGroupComparison ω c) (TauCeti.NovikovSeries.single A r) =
      (TauCeti.Floer.periodGroupComparison ω c) (TauCeti.NovikovSeries.single B r) ↔
    ω A = ω B ∧ c A = c B
TauCeti.Floer.periodGroupComparison_sing.doc:
Monomial descent identifies precisely the joint periods, retaining equal-area classes
of different Chern number. The coefficient is assumed nonzero.

TauCeti.Floer.coefficientComparison.doc:
The completed coefficient comparison `q^A ↦ e^(-q A)`, with source period `ω` and
target period `-Ω`. Area preservation makes it a unital ring homomorphism.

TauCeti.Floer.add_sub_add_two_mul_chern_.signature:
TauCeti.Floer.add_sub_add_two_mul_chern_productClass_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {S : Type u_1}
  [AddGroup S] {ω : S →+ ℝ} {c : S →+ ℤ} {C₁ : Type u_2} {C₂ : Type u_3} {C₀ : Type u_4}
  [AddTorsor (TauCeti.Floer.PeriodGroup ω c) C₀] {glue : C₁ → C₂ → C₀}
  [AddTorsor (TauCeti.Floer.PeriodGroup ω c) C₁] [AddTorsor (TauCeti.Floer.PeriodGroup ω c) C₂]
  {m₁ : C₁ → ℤ} {m₂ : C₂ → ℤ} {m₀ : C₀ → ℤ}
  (hglue₁ :
    ∀ (γ : TauCeti.Floer.PeriodGroup ω c) (D₁ : C₁) (D₂ : C₂), glue (γ +ᵥ D₁) D₂ = γ +ᵥ glue D₁ D₂)
  (hglue₂ :
    ∀ (γ : TauCeti.Floer.PeriodGroup ω c) (D₁ : C₁) (D₂ : C₂), glue D₁ (γ +ᵥ D₂) = γ +ᵥ glue D₁ D₂)
  (hm₁ :
    ∀ (γ : TauCeti.Floer.PeriodGroup ω c) (D : C₁),
      m₁ (γ +ᵥ D) = 2 * (TauCeti.Floer.PeriodGroup.chern ω c) γ + m₁ D)
  (hm₂ :
    ∀ (γ : TauCeti.Floer.PeriodGroup ω c) (D : C₂),
      m₂ (γ +ᵥ D) = 2 * (TauCeti.Floer.PeriodGroup.chern ω c) γ + m₂ D)
  (hm₀ :
    ∀ (γ : TauCeti.Floer.PeriodGroup ω c) (D : C₀),
      m₀ (γ +ᵥ D) = 2 * (TauCeti.Floer.PeriodGroup.chern ω c) γ + m₀ D)
  (D₁ D₁' : C₁) (D₂ D₂' : C₂) (D₀ D₀' : C₀) :
  m₁ D₁ + m₂ D₂ - m₀ D₀ +
      2 * (TauCeti.Floer.PeriodGroup.chern ω c) (TauCeti.Floer.productClass glue D₁ D₂ D₀) =
    m₁ D₁' + m₂ D₂' - m₀ D₀' +
      2 * (TauCeti.Floer.PeriodGroup.chern ω c) (TauCeti.Floer.productClass glue D₁' D₂' D₀')
TauCeti.Floer.add_sub_add_two_mul_chern_.doc:
Cap independence of the index `μ₁(D₁) + μ₂(D₂) − μ₀(D₀) + 2 c₁(A)` of a product coefficient,
for gradings `mᵢ` obeying the recapping law for twice the first Chern number. The Fredholm index
of a pair of pants in class `A` is this quantity minus half the dimension of the target.

TauCeti.Floer.PeriodGroup.signature: TauCeti.Floer.PeriodGroup.{u_1} {S : Type u_1} [AddGroup S] (ω : S →+ ℝ) (c : S →+ ℤ) : Type u_1
TauCeti.Floer.PeriodGroup.doc:
The period group `Γ = S ⧸ (ker ω ⊓ ker c)` of a group of spherical classes `S` with symplectic
area `ω` and first Chern number `c`, written as the quotient by the kernel of `s ↦ (ω s, c s)`.

It is an abbreviation so that the quotient group API of Mathlib applies to it directly.

TauCeti.Floer.NovikovRing.forall_finite_.doc:
For a positively monotone pair, a coefficient function on the period group satisfies the
Novikov condition of the Floer Novikov ring exactly when the degrees of its support are bounded
above.

TauCeti.Floer.NovikovRing.signature:
TauCeti.Floer.NovikovRing.{u_1, u_2} {S : Type u_1} [AddGroup S] (R : Type u_2) (ω : S →+ ℝ)
  (c : S →+ ℤ) [Zero R] : Type (max u_1 u_2)
TauCeti.Floer.NovikovRing.doc:
The Floer Novikov ring over `R`: Novikov series `∑ a_γ e^γ` over the period group, with
valuation `ν(γ) = -ω(γ)`, so that for every bound `C` only finitely many classes with nonzero
coefficient have area greater than `-C`. It is graded by `PeriodGroup.degree`.

TauCeti.Floer.CapClass.mk_eq_mk_iff_acti.signature:
TauCeti.Floer.CapClass.mk_eq_mk_iff_action_eq_and_index_eq.{u_1, u_2} {S : Type u_1} [AddGroup S]
  {ω : S →+ ℝ} {c : S →+ ℤ} {P : Type u_2} [AddTorsor S P] {a : P → ℝ} {m : P → ℤ}
  (ha : ∀ (g : S) (p : P), a (g +ᵥ p) = ω g + a p)
  (hm : ∀ (g : S) (p : P), m (g +ᵥ p) = 2 * c g + m p) {p q : P} :
  Quotient.mk'' p = Quotient.mk'' q ↔ a p = a q ∧ m p = m q
TauCeti.Floer.CapClass.mk_eq_mk_iff_acti.doc:
Two raw caps have the same class exactly when they have the same action and the same grading,
for functions `a` and `m` on raw caps obeying the recapping laws for area and twice the first
Chern number.

TauCeti.FixedPoints.subalgebra_eq_adjoin.signature:
TauCeti.FixedPoints.subalgebra_eq_adjoin_sum_smul_prod_pow.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {R : Type u_1}
  {A : Type u_2} {G : Type u_3} [CommRing R] [Algebra ℚ R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] [Fintype G]
  {ι : Type u_4} [Group G] [MulSemiringAction G A] [SMulCommClass G R A] (x : ι → A)
  (hx : Algebra.adjoin R (Set.range x) = ⊤) :
  FixedPoints.subalgebra R A G =
    Algebra.adjoin R
      ((fun d => ∑ g, g • d.prod fun i n => x i ^ n) '' {d | Finsupp.degree d ≤ Fintype.card G})
TauCeti.FixedPoints.subalgebra_eq_adjoin.doc:
**Noether's degree bound.** If a family `x`, finite or not, generates a commutative algebra `A`
over a `ℚ`-algebra `R`, then the invariants of a finite group `G` acting on `A` are generated by the
orbit sums `∑_{g ∈ G} g • x^d` of the monomials `x^d` of total degree at most `|G|`.

TauCeti.FixedPoints.finiteType_subalgebra.{u_1, u_2, u_3} (R : Type u_1) (A : Type u_2)

**Noether's finiteness theorem.** Over a Noetherian base ring `R`, the invariants of a finite
group acting on a finite-type `R`-algebra form a finite-type `R`-algebra.

**The invariants of a finite étale algebra under a finite monoid of algebra endomorphisms form
an étale algebra.**

Transport the candidate through an equivariant surjection with finite kernel whose only
fixed point is the identity.

  [Semiring R] : Submodule R ((n : ℕ) → A n →₀ R)
TauCeti.FiniteQuotientTower.compatibleFa.doc:
The **compatible families** along a tower: the families of finitely supported coefficients
`c n : A n →₀ R` such that pushing `c n` forward along the transition map to a level `m ≤ n`,
which sums the coefficients over each fibre, gives `c m`.

TauCeti.FiniteQuotientTower.signature:
TauCeti.FiniteQuotientTower.{u_1, u_2} (Γ : Type u_1) [Group Γ] [TopologicalSpace Γ]
  (A : ℕ → Type u_2) [(n : ℕ) → Group (A n)] [(n : ℕ) → TopologicalSpace (A n)]
  [∀ (n : ℕ), DiscreteTopology (A n)] : Type (max u_1 u_2)
TauCeti.FiniteQuotientTower.doc:
A **tower of finite quotients** of a topological group `Γ`: continuous surjective
homomorphisms `q n : Γ → A n` onto discrete groups, with transition homomorphisms
`t h : A n → A m` for `m ≤ n` compatible with the projections, such that the projections separate
the points of `Γ`.

The transition homomorphisms are determined by the projections (`FiniteQuotientTower.ext`).
When `Γ` is compact the groups `A n` are finite (`FiniteQuotientTower.finite`) and the kernels of
the projections are cofinal among the open subgroups
(`FiniteQuotientTower.exists_ker_le_of_isOpen`).

TauCeti.FiniteQuadraticModule.orthogonal.doc: The orthogonal group `O(A)` of a finite quadratic module `A`.

TauCeti.FiniteQuadraticModule.doc:
A finite abelian group equipped with a quadratic map to `ℚ/ℤ`.

The associated bilinear pairing is required to be the polar form, so the quadratic map determines
all pairing values.

TauCeti.FiniteField.rationalPointsMulEquivFixedSubgroupGeometricFrobenius.{u_1, u_2, u_3}
  (K : Type u_1) [Field K] [Fintype K] (k : Type u_2) [CommRing k] [IsDomain k] [Algebra K k]

TauCeti.FiniteField.rationalPointsMulEqu.doc:
**`G₀(K) ≃ G^F`.** The `K`-rational points of `H` are isomorphic to the points of the base
change `k ⊗[K] H` over a domain `k` fixed by the geometric Frobenius. The isomorphism sends a
rational point `g` to `s ⊗ h ↦ s * g h`.

TauCeti.FiniteEtaleScheme.galoisEquivale.signature:
TauCeti.FiniteEtaleScheme.galoisEquivalenceCommGrp.{u} (K Ω : Type u) [Field K] [Field Ω]
  [Algebra K Ω] [IsSepClosed Ω] [IsGalois K Ω] :

    CategoryTheory.CommGrp (ContAction FintypeCat Gal(Ω/K))
TauCeti.FiniteEtaleScheme.galoisEquivale.doc:
**Finite étale commutative group schemes over a field are finite Galois modules.**
Commutative group objects in finite étale `K`-schemes are equivalent to commutative group objects
in finite continuous `Gal(Ω/K)`-sets, that is, to finite abelian groups with a continuous action
of `Gal(Ω/K)` by group automorphisms.

TauCeti.FiniteEtaleScheme.galoisEquivale.signature:
TauCeti.FiniteEtaleScheme.galoisEquivalence.{u} (K Ω : Type u) [Field K] [Field Ω] [Algebra K Ω]
  [IsSepClosed Ω] [IsGalois K Ω] :
  TauCeti.FiniteEtaleScheme (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec ↧K) ≌ ContAction FintypeCat Gal(Ω/K)
TauCeti.FiniteEtaleScheme.galoisEquivale.doc:
**Galois theory for finite étale schemes over a field.** For a separable closure `Ω` of `K`,
finite étale `K`-schemes are equivalent to finite sets with a continuous action of `Gal(Ω/K)`.
A finite étale scheme `Spec A` goes to the set of `Ω`-valued points of `A`
(`specCompGaloisEquivalenceFunctorIso`).

TauCeti.FiniteEtaleScheme.fiber.signature:
TauCeti.FiniteEtaleScheme.fiber.{u} {S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω]
  [IsSepClosed Ω] (x : AlgebraicGeometry.Spec ↧Ω ⟶ S) :
  CategoryTheory.Functor (TauCeti.FiniteEtaleScheme S) FintypeCat
TauCeti.FiniteEtaleScheme.fiber.doc:
The geometric fibre functor at a geometric point `x : Spec Ω ⟶ S`, for `Ω` separably
closed: a finite étale `S`-scheme `X` goes to the finite set classifying `X ×_S Spec Ω`.

TauCeti.FiniteEtaleScheme.exists_isColim.doc:
Every monomorphism `i : X ⟶ Y` of finite étale schemes over `S` is the inclusion of a direct
summand: there is a finite étale `Z` over `S` with a morphism `u : Z ⟶ Y` exhibiting `Y` as the
coproduct of `X` and `Z`. Here `Z` is the open complement of the image of `i`.

TauCeti.FiniteEtaleScheme.epi_iff_surjec.doc:
A morphism of finite étale schemes is an epimorphism if and only if its underlying morphism
of schemes is surjective.

TauCeti.FiniteCoveringSpace.profiniteCom.doc:
**The profinite completion of `π₁(X, x₀)` is the automorphism group of the finite-cover fibre
functor.**

TauCeti.FiberInclusionPathFiber.loopHomo.signature:
TauCeti.FiberInclusionPathFiber.loopHomotopyEquiv.{u, v} {E : Type u} {B : Type v}
  [TopologicalSpace E] [TopologicalSpace B] {p : C(E, B)} (e₀ : E)

TauCeti.FiberInclusionPathFiber.loopHomo.doc:
**The homotopy fibre of the fibre inclusion is the loop space of the base.** For a Hurewicz
fibration `p`, the space of paths in `E` from the fibre through `e₀` to `e₀` is homotopy
equivalent to the loop space `Ω B (p e₀)`, by composing the paths with `p`.

TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.spaXAdicSpaceCon.signature:
TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.spaXAdicSpaceCongr.{v} {p : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {R : Type v}
  [CommRing R] {ϖ ϖ' : R} [TopologicalSpace (WittVector p R)] [CharP R p] [PerfectRing R p]
  [IsTopologicalRing (WittVector p R)] (P : TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition (WittVector p R))
  (hI : IsAdic (Ideal.span {↑p, (WittVector.teichmuller p) ϖ}))
  (hI' : IsAdic (Ideal.span {↑p, (WittVector.teichmuller p) ϖ'}))
  (h : TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.spaY p ϖ = TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.spaY p ϖ')
  (hY : (TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.spaYPresheaf P ϖ).IsSheaf) :
  TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.spaXAdicSpace P hI hY ≅ TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.spaXAdicSpace P hI' ⋯
TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.spaXAdicSpaceCon.doc:
**The adic Fargues–Fontaine curves `𝒳 = 𝒴 / φ^ℤ` for two pseudouniformisers are isomorphic.**
If `ϖ` and `ϖ'` define the same subset `𝒴` of `Spa(𝕎 R, 𝕎 R)`, as they do when they generate ideals
with the same radical (`spaY_eq_of_radical_eq`), and `𝒪_𝒴` is a sheaf, then the isomorphism
`spaXPreAdicSpaceCongr` of pre-adic spaces is an isomorphism in the full subcategory `(Adic)`. It is
the isomorphism induced by `spaYAdicSpaceCongr` on the quotients by Frobenius
(`quotientAdicHom_comp_spaXAdicSpaceCongr_hom`), and on points it is the homeomorphism
`spaXCongr` of orbit spaces (`spaXPreAdicSpaceCongr_hom_base`). When `R` is perfect of
characteristic `p` and is the ring of integers of a valuation `v` on a field, and `0 < v(ϖ) < 1`,
`𝒪_𝒴` is a sheaf by `isSheaf_spaYPresheaf`.

TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.quotientMap_imag.signature:
TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.quotientMap_image_window_mem_affinoidOpens.{u, u_1} {p : ℕ}
  [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {O : Type u} [CommRing O] {ϖ : O} {q q' : ℚ≥0} {K : Type u_1} [Field K]
  [Algebra O K] {v : Valuation K NNReal} [CharP O p] [PerfectRing O p] (hv : v.Integers O)
  (hϖ : ϖ ≠ 0) (hϖ' : v ((algebraMap O K) ϖ) < 1) [TopologicalSpace (WittVector p O)]
  [IsTopologicalRing (WittVector p O)] {hI : IsAdic (Ideal.span {↑p, (WittVector.teichmuller p) ϖ})}
  {P : TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition (WittVector p O)}
  (hY : (TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.spaYPresheaf P ϖ).IsSheaf) (hq : q ≠ 0) (hqq' : q ≤ q')
  (hW :
    ∀ (k : ℤ),
      k ≠ 0 →
        Disjoint
          (⇑(TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.frobeniusHomeomorph hI ^ k) ⁻¹'
            Subtype.val ⁻¹'
              {v |
                v ∈ TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.spaY p ϖ ∧
                  TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.IsRadiusLowerBound p ϖ q v ∧
                    TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.IsRadiusUpperBound p ϖ q' v})
          (Subtype.val ⁻¹'
            {v |
              v ∈ TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.spaY p ϖ ∧
                TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.IsRadiusLowerBound p ϖ q v ∧
                  TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.IsRadiusUpperBound p ϖ q' v})) :
  {
      carrier :=
        TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.quotientMap hI ''
          Subtype.val ⁻¹'
            {v |
              v ∈ TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.spaY p ϖ ∧
                TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.IsRadiusLowerBound p ϖ q v ∧
                  TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.IsRadiusUpperBound p ϖ q' v},

    (TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.spaXPreAdicSpace P hI hY).affinoidOpens
TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.quotientMap_imag.doc:
**The image in `𝒳` of a wandering window is an open affinoid subspace.** Let `O` be the ring of
integers of `v`, perfect of characteristic `p`, with pseudouniformiser `ϖ`, and suppose `𝒪_𝒴` is a
sheaf. If `0 < q ≤ q'` and the window `W = {v ∈ 𝒴 : q ≤ κ(v) ≤ q'}` meets none of its nontrivial
integer Frobenius translates, then `𝒳` restricted to `q(W)` is affinoid: it is isomorphic to
`Spa(B^I, B^{I,+})` for the interval `I = [v(ϖ) ^ (1 / q), v(ϖ) ^ (1 / q')]`, through the window
chart `spaXWindowChart`.

TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.isSheaf_spaYPres.doc:
**`𝒪_𝒴` is a sheaf**: let `R` be the ring of integers of a valuation `v` on a field `K`,
perfect of characteristic `p`, and `ϖ ∈ R` with `0 < v(ϖ) < 1`; for `R = 𝒪_F` this is the
Fargues–Fontaine space `𝒴 ⊆ Spa(A_inf, A_inf)`. Then the structure presheaf `𝒪_𝒴` is a sheaf, so
`𝒴` and `𝒳 = 𝒴 / φ^ℤ` are adic spaces (`isAdic_spaYPreAdicSpace_iff`, `isAdic_spaXPreAdicSpace`).
The window `W_n = {p ^ (-n) ≤ κ ≤ p ^ n}` is `Spa(B^I, B^{I,+})` for
`I = [v(ϖ) ^ (p ^ n), v(ϖ) ^ (p ^ (-n))]` (`TauCeti.FarguesFontaine.windowPreAdicSpaceIso`), and
this pair is sheafy because `B^I` is strongly noetherian (Kedlaya's Theorem 4.10), so `𝒪_𝒴` is
sheafy on each window (`isSheafy_spaYPreAdicSpace_restrict`), and hence a sheaf
(`isSheaf_spaYPresheaf_of_isSheafy_restrict`).

TauCeti.F4ShortRoot.groupScheme_hom_ext_.doc:
**Two morphisms out of the short-root type-`F₄` carrier agree as soon as they agree on its
eight numbered root subgroups.** This drops the weight-torus hypothesis of
`TauCeti.F4ShortRoot.groupScheme_hom_ext`, which root generation of the carrier makes
redundant.

TauCeti.F4ShortRoot.PrimeField.specialIs.doc: Squaring the special endomorphism gives the prime-field Frobenius on all carrier points.

TauCeti.Excellence.RegularAlgebraMap.signature:
TauCeti.Excellence.RegularAlgebraMap.{u, v} (R : Type u) (B : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing B]
  [Algebra R B] : Prop
TauCeti.Excellence.RegularAlgebraMap.doc:
An `R`-algebra `B` is a *regular algebra*, or `R → B` is a *regular ring map*, if `B` is flat
over `R` and for every prime `p` of `R` the fibre `κ(p) ⊗[R] B` is geometrically regular over the
residue field `κ(p)` (Stacks, Definition 15.42.1).

TauCeti.Excellence.GeometricallyRegular.signature:
TauCeti.Excellence.GeometricallyRegular.{u, v} (k : Type u) (B : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing B]
  [Algebra k B] : Prop
TauCeti.Excellence.GeometricallyRegular.doc:
An algebra `B` over a field `k` is *geometrically regular* if `B` is Noetherian and
`L ⊗[k] B` is a regular ring for every finite purely inseparable field extension `L / k`
(Stacks, Definition 10.166.2, in the form of Lemma 10.166.1). The extensions `L` range over the
universe of `k`; `GeometricallyRegular.isRegularRing_tensorProduct'` removes that restriction.

TauCeti.ExactStructure.IsResolving.resol.signature:
TauCeti.ExactStructure.IsResolving.resolutionEquiv.{w, v, u} {C : Type u}
  [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Preadditive C]
  [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroObject C] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasBinaryBiproducts C]
  (E : TauCeti.ExactStructure C) (P : CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty C) [E.IsResolving P]

  TauCeti.ExactK0 (E.resolvingSubcategory P) ≃+ TauCeti.ExactK0 E
TauCeti.ExactStructure.IsResolving.resol.doc:
**The resolution theorem.** For a resolving property `P` of an exact category, the inclusion
of the full subcategory on `P` induces an isomorphism of exact Grothendieck groups. Its inverse
sends the class of an object to the alternating class of any finite `P`-resolution of it, by
`TauCeti.ExactStructure.IsResolving.resolutionEquiv_symm_of`.

TauCeti.ExactStructure.IsFrobenius.stabl.signature:
TauCeti.ExactStructure.IsFrobenius.stableIsTriangulated.{v, u} {C : Type u}
  [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Preadditive C]
  [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroObject C] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasBinaryBiproducts C]

  CategoryTheory.IsTriangulated E.ProjectiveStableCategory
TauCeti.ExactStructure.IsFrobenius.stabl.doc:
**Happel's theorem.** The stable category of a Frobenius exact category, with the shift
generated by stable suspension and the triangles generated by conflations, is triangulated.

TauCeti.EulerProductData.hasProd_eulerFa.signature:
TauCeti.EulerProductData.hasProd_eulerFactor_convolution.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K]
  [NumberField K] (D E : TauCeti.EulerProductData K) {s : ℂ}
  (hD : Summable (TauCeti.idealTerm K D.toIdealArithmeticFunction s))
  (hE : Summable (TauCeti.idealTerm K E.toIdealArithmeticFunction s)) :
  HasProd (fun P => (D.convolution E).eulerFactor P s)
    (LSeries (⇑((TauCeti.normCoeff K) D.toIdealArithmeticFunction)) s *
      LSeries (⇑((TauCeti.normCoeff K) E.toIdealArithmeticFunction)) s)
TauCeti.EulerProductData.hasProd_eulerFa.doc:
The Euler factors of a convolution have an unrestricted product equal to the product of
the original norm-regrouped Dirichlet series, whenever both ideal-indexed series converge
absolutely.

TauCeti.EulerProductData.hasProd_eulerFa.signature:
TauCeti.EulerProductData.hasProd_eulerFactor.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [NumberField K]
  (D : TauCeti.EulerProductData K) {s : ℂ}
  (hs : Summable (TauCeti.idealTerm K D.toIdealArithmeticFunction s)) :
  HasProd (fun P => D.eulerFactor P s)
    (LSeries (⇑((TauCeti.normCoeff K) D.toIdealArithmeticFunction)) s)
TauCeti.EulerProductData.hasProd_eulerFa.doc:
**The analytic Euler product.** If the ideal-indexed Dirichlet series of `D` converges
absolutely at `s`, then its local Euler factors have an unrestricted
infinite product over the height-one primes, and that product is the `LSeries` of the norm
coefficients of `D`.

The hypothesis is absolute convergence of the *ideal-indexed* series, not of the regrouped one:
regrouping can only improve convergence, and the finite partial products of the local factors are
sums over ideals, not over norms.

TauCeti.EulerProductData.convolution.signature:
TauCeti.EulerProductData.convolution.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [NumberField K]
  (D E : TauCeti.EulerProductData K) : TauCeti.EulerProductData K
TauCeti.EulerProductData.convolution.doc:
Convolve two ideal coefficient systems. This operation multiplies local series and is
distinct from the pointwise multiplication instance on `EulerProductData`.

TauCeti.DynkinType.rootLatticeIsometryCh.signature:
TauCeti.DynkinType.rootLatticeIsometryCheckerboard (n : ℕ) (hn : 4 ≤ n)
  (ht : (TauCeti.DynkinType.D n).IsSimplyLaced) :
  ((TauCeti.DynkinType.D n).rootLattice ht).Isometry (TauCeti.IntegralLattice.checkerboardLattice n)
TauCeti.DynkinType.rootLatticeIsometryCh.doc:
**The root lattice of type `Dₙ` is the checkerboard lattice.**  For `4 ≤ n`, the isometry
sends the `i`-th simple root to the `i`-th Bourbaki simple root of the Conway--Sloane coordinate
model `{x ∈ ℤⁿ | ∑ xᵢ even}`; both bases have Gram matrix `CartanMatrix.D n`.

TauCeti.DynkinType.rootLattice.signature:
TauCeti.DynkinType.rootLattice (t : TauCeti.DynkinType) (ht : t.IsSimplyLaced) :
  TauCeti.IntegralLattice (Fin t.rank → ℚ)
TauCeti.DynkinType.rootLattice.doc:
**The positive root lattice of a simply-laced Dynkin type** `t`: the integral lattice on
`Fin t.rank → ℚ` whose Gram matrix in the standard basis is the Cartan matrix `t.cartanMatrix`.
The standard coordinate vectors are the simple roots, in Bourbaki numbering.

TauCeti.DyadicCyclotomicEight.map_restri.doc:
Lower numbering fails to commute with this restriction: the image at depth three is
the whole quadratic Galois group, but the quadratic lower group at depth three is trivial.

TauCeti.DualGraph.sum_arithmeticGenus_cu.signature:
TauCeti.DualGraph.sum_arithmeticGenus_cutComponent_add_card.{u, v} {ι : Type v}
  (G : TauCeti.DualGraph ι) (S : Finset G.Edge) :
  ∑ x, (G.cutComponent S x).arithmeticGenus + S.card + 1 =
    G.arithmeticGenus + Fintype.card (G.smoothing Sᶜ).Vertex
TauCeti.DualGraph.sum_arithmeticGenus_cu.doc:
**Genus of a partial normalization.** The sum of the arithmetic genera of its connected
pieces, plus the number of cut nodes plus one, equals the original genus plus the number of
pieces. This includes separating, nonseparating and simultaneous cuts, without subtraction.

TauCeti.DualGraph.exists_reflTransGen_st.signature:
TauCeti.DualGraph.exists_reflTransGen_stabilizationStep_isStable.{u, v} {ι : Type v}

  ∃ H, Relation.ReflTransGen TauCeti.DualGraph.StabilizationStep G H ∧ H.IsStable
TauCeti.DualGraph.exists_reflTransGen_st.doc:
**Stabilization terminates.** In the stable range `2g - 2 + n > 0`, iterating stabilization
steps from any graph reaches a stable graph, of the same arithmetic genus by
`TauCeti.DualGraph.arithmeticGenus_eq_of_reflTransGen`. Termination holds because every step
removes a vertex.

TauCeti.DualGraph.arithmeticGenus_smooth.signature:
TauCeti.DualGraph.arithmeticGenus_smoothing.{u, v} {ι : Type v} (G : TauCeti.DualGraph ι)
  (S : Finset G.Edge) : (G.smoothing S).arithmeticGenus = G.arithmeticGenus
TauCeti.DualGraph.arithmeticGenus_smooth.doc:
**Smoothing preserves the arithmetic genus.** The first Betti number lost by smoothing the
nodes in `S` reappears in the genera of the smoothed components.

TauCeti.Divisor.sectionRing.signature:

The **section ring** `⨁ₙ L(nD)` of a divisor `D`: the `k`-subalgebra of `F[X]` of polynomials
`∑ fₙ Xⁿ` with `fₙ ∈ L(nD)` for every `n`.

It is an abbreviation for `TauCeti.coeffSubalgebra` of the family `n ↦ L(nD)`, so that the
grading and its API apply to it directly.

TauCeti.Diffeology.instDiffeologicalSpac.signature:
TauCeti.Diffeology.instDiffeologicalSpaceQuotient.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} [DiffeologicalSpace X]
  (s : Setoid X) : DiffeologicalSpace (Quotient s)
TauCeti.Diffeology.instDiffeologicalSpac.doc: The quotient diffeology on a quotient type: the diffeology coinduced by the projection.

TauCeti.DescentDatum.descended.doc:
The scheme descended from a descent datum `D` on an affine morphism `X ⟶ S'`: the relative
spectrum over `S` of the functions on `X` whose pullbacks along the action and along the second
projection `S' ×_S X ⟶ X` agree.

TauCeti.DerivationExtension.innerEquiv.{u, v, u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] {A : Type u} [Ring A]

TauCeti.DerivationExtension.innerEquiv.doc:
Changing a derivation by an inner derivation does not change its self-extension: when
`δ' = δ + ad b`, the map `(u, v) ↦ (u + b • v, v)` is an isomorphism `E_δ(M) ≃ E_δ'(M)`.

TauCeti.DerivationExtension.signature:
TauCeti.DerivationExtension.{u, v, u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] {A : Type u} [Ring A]
  [Algebra R A] (δ : ↥(TauCeti.derivationLieAlgebra R A)) (M : Type v) : Type v
TauCeti.DerivationExtension.doc:
The **self-extension** `E_δ(M)` of a module `M` attached to a derivation `δ`: pairs `(u, v)`
of elements of `M`, on which `a` acts by `a • (u, v) = (a • u + δ a • v, a • v)`. The first
coordinate carries the submodule `M` and the second the quotient `M`.

TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.weak_regularity.signature:
TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.weak_regularity_frieze_kannan.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω) [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ]

TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.weak_regularity.doc:
**Frieze--Kannan weak regularity.** Every graphon has a measurable block-average step graphon
within `ε` in cut norm, on a partition with at most `4 ^ ⌈1 / ε²⌉` parts.

TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.tendsto_cutDist.doc:
**Cut-distance convergence is convergence of all homomorphism densities**, for graphons on
arbitrary, possibly different, probability carriers, indexed by any type and taken along any
filter: `δ□(Wᵢ, W) → 0` if and only if `t(F, Wᵢ) → t(F, W)` for every finite simple graph `F`.
Sequences are the case of `atTop` on `ℕ`.

TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.lovasz_szegedy_.signature:

    TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.IsIsoInvariant f ∧

        TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.IsNormalized f ∧ TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.IsReflectionPositive f
TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.lovasz_szegedy_.doc:
**The Lovász–Szegedy characterization of homomorphism densities.** A graph parameter is the
homomorphism density of a graphon on an atomless standard Borel carrier `(Ω, μ)`, such as the unit
interval, if and only if it is isomorphism invariant, multiplicative, normalized and reflection
positive.

TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.isDissociated_i.doc:
**Dissociated relational laws of graphs are graphon sampling laws.** An exchangeable relational
law of the language of graphs whose marginals are concentrated on simple graphs is dissociated
exactly when it is the relational law of the sampling law of a graphon, which may be taken on any
atomless standard Borel carrier `(Ω, μ)`, such as the unit interval.

TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.exists_graphon_.doc:
**Every convergent graph sequence has a limit graphon** (Lovász--Szegedy), on every atomless
standard Borel carrier `(Ω, μ)`, such as the unit interval. A sequence of finite graphs on nonempty
vertex sets converges in the cut distance of step graphons to some graphon on `(Ω, μ)` if and only
if every finite homomorphism density `t(F, Gₙ)` is a Cauchy, hence convergent, sequence.

TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.cutDist_triangle.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {Ω₁ : Type u_1} {Ω₂ : Type u_2}

    TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.cutDist U W + TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.cutDist W X
TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.cutDist_triangl.doc:
The coupling-primary graphon cut distance satisfies the triangle inequality on arbitrary
probability carriers.

TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.cutDist.signature:
TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.cutDist.{u_1, u_2} {Ω₁ : Type u_1} {Ω₂ : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace Ω₁]

TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.cutDist.doc:
The **cut distance** of two graphons: the infimum, over couplings of their carriers, of the cut
norm of the overlaid difference.

The two graphons may live on different probability spaces, and no standard Borel or atomless
hypothesis is imposed on either.

TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.InfiniteExchang.doc:
**Exchangeable laws on infinite graphs are the exchangeable relational laws of the language of
graphs on `ℕ` concentrated on simple graphs**, that is, on symmetric irreflexive configurations.
The inverse pulls the law back along the encoding.

**Every exchangeable law on infinite graphs is a graphon mixture, for exactly one mixing
measure.** The integral form of the Diaconis–Janson correspondence: the law is the bind of a
unique probability measure on graphon space against the joint sampling laws.

TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.GraphonSpace.in.signature:
TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.GraphonSpace.instCompactSpace.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω]

  [MeasureTheory.NullSingletonClass μ] : CompactSpace (TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.GraphonSpace Ω μ)
TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.GraphonSpace.in.doc:
**Lovász--Szegedy compactness over atomless standard Borel carriers.** The cut-distance
quotient of graphons on a standard Borel space with an atomless probability measure is a compact
metric space, being isometric to `GraphonSpaceI`.

TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.Graphon.unitInt.signature:
TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.Graphon.unitIntervalRepr.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ]

TauCeti.DenseGraphLimits.Graphon.unitInt.doc:
A graphon on the unit interval at cut distance zero from `W`, for `W` on an arbitrary
probability carrier.

The representative is an arbitrary choice; `cutDist_unitIntervalRepr_left` and
`cutDist_unitIntervalRepr_right` show that no cut distance depends on it.

TauCeti.DenseCompactification.isLimitCom.doc: The common refinement is the binary product in the category of dense compactifications.

TauCeti.DenseCompactification.signature: TauCeti.DenseCompactification.{u} {X S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ S) : Type (u + 1)
TauCeti.DenseCompactification.doc: The full subcategory of compactifications with scheme-theoretically dense interior.

TauCeti.Dagger.washnitzerAlgebra.toTate.doc:
The inclusion of the Monsky–Washnitzer algebra into the unit-radius Tate algebra `R{X/1}`,
through which `W` carries the Gauss norm.

TauCeti.Dagger.washnitzerAlgebra.substEq.doc:
**Isomorphisms of Monsky–Washnitzer algebras from inverse substitutions.** If two families of
unit-ball polynomials without constant term are inverse to each other under substitution, the
substitutions are mutually inverse `R`-algebra isomorphisms `R⟨X⟩† ≃ R⟨Y⟩†`.

TauCeti.Dagger.washnitzerAlgebra.isUnit_.doc:
An overconvergent series is a unit of the Tate algebra iff it is a unit of the
Monsky–Washnitzer algebra: the inverse of an overconvergent series is overconvergent.

TauCeti.Dagger.washnitzerAlgebra.exists_.signature:
TauCeti.Dagger.washnitzerAlgebra.exists_triangularEquiv_isDistinguished_isUnit.{u_1, u_3}

            ↑(MvPowerSeries.restrictedOptionEquiv

TauCeti.Dagger.washnitzerAlgebra.exists_.doc:
**Distinguishing automorphisms of Monsky–Washnitzer algebras.** Over a complete
nonarchimedean field `K`, every nonzero overconvergent series `f` in the variables `Option σ`,
for finite `σ`, is carried by a triangular automorphism `Y ↦ Y`, `Xᵢ ↦ Xᵢ + Y ^ α i` of
`K⟨X, Y⟩†` to a series which, as a restricted series in the variable `Y = none` over the Tate
algebra in the variables `σ`, is distinguished of some degree `s` at radius `1` with a unit
coefficient in degree `s`.

TauCeti.Dagger.washnitzerAlgebra.signature:
TauCeti.Dagger.washnitzerAlgebra.{u_1, u_2} (σ : Type u_1) (R : Type u_2) [NormedCommRing R]
  [IsUltrametricDist R] : Subalgebra R (MvPowerSeries σ R)
TauCeti.Dagger.washnitzerAlgebra.doc:
The **Monsky–Washnitzer algebra** `R⟨X⟩†` of overconvergent power series: the series
restricted at some constant radius `ρ > 1`.

TauCeti.Dagger.primitive_mem_washnitzerA.doc:
**Primitives of overconvergent series are overconvergent.** Over an ultrametric normed field
of characteristic zero, the termwise primitive with respect to `Xᵢ` of an overconvergent series is
overconvergent. See `MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted.primitive` for the radius-by-radius version.

TauCeti.Dagger.isUnit_washnitzerAlgebra_.signature:
TauCeti.Dagger.isUnit_washnitzerAlgebra_iff.{u_1, u_2} {σ : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} [NormedField K]
  [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K] (f : ↥(TauCeti.Dagger.washnitzerAlgebra σ K)) :
  IsUnit f ↔
    MvPowerSeries.constantCoeff ↑f ≠ 0 ∧
      ∀ (t : σ →₀ ℕ), t ≠ 0 → ‖(MvPowerSeries.coeff t) ↑f‖ < ‖MvPowerSeries.constantCoeff ↑f‖
TauCeti.Dagger.isUnit_washnitzerAlgebra_.doc:
**Units of the Monsky–Washnitzer algebra.** Over a complete ultrametric normed field, an
overconvergent series is a unit of `W` iff its constant coefficient is nonzero and strictly
dominates the norm of every other coefficient.

TauCeti.Dagger.exists_isDistinguished_is.signature:
TauCeti.Dagger.exists_isDistinguished_isUnit_of_isDistinguished_one.{u_1, u_3} {σ : Type u_1}
  {K : Type u_3} [NormedField K] [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K]
  {g : ↥(TauCeti.Dagger.washnitzerAlgebra (Option σ) K)} {s : ℕ}
  (hg :
    TauCeti.PowerSeries.IsDistinguished 1 s
      ↑(MvPowerSeries.restrictedOptionEquiv
          ((TauCeti.Dagger.washnitzerAlgebra.toTate (Option σ) K) g)))
  (hu :
    IsUnit
      ((PowerSeries.coeff s)
        ↑(MvPowerSeries.restrictedOptionEquiv
            ((TauCeti.Dagger.washnitzerAlgebra.toTate (Option σ) K) g))))
  {ρ₀ : ℝ} (hρ₀ : 1 < ρ₀) :
  ∃ ρ,
    ∃ (x : Fact (0 < ρ)),
      ∃ r,
        1 < ρ ∧
          ρ ≤ r ∧
            r ≤ ρ₀ ∧

                ∃ G,
                  (∀ (m : ℕ),

                    TauCeti.PowerSeries.IsDistinguished r s G ∧ IsUnit ((PowerSeries.coeff s) G)
TauCeti.Dagger.exists_isDistinguished_is.doc:
**Radius selection for distinguished overconvergent series.** Let `g` be an overconvergent
series in the variables `Option σ` which, as a series in `Y = X none` over the Tate algebra in the
variables `σ`, is distinguished of degree `s` at radius `1` with a unit coefficient `g_s`. Then for
every `ρ₀ > 1` there are radii `1 < ρ ≤ r ≤ ρ₀` such that `g` is restricted at `r`, and its
coefficient slices `gₘ`, which are restricted at `ρ`, form a series `G = ∑ₘ gₘ Yᵐ` over the
series restricted at `ρ` that is distinguished of degree `s` at radius `r`, with `g_s` a unit.

This is the radius selection behind Weierstrass division by `g` inside the Monsky–Washnitzer
algebra. A single common radius `ρ = r > 1` does not suffice in general.

The **cone** of a closed degree-zero morphism `u : P ⟶ Q` of twisted objects: the twisted
object `(Q ⊕ P⟦1⟧, δ)` whose twisting matrix has the twists of `Q` and `P⟦1⟧` on the diagonal
and the morphism `P⟦1⟧ ⟶ P ⟶ Q` underlying `u` in the block from `P⟦1⟧` to `Q`.

A **twisted object** of a differential graded category: an object `obj` with a degree-one
endomorphism `twist` satisfying the Maurer–Cartan equation `d δ = dgComp δ δ`, which in Keller's
order is `d δ + δ ∘ δ = 0`.  The twisted objects form a differential graded category whose Hom
complexes carry the twisted differential; see `TauCeti.DGTwistedObject.homComplexData`.

**The homotopy category of curved right modules is triangulated**, with the shift by one given
by the cohomological shift.

TauCeti.CurvedDGRightModuleCat.absolutel.doc:
The **absolutely acyclic** curved right modules: the smallest thick triangulated subcategory
of the curved homotopy category containing all totalizations of short exact sequences.

trivial coefficients.

one-dimensional.** Here `L` is a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field
of characteristic zero whose adjoint module is irreducible and whose Killing form is
nondegenerate, for instance a simple Lie algebra; the residue class of the Killing form spans.

The residue central extension of a perfect Lie algebra over a field is perfect if and
only if its form is nonzero. No finite-dimensionality or characteristic assumption is needed.

TauCeti.CoveringSpace.monodromyEquivalen.doc:
**The classification of covering spaces by fundamental-groupoid actions.** Over a
path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected base, monodromy is an
equivalence from covering spaces to functors from the fundamental groupoid to types.

TauCeti.CoveringSpace.mk.doc:
Construct a covering space over `X` from a covering map `p`. The definition is `@[expose]`d
so that its total space is `E` and its projection is `p` by `rfl` in downstream modules.

TauCeti.CoveringSpace.autFiberFunctorMul.doc:
**The fundamental group of `X` at `x₀` is the automorphism group of the fibre functor over
`x₀`.**

A loop class is sent to the natural automorphism acting on every fibre by monodromy; that this is
a bijection onto all natural automorphisms is Tannaka duality for `π₁(X, x₀)`-sets, transported
along the classification of covering spaces by `π₁(X, x₀)`-sets.

TauCeti.CoveringSpace.doc:
The category of covering spaces over `X`. Its objects are covering maps to `X`, and its
morphisms are continuous maps commuting with the projections to `X`.

cotangent bundle by a one-form `α` preserves the canonical symplectic form exactly when `α` is
closed.

TauCeti.CotangentBundle.mpullback_liouvi.doc:
**The Liouville form is tautological.** Pulling it back along the smooth section of the
cotangent bundle defined by a smooth one-form `α` gives back `α`.

TauCeti.CotangentBundle.isSymplectic_sym.doc: The canonical symplectic form of the cotangent bundle is closed and nondegenerate.

TauCeti.CotangentBundle.isLiouvilleDomai.doc:
**The unit codisc bundle is a Liouville domain.** For a compact smooth Riemannian manifold
`M` without boundary, the unit codisc bundle `D*M` is a Liouville domain in `T*M` for the
canonical symplectic form `ω = -dλ`, with primitive `-λ`: its Liouville field, the radial field
`p ∂_p`, points strictly outwards along the unit cosphere bundle, the level `‖p‖ = 1` of the norm
of covectors.

TauCeti.CotangentBundle.inChartAt_symple.doc:
**Chart formula for the canonical symplectic form.** In every preferred chart of the cotangent
bundle, the canonical symplectic form is the linear form
`TauCeti.strongDualCotangentSymplecticForm`, `ω((δq, δp), (δq', δp')) = δp'(δq) - δp(δq')`.

preferred chart at `z₁` sends `(q, p)` to `(φ q, p ∘ (dφ_q)⁻¹)`, where `φ` is the change of base
charts; `(dφ_q)⁻¹` is the derivative of the inverse change of charts at `φ q`.

TauCeti.CotangentBundle.doc:
The cotangent bundle of a manifold `M` modelled on `I`: the total space of the bundle whose
fibre at `x` is the space of continuous linear functionals on `TangentSpace I x`. It is a manifold
modelled on `I.prod 𝓘(𝕜, E →L[𝕜] 𝕜)`.

the curve over the window minus that of its cap is `crossingAngle γ t₀ / 2π`.  Beyond the
standing continuity, tangent, and radius hypotheses -- which already give equal endpoint radii
and endpoint matching -- the only extra input is the principal value of `(z - s)⁻¹` along the
generally asymmetric exit-time interval.

**The real bounded-integrand formula, allowing crossings** (Hungerbühler–Wasem Prop 2.3).
For a closed piecewise-`C¹` immersion `γ` on `[[a, b]]` that avoids `s` at the basepoint `a`
(`hsa`, so also at `b` by closedness — every other crossing of `s`, if any, is automatically
interior to `[[a, b]]`) and is `C^{1,1}` on each side of any such crossing (`derivWithin γ`
Lipschitz on a one-sided closed piece ending or starting there, `hγ_lip` — the two sides need not
agree, so a crossing may coincide with a breakpoint of the immersion) — in particular satisfied
vacuously if `γ` never meets `s` — the generalized winding number `n_s(γ)` is a real number equal
to its ordinary (non-principal-value) integral:

`n_s(γ) = (1 / 2π) ∫_a^b (x ẏ - y ẋ) / (x² + y²) dt`, `x + i y = γ - s`.

The two sides of a crossing need not agree: `hγ_lip` allows the crossing to coincide with a
breakpoint of the piecewise-`C¹` immersion (a corner), matching Hungerbühler–Wasem's own proof of
Prop 2.3, which handles that case via the same one-sided splitting (arXiv:1808.00997, p. 9).
Orientation-generic, like `windingNumber` and `intervalIntegral` themselves: no `a ≤ b` is
needed.

principal-value normalization of the index integral for a curve `γ : ℝ → ℂ` on `[a, b]` and any
point `z₀`. See `windingNumber_eq_integral_of_avoidance` for its reduction to the ordinary index
integral; as a `limUnder`-based value it is junk when the principal value does not exist.

that is `C²` at the crossing parameter `t₀` with nonvanishing velocity there, the real winding

`g z / (z - z₀) ^ (k + 1)` has residue the Taylor coefficient `iteratedDeriv k g z₀ / k !` at `z₀`:

of index `k` sits at order `−1`. This is the residue behind Cauchy's integral formula for the
`k`-th derivative; the constant case is `TauCeti.Contour.residue_const_div_sub_pow`.

TauCeti.Contour.isExactOn_of_starConvex.doc:
**Holomorphic functions have primitives on a star-shaped set.** If `U` is open and
star-shaped about some point, then every function holomorphic on `U` has a primitive on `U`.

TauCeti.Contour.homologyCauchyTheorem.doc:
**The homology Cauchy theorem** (roadmap `homologyCauchyTheorem`, Layer 3). Let `γ` be a
closed piecewise-`C¹` curve on `[[a, b]]`, null-homologous in an open set `Ω` containing it, and
let `f` be holomorphic on `Ω`. Then the contour integral of `f` along `γ` vanishes:
`∫ t in a..b, deriv γ t • f (γ t) = 0`.

Dixon's argument: the piecewise-`C¹` regularity supplies continuity, differentiability off the
finitely many breakpoints, and interval-integrability of `deriv γ` (the `IsPiecewiseC1On` API);
the compact curve image cannot exhaust the open `Ω`, giving a base point `w₀ ∈ Ω` off the curve
(`exists_mem_off_curve`); and `homologyCauchyTheorem_of_point_off_curve` — vanishing of the glued
Dixon function by Liouville, then the Cauchy integral formula at `w₀` — concludes.

TauCeti.Contour.firstExitTimeLeft.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [Sub E] [Norm E] (γ : ℝ → E) (t₀ δ : ℝ)
  (s : E) (ε : ℝ) : ℝ

**First exit time at radius `ε` (left side)**: the `sSup` of the times `t ∈ [t₀ - δ, t₀]`
with `ε ≤ ‖γ t - s‖` — the latest outside-the-ball time before `t₀`, which is the first exit
when moving left from `t₀`. The junk value is `sSup ∅` when the defining set is empty.

closed disc `C(c, R)` (`R > 0`) and every point of nonzero meromorphic order lies in a finite set
`S` inside the open disc, then `∮_{C(c,R)} f = 2πi · ∑_{s ∈ S} residue f s`. Since residues at
non-poles vanish, `classicalResidueTheorem_circle_of_meromorphicOrderAt_neg` proves the same
conclusion asking only the poles (points of negative order) to lie in `S`.

**Cauchy's integral formula for the `k`-th derivative, homology form.** Let `f` be holomorphic
on an open `U`, let `γ` be a closed piecewise-`C¹` curve in `U` that is null-homologous there, and
let `z ∈ U` lie off the curve. Then for every `k`,

`∫ t in a..b, γ' t • (f (γ t) / (γ t − z) ^ (k + 1)) = 2πi · n_z(γ) · f⁽ᵏ⁾(z) / k !`,

the `k`-th Taylor coefficient of `f` at `z` weighted by the generalized winding number of `γ` about
`z`. Only the residue at `z` contributes: the residue theorem for a null-homologous cycle applied
to the Cauchy kernel `w ↦ f w / (w − z) ^ (k + 1)`, whose only possible singularity in `U` is at
`z`, leaves the single residue `iteratedDeriv k f z / k !`.

`IsPwC1ImmersionOn.finite_crossings`.

Let `U` be open, `S ⊆ U` finite, `f` holomorphic on `U ∖ S` and meromorphic at each point of
`S`, and let `C` be a contour cycle in `U`, **null-homologous** in `U`, whose curves are
piecewise-`C¹` immersions rooted off `S` and satisfy conditions (A′) and (B). Then the Cauchy
principal value of `f` along `C` exists and

`PV ∮_C f = 2πi · ∑_{s ∈ S} n_s(C) · Res_s f`,

each singularity weighted by the **generalized** winding number of `C` about it. The
singularities are allowed to lie **on** `C`, where those weights are in general not integers and
the contour integral only exists as a principal value.

Null-homology is asked of the cycle only, never of its generators, so the theorem covers the
combinations that make cycles worth having: a difference of two homologous loops around a hole of
`U`, neither of them null-homologous, is null-homologous. Its `S = ∅` case is the homology Cauchy
theorem for cycles
(`TauCeti.Contour.Cycle.homologyCauchyTheorem`), and its one-generator case is the single-curve
theorem `TauCeti.Contour.hungerbuhlerWasem_residueTheorem`. Where the trace of `C` avoids `S`
the principal value is an ordinary integral and the statement is the classical residue theorem
for cycles (`TauCeti.Contour.Cycle.classicalResidueTheorem_nullHomologous`), which needs neither
immersions nor the conditions.

  (TauCeti.Contour.Cycle.integral f) C = 0
TauCeti.Contour.Cycle.homologyCauchyTheo.doc:
**The homology Cauchy theorem for contour cycles.** Let `C` be a finite formal integer
combination of closed piecewise-`C¹` curves whose trace lies in an open set `U`. If `C` is
null-homologous in `U` and `f` is holomorphic on `U`, with values in any complex normed space,
then the contour integral of `f` over the whole cycle vanishes.

The null-homology assumption is imposed only on `C`, not on each supported curve, so the theorem
includes cancellations between different generators.

TauCeti.Contour.Cycle.classicalResidueTheorem_nullHomologous {f : ℂ → ℂ} {S : Finset ℂ} {U : Set ℂ}
  (hU : IsOpen U) (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (U \ ↑S)) (hmero : ∀ s ∈ S, s ∈ U → MeromorphicAt f s)
  {C : TauCeti.Contour.Cycle} (hCU : C.IsIn U) (hoff : ∀ s ∈ S, s ∉ C.trace)
  (hnull : C.IsNullHomologous U) :
  (TauCeti.Contour.Cycle.integral f) C =
    2 * ↑Real.pi * Complex.I *
      ∑ s ∈ S, (TauCeti.Contour.Cycle.windingNumber s) C * TauCeti.Contour.residue f s
TauCeti.Contour.Cycle.classicalResidueTh.doc:
**The classical residue theorem for a null-homologous contour cycle.** Let `U` be open, `S` a
finite set, `f` differentiable on `U ∖ S` and meromorphic at each point of `S` lying in `U`, and let
`C` be a contour cycle in `U`, **null-homologous** in `U`, whose trace **avoids** `S`. Then

`Cycle.integral f C = 2πi · ∑_{s ∈ S} n_s(C) · Res_s f`,

each pole weighted by the generalized winding number of `C` about it.

Null-homology is asked of the cycle only, never of its generators, so the theorem covers the
combinations that make cycles worth having: a difference of two loops around a hole of `U`, neither
of them null-homologous, is. Points of `S` outside `U` are harmless rather than excluded, their
winding number vanishing by null-homology, and `S` may list regular points of `f`, whose residues
are `0`.

Its `S = ∅` case is the homology Cauchy theorem for cycles
(`TauCeti.Contour.Cycle.homologyCauchyTheorem`), and its one-generator case is the single-curve
theorem `TauCeti.Contour.classicalResidueTheorem_nullHomologous`.

TauCeti.Colored3Graph.IsTopRegularOverPo.doc:
**Slicing lemma.** If `H` is `(δ, r)`-top-regular over `P` at a positive rank, then it is
`(max (2δ) (δ / α), r)`-top-regular over every polyad `P'` whose pair graphs lie in those of `P`
and whose support is at least an `α`-fraction of the support of `P`. The polyad `P'` may live
over a different skeleton, so this is how top regularity passes to a refined lower skeleton.

`H` is `(δ, r)`-top-regular over the polyad `P` when, for every top color `c` and every
family of `r` subpolyads of `P` whose union support has at least `δ` times the size of the
support of `P`, the relative density of `c` on that union is within `δ` of the relative density
of `c` over `P`. Members of the family may repeat, so this tests unions of at most `r`
subpolyads.

invariant map.

TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.invMap (K : Type) [Field K] [ValuativeRel K] [TopologicalSpace K]
  [IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K] : TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.Br K ≃+ AddCircle 1
TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.invMap.doc:
**The local invariant** `inv_K : Br K ≃+ ℚ/ℤ` of a nonarchimedean local field `K`, normalized
by arithmetic Frobenius: on the classes inflated from an unramified extension `E/K` inside `Kˢ`
it is the invariant `TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.unramifiedInv K E` of the layer
(`invMap_relBrInfl`).

TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.hilbertProductF.signature:
TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.hilbertProductFormula {K : Type} [Field K] [NumberField K] (a b : Kˣ) :
  ∑ v ∈ TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.finiteHilbertSupport K a b,
        TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.finiteHilbertInvariantAt K v a b +
      ∑ w, TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.infiniteHilbertInvariantAt K w a b =
    0
TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.hilbertProductF.doc:
**Hilbert reciprocity.** For `a, b ∈ Kˣ`, the Hilbert invariants of `a` and `b` at all the
finite and infinite places of the number field `K` sum to zero.

TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.globalInv_injec.signature:
TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.globalInv_injective {K : Type} [Field K] [NumberField K]
  (L : TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.NormalLayer (TauCeti.AbsoluteGaloisGroup K)) :
  Function.Injective ⇑(TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.globalInv K L)
TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.globalInv_injec.doc:
**The global invariant is injective**, because the idele-class `H¹` vanishes and the sum of
the local invariants vanishes only on the classes that die in the idele classes.

TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.globalInv.signature:
TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.globalInv (K : Type) [Field K] [NumberField K]
  (L : TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.NormalLayer (TauCeti.AbsoluteGaloisGroup K)) :
  ↑(L.H (TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.globalFormation K) 2) →+ AddCircle 1
TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.globalInv.doc:
**The global invariant** `H²(Gal(L/F), C_L) → ℚ/ℤ` of a finite normal layer `L/F` inside
`Kˢ`: the invariant of a class is the sum of the local invariants of a lift to the ideles of its
inflation to some refinement of the layer. By `globalInv_eq` it does not depend on the refinement
or on the lift, and `globalInv_unique` characterizes it by the equations `globalInv_ideleToClassH2`
and `globalInv_infl`.

TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.globalClassForm.doc:
**The global class formation**: the idele-class formation of `K` is a class formation, whose
invariant on a layer is the global invariant (`globalClassFormation_inv`).

TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.globalArtinEqui.signature:
TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.globalArtinEquiv.{u_1} (K : Type) [Field K] [NumberField K] (L : Type u_1)
  [Field L] [NumberField L] [Algebra K L] [IsGalois K L] (ι : L →ₐ[K] SeparableClosure K) :
  Additive
      (NumberField.IdeleClassGroup (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K ⧸
        (↑(TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.ideleClassNormMap K L)).range) ≃+
    Additive (Abelianization Gal(L/K))
TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.globalArtinEqui.doc:
**Finite global reciprocity** `C_K / N_{L/K}(C_L) ≃ Gal(L/K)^ab` for a finite Galois extension
`L/K` of number fields, embedded in the separable closure of `K` by `ι`: the abstract Artin
reciprocity isomorphism `ClassFormation.artinEquiv` of the global class formation on the layer of
`L`, read through `globalLayerNormQuotientEquiv K L` and `layerGalEquiv ι`. It does not depend on
`ι` (`globalArtinEquiv_eq_of_iota`).

TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.exists_abelianL.signature:
TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.exists_abelianLayer_globalNormSubgroup_eq_of_pow_mem {K : Type} [Field K]
  [NumberField K] {p : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] [HasEnoughRootsOfUnity K p]
  {N : Subgroup (NumberField.IdeleClassGroup (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K)} (hN : IsOpen ↑N)
  (hpow : ∀ (c : NumberField.IdeleClassGroup (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K), c ^ p ∈ N) :
  ∃ V, V.IsAbelianClassFieldLayer ∧ TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.globalNormSubgroup K V = N
TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.exists_abelianL.doc:
**The Kummer case of global existence** (Milne VII, Lemma 9.3). Let `K` be a number field
containing the `p`-th roots of unity for a prime `p`. Every open subgroup of the idele class group
`C_K` containing the `p`-th powers is the norm subgroup of a finite abelian extension of `K`.

TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.card_ideleClass.signature:
TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.card_ideleClassNormQuotient.{u_1} (K : Type) [Field K] [NumberField K]
  (L : Type u_1) [Field L] [NumberField L] [Algebra K L] [IsAbelianGalois K L] :
  Nat.card
      (NumberField.IdeleClassGroup (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K ⧸
        (↑(TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.ideleClassNormMap K L)).range) =
    Module.finrank K L
TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.card_ideleClass.doc:
**The norm index theorem**: for a finite abelian extension `L/K` of number fields,
`[C_K : N_{L/K}(C_L)] = [L : K]`, since finite global reciprocity identifies the norm quotient with
`Gal(L/K)^ab`, which is `Gal(L/K)` itself.

TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.ClassFormation..signature:
TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.ClassFormation.tateIso {G : Type} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
  [IsTopologicalGroup G] [CompactSpace G] [TotallyDisconnectedSpace G]
  {F : TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.Formation G} (cf : TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.ClassFormation F)
  (L : TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.NormalLayer G) (r : ℤ) : ↑(L.TrivialTateH r) ≃+ ↑(L.TateH F (r + 2))
TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.ClassFormation..doc:
**Tate's theorem for a class formation**, in every integer degree: the generic theorem applied
to the fundamental class, with the three hypotheses discharged by the three individually named
consequences of the axioms. This is Artin–Tate's Main Theorem (Chapter XIV §4, Theorem 1).

TauCeti.CkHolderSpace.signature:
TauCeti.CkHolderSpace.{u, v} (k : ℕ) (α : NNReal) (E : Type u) (F : Type v) [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] : Type (max u v)
TauCeti.CkHolderSpace.doc:
The space of bounded `C^k` maps whose iterated Fréchet derivatives through order `k` are
bounded and whose `k`-th iterated derivative is globally `α`-Hölder. Its norm is

`∑_{i ≤ k} ‖D^i f‖_∞ + [D^k f]_α`.

TauCeti.CircleSobolev.norm_mul_le.signature:
TauCeti.CircleSobolev.norm_mul_le.{u_4} {s : ℝ} {A : Type u_4} [NormedRing A] [NormedAlgebra ℂ A]
  [CompleteSpace A] [hs : Fact (1 / 2 < s)] (a b : TauCeti.CircleSobolev s A) :
  ‖a * b‖ ≤ 2 ^ (s + 1) * √(∑' (n : ℤ), TauCeti.CircleSobolev.weight (-(2 * s)) n) * ‖a‖ * ‖b‖

TauCeti.CircleSobolev.mulFourierSeriesEq.signature:
TauCeti.CircleSobolev.mulFourierSeriesEquiv.{u_1} {s : ℝ} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℂ E] [CompleteSpace E] {T : ℝ} [Fact (0 < T)] (f : AddCircle T → ℂ)
  (hf : ContDiff ℝ ↑⊤ fun x => f ↑x) (hf₀ : ∀ (x : AddCircle T), f x ≠ 0) :
  TauCeti.CircleSobolev s E ≃L[ℂ] TauCeti.CircleSobolev s E
TauCeti.CircleSobolev.mulFourierSeriesEq.doc:
For a smooth function `f` on the circle that vanishes nowhere, multiplication by `f` as a
continuous linear automorphism of `H^s`, for every real `s`; its inverse is multiplication by
`f⁻¹`.

TauCeti.CircleSobolev.isUnit_iff_forall_.signature:
TauCeti.CircleSobolev.isUnit_iff_forall_isUnit.{u_1} {s : ℝ} {A : Type u_1} [NormedCommRing A]
  [NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] [hs : Fact (1 / 2 < s)] (T : ℝ) [Fact (0 < T)]
  {a : TauCeti.CircleSobolev s A} :
  IsUnit a ↔ ∀ (x : AddCircle T), IsUnit (((TauCeti.CircleSobolev.toContinuousMap T ⋯) a) x)
TauCeti.CircleSobolev.isUnit_iff_forall_.doc:
**Wiener's lemma for `H^s(A)`, `s > 1/2`.** An element of `H^s(A)` is a unit if and only if
its continuous representative takes invertible values at every point of the circle.

TauCeti.CircleSobolev.analyticOnNhd_nemy.signature:
TauCeti.CircleSobolev.analyticOnNhd_nemytskii {s : ℝ} (T : ℝ) [hT : Fact (0 < T)]
  [hs : Fact (1 / 2 < s)] {F : ℂ → ℂ} {U : Set ℂ} (hU : IsOpen U) (hF : DifferentiableOn ℂ F U) :
  AnalyticOnNhd ℂ (TauCeti.CircleSobolev.nemytskii F)
    {u | ∀ (x : AddCircle T), ((TauCeti.CircleSobolev.toContinuousMap T ⋯) u) x ∈ U}
TauCeti.CircleSobolev.analyticOnNhd_nemy.doc:
**The holomorphic Nemytskii map is holomorphic.** If `F` is holomorphic on an open set `U`,
then `u ↦ nemytskii F u` is analytic on the open subset of `H^s`, `s > 1/2`, of elements with
values in `U` (`isOpen_setOf_forall_toContinuousMap_mem`).

TauCeti.CStarAction.isKMSState_iff_of_de.signature:
TauCeti.CStarAction.isKMSState_iff_of_dense.{u_1} {A : Type u_1} [NonUnitalCStarAlgebra A]
  {α : TauCeti.CStarAction (Multiplicative ℝ) A} {β : ℝ} [PartialOrder A] [StarOrderedRing A]
  {ω : A →P[ℂ] ℂ} {s : Set A} (hs : Dense s) (hinv : IsInvariant (fun t a => (α t) a) s)
  (hentire : ∀ b ∈ s, α.IsEntireAnalytic b) :
  α.IsKMSState β ω ↔
    ‖ω.toContinuousLinearMap‖ = 1 ∧
      ∀ a ∈ s, ∀ b ∈ s, ω (a * α.entireExtension b (↑β * Complex.I)) = ω (b * a)
TauCeti.CStarAction.isKMSState_iff_of_de.doc:
**Dense analytic KMS criterion.** A state is β-KMS if and only if the analytic KMS
identity holds for pairs in a norm-dense invariant set of entire analytic elements.
In particular, the set can be a norm-dense invariant star subalgebra.

TauCeti.CStarAction.isCompact_kmsStates.signature:
TauCeti.CStarAction.isCompact_kmsStates.{u_2} {B : Type u_2} [CStarAlgebra B] [PartialOrder B]
  [StarOrderedRing B] {α : TauCeti.CStarAction (Multiplicative ℝ) B} {β : ℝ} :
  IsCompact (α.kmsStates β)
TauCeti.CStarAction.isCompact_kmsStates.doc: **Weak-* compactness of `K_β`.** For unital `B`, the set of β-KMS states is weak-* compact.

TauCeti.CStarAction.entireAnalytic.signature:
TauCeti.CStarAction.entireAnalytic.{u_1} {A : Type u_1} [NonUnitalCStarAlgebra A]
  (α : TauCeti.CStarAction (Multiplicative ℝ) A) : NonUnitalStarSubalgebra ℂ A
TauCeti.CStarAction.entireAnalytic.doc: The entire analytic elements of a real action, as a nonunital star subalgebra.

TauCeti.CStarAction.dense_entireAnalytic.signature:
TauCeti.CStarAction.dense_entireAnalytic.{u_1} {A : Type u_1} [NonUnitalCStarAlgebra A]
  (α : TauCeti.CStarAction (Multiplicative ℝ) A) : Dense ↑α.entireAnalytic
TauCeti.CStarAction.dense_entireAnalytic.doc:
**Density of entire analytic elements.** The entire analytic elements of a point-norm
continuous real action are dense, since every element is a limit of its Gaussian smearings.

TauCeti.CStarAction.convex_kmsStates.signature:
TauCeti.CStarAction.convex_kmsStates.{u_1} {A : Type u_1} [NonUnitalCStarAlgebra A] [PartialOrder A]
  [StarOrderedRing A] {α : TauCeti.CStarAction (Multiplicative ℝ) A} {β : ℝ} :
  Convex ℝ (α.kmsStates β)
TauCeti.CStarAction.convex_kmsStates.doc: **Convexity of `K_β`.** Convex combinations of β-KMS states are β-KMS states.

TauCeti.CStarAction.IsKMSState.of_tendst.doc:
**Pointwise limits of KMS states.** If β-KMS states converge pointwise to a positive
functional of norm one, then the limit is a β-KMS state.

TauCeti.CStarAction.IsKMSState.apply_act.signature:
TauCeti.CStarAction.IsKMSState.apply_action.{u_1} {A : Type u_1} [NonUnitalCStarAlgebra A]
  {α : TauCeti.CStarAction (Multiplicative ℝ) A} {β : ℝ} [PartialOrder A] [StarOrderedRing A]
  {ω : A →P[ℂ] ℂ} (hω : α.IsKMSState β ω) (hβ : β ≠ 0) (t : Multiplicative ℝ) (a : A) :
  ω ((α t) a) = ω a
TauCeti.CStarAction.IsKMSState.apply_act.doc:
**KMS states are invariant.** For `β ≠ 0`, every β-KMS state `ω` is invariant under the
dynamics: `ω (α_t(a)) = ω a`. At `β = 0` the KMS states are the tracial states, which need not
be invariant.

TauCeti.CStarAction.CovariantRepresentat.signature:
TauCeti.CStarAction.CovariantRepresentation.regular.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {G : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2}
  {H : Type u_3} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [NonUnitalCStarAlgebra A] [NormedAddCommGroup H]
  [InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H] [IsTopologicalGroup G] [MeasurableSpace G]
  [BorelSpace G] (α : TauCeti.CStarAction G A) (ρ : A →⋆ₙₐ[ℂ] H →L[ℂ] H)
  (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure G) [μ.IsMulLeftInvariant] [μ.InnerRegularCompactLTTop]
  [MeasureTheory.IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ] : α.CovariantRepresentation ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp H 2 μ)
TauCeti.CStarAction.CovariantRepresentat.doc:
The regular covariant representation on `L²(G, H)` induced by a representation `ρ` of `A` on
`H`: `a` acts by `ξ ↦ (r ↦ ρ (α_{r⁻¹}(a)) (ξ r))` and `s` by left translation
`ξ ↦ (r ↦ ξ (s⁻¹ r))`.

TauCeti.CStarAction.CovariantRepresentat.signature:
TauCeti.CStarAction.CovariantRepresentation.norm_integratedOperator_le.{u_1, u_2, u_3}
  {G : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2} {H : Type u_3} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [MeasurableSpace G]
  [OpensMeasurableSpace G] [NonUnitalCStarAlgebra A] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [CompleteSpace H] {α : TauCeti.CStarAction G A} (P : α.CovariantRepresentation H)
  (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure G) [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ]
  (f : CompactlySupportedContinuousMap G A) : ‖(P.integratedOperator μ) f‖ ≤ ∫ (g : G), ‖f g‖ ∂μ
TauCeti.CStarAction.CovariantRepresentat.doc: The integrated form is bounded by the coefficient function's L¹ norm.

TauCeti.CStarAction.CovariantRepresentat.signature:
TauCeti.CStarAction.CovariantRepresentation.integratedOperator_convolution.{u_1, u_2, u_3}
  {G : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2} {H : Type u_3} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [MeasurableSpace G]
  [OpensMeasurableSpace G] [NonUnitalCStarAlgebra A] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
