      (((Rep.resFunctor φ).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.down ℕ)).map
        (TauCeti.universalGSpaceChainComplexToStandardComplex k H)) =
    CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (TauCeti.universalGSpaceChainComplexToStandardComplex k G)
      φ.standardComplexMap
MonoidHom.universalGSpaceChainComplexToS.doc:
**The join-to-standard comparison is natural in the group.** Relabelling simplices before
forgetting their indices agrees with first forgetting indices and then relabelling the tuples.
This is an equality of chain maps in `Rep k G`, with target actions restricted along `φ`.

MonoidHom.restrictScalarsMonoidalLeftAct.doc:
The left action of a monoid `H` on `ModuleCat A` by twisting along a homomorphism
`a : H →* RingAut A`: an element `h` acts by restricting scalars along `(a h)⁻¹`. The associator
`(g * h) ⊙ₗ M ≅ g ⊙ₗ h ⊙ₗ M` and the unitor `1 ⊙ₗ M ≅ M` are the comparison isomorphisms
of restriction of scalars, with identity underlying linear maps.

ModuleCat.exists_isAlmostSplit_X₃_eq_iff.signature:
ModuleCat.exists_isAlmostSplit_X₃_eq_iff.{u, v, w} (k : Type u) {A : Type v} [Field k] [Ring A]
  [Algebra k A] [FiniteDimensional k A] (M : ModuleCat A) [Module.Finite A ↑M] :
  (∃ S, S.X₃ = M ∧ S.IsAlmostSplit) ↔ CategoryTheory.Indecomposable M ∧ ¬CategoryTheory.Projective M
ModuleCat.exists_isAlmostSplit_X₃_eq_iff.doc:
Over a finite-dimensional algebra, a finitely generated module ends an almost-split sequence
of `A`-modules exactly when it is indecomposable and non-projective.

Module.SatisfiesSerreS.signature:
Module.SatisfiesSerreS.{u, v} (n : ℕ) (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M]
  [_root_.Module R M] : Prop
Module.SatisfiesSerreS.doc:
An `R`-module `M` satisfies *Serre's condition* `(S_n)` if for every prime `p` of `R` the depth
of `M_p` over `R_p` is at least `min (n, dim Supp M_p)`. This is meant for finite modules over a
Noetherian ring. Since the zero module has depth `⊤`, primes outside the support impose nothing.
Stacks, Definition 10.157.1 (031P).

Module.End.mk_trace_homogeneousSubmodule.signature:
Module.End.mk_trace_homogeneousSubmoduleMapₛₗ_mul_reverse_charpoly_of_pow_eq_one.{u_1, u_2}
  {K : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [_root_.Module K V]
  [FiniteDimensional K V] {f : Module.End K V} {n : ℕ} (hn : ↑n ≠ 0) (hf : f ^ n = 1) :
  (PowerSeries.mk fun m =>
        (LinearMap.trace K ↥(TauCeti.SymmetricAlgebra.homogeneousSubmodule K V m))
          (TauCeti.SymmetricAlgebra.homogeneousSubmoduleMapₛₗ f m)) *
      ↑(LinearMap.charpoly f).reverse =
    1
Module.End.mk_trace_homogeneousSubmodule.doc:
**The graded trace formula for an endomorphism of finite order** of a finite-dimensional
vector space over an arbitrary field: if `f ^ n = 1` with `n` nonzero in `K`, then
`(∑ₘ tr(f | Symᵐ V) tᵐ) * det(1 - t f) = 1`.

No eigenvalue of `f` need lie in `K`: over an algebraic closure `f` becomes diagonalizable, and
both factors commute with scalar extension
(`Module.End.trace_homogeneousSubmoduleMapₛₗ_baseChange`, `LinearMap.charpoly_baseChange`).

Module.Basis.existsUnique_ringHom_nonneg.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [Fintype ι]

Module.Basis.existsUnique_ringHom_nonneg.doc:
**The Frobenius–Perron character.** A ring with a finite nonempty `ℤ`-basis with nonnegative
structure constants, such that every basis element occurs in `b j * ∑ i, b i` for every `j`, has
exactly one character to `ℝ` which is nonnegative on the basis.

MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto.signature:
MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_haarAddCircle_iff.{u_1} {T : ℝ} [Fact (0 < T)]
  {ι : Type u_1} {L : Filter ι} {μs : ι → MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure (AddCircle T)} :

MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto.doc:
Circle probability measures tend weakly to Haar probability exactly when every nonzero
integer Fourier moment tends to zero.

MeasureTheory.Measure.markovChainLaw_map.signature:
MeasureTheory.Measure.markovChainLaw_map_eval.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace α]

MeasureTheory.Measure.markovChainLaw_map.doc:
**The time-`n` marginal of the chain**: the state at time `n` has law `(κ ^ n) ∘ₘ ν`, the
initial law propagated by the `n`-step transition kernel. This holds for every initial measure
`ν`.

MeasureTheory.Measure.eq_markovChainLaw.signature:
MeasureTheory.Measure.eq_markovChainLaw.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace α]
  (ν : MeasureTheory.Measure α) (κ : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel α α)
  [ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel κ] [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure ν]

MeasureTheory.Measure.eq_markovChainLaw.doc:
**Uniqueness of the path law.** For a finite initial measure `ν`, a measure on path space whose
time-zero marginal is `ν` and whose prefix laws satisfy the Markov recursion of
`markovChainLaw_map_prefix_succ_eq_compProd` is the path law `markovChainLaw ν κ`.

MeasureTheory.Measure.deFinettiBarycente.signature:
MeasureTheory.Measure.deFinettiBarycenter.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace α]
  (π : MeasureTheory.Measure (MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure α)) : MeasureTheory.Measure (ℕ → α)
MeasureTheory.Measure.deFinettiBarycente.doc:
The **de Finetti barycenter** of a mixing law `π` on `ProbabilityMeasure α`: the measure
`∫ P^{⊗ℕ} dπ(P)` on `ℕ → α` mixing the countable powers against `π`. For `π` a probability
measure this is the law of a sequence drawn i.i.d. from a `π`-random probability measure.

MeasureTheory.Measure.addHaar_image_mulV.signature:
MeasureTheory.Measure.addHaar_image_mulVec.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] [ValuativeRel K]

MeasureTheory.Measure.addHaar_image_mulV.doc:
**The scaling law for Haar measure.** If the determinant of a square matrix `A` over `𝒪[K]`
is associated to `ϖ ^ k` for a uniformizer `ϖ`, then for every regular additive Haar measure `μ`
on `ι → K` and every set `s`, `μ (A '' s) = q ^ (-k) * μ s`, where `q = Nat.card 𝓀[K]`. This is
the nonarchimedean analogue of `MeasureTheory.Measure.addHaar_image_linearMap`.

MeasureTheory.Lp.prodMulL.doc:
**The tensor as a bounded bilinear map.** `prodMulL F G = prodMul F G`, packaged so that
either operand can be fixed: `prodMulL F` fixes the left factor, `prodMulL.flip G` the right.
Its operator norm is at most `1`; neither measure needs to be s-finite.

MeasureTheory.Lp.norm_add_rpow_add_norm_.doc:
**Clarkson's inequality.** For `2 ≤ p < ∞` and `f g : Lp E p μ`, where the norm of `E`
satisfies the parallelogram identity,
`‖f + g‖ ^ p + ‖f - g‖ ^ p ≤ 2 ^ (p - 1) * (‖f‖ ^ p + ‖g‖ ^ p)`.

MeasureTheory.Integrable.exists_convexOn.signature:
MeasureTheory.Integrable.exists_convexOn_superlinear_integrable.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1}
  {F : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace α] [NormedAddCommGroup F] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure α}

MeasureTheory.Integrable.exists_convexOn.doc:
**De la Vallée Poussin's lemma.** Every integrable function `f` remains integrable after
composing its norm with some convex, monotone function `Φ` with `Φ 0 = 0` that grows
superlinearly, `Φ t / t → ∞`.

Matrix.minorGcd_mul_subspaceHeight_ker_m.signature:
Matrix.minorGcd_mul_subspaceHeight_ker_mulVecLin.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [LinearOrder ι]

Matrix.minorGcd_mul_subspaceHeight_ker_m.doc:
**The height of the kernel of an integer matrix.** The greatest common divisor of the maximal
minors of an integer matrix `A`, times the absolute Euclidean height of the space of rational
solutions of `A y = 0`, is `√det (A Aᵀ)`. If the rows are linearly dependent, both sides
vanish.

Matrix.minorGcd.signature:
Matrix.minorGcd.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {R : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [DecidableEq m] [Fintype n] [CommRing R] [NormalizedGCDMonoid R] (A : Matrix m n R) : R
Matrix.minorGcd.doc:
The gcd of the maximal minors of `A`: the normalized gcd of the determinants
`det (A.submatrix id e)` over all embeddings `e : m ↪ n`. It is `0` exactly when every maximal
minor vanishes, in particular when `n` has fewer elements than `m`.

Matrix.exists_linearIndependent_mulVec_e.signature:
Matrix.exists_linearIndependent_mulVec_eq_zero_prod_norm_le.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] {p : ℕ}
  {A : Matrix (Fin p) ι ℤ} (hA : LinearIndependent ℚ (A.map Int.cast).row) :
  ∃ x,
    LinearIndependent ℤ x ∧
      (∀ (l : Fin (Fintype.card ι - p)), A.mulVec (x l) = 0) ∧

matrix with linearly independent rows, and let `g` be the greatest common divisor of its maximal
minors. Then `A x = 0` has `n - p` linearly independent integral solutions `x l`, each with
coprime coordinates, whose sup norms `‖x l‖ = max_i |x l i|` satisfy
`∏ l, ‖x l‖ ≤ √det (A Aᵀ) / g`.

Matrix.continuous_mulVec_extension_iff.signature:
Matrix.continuous_mulVec_extension_iff.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {R : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2}

Matrix.continuous_mulVec_extension_iff.doc:
A matrix over the group ring has a unique continuous extension of its action to completed
coordinate modules. Its entries are included coefficientwise in the Novikov ring. No topology
on the group ring is needed to state this uniqueness property.

At a point where `f` is differentiable for the models over `𝕜'`, the derivative of `f` over the
smaller field `𝕜` is its derivative over `𝕜'` with scalars restricted to `𝕜`, both read in the model

LocallyFinite.isSemianalytic_iUnion.signature:
LocallyFinite.isSemianalytic_iUnion.{u_1, u_3} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E]

LocallyFinite.isSemianalytic_iUnion.doc:
**Locally finite unions.** The union of a locally finite family of semianalytic sets is
semianalytic.

LipschitzWith.lintegral_normDet_fderiv_m.signature:
LipschitzWith.lintegral_normDet_fderiv_mul_eq_lintegral_tsum.{u_1, u_2} {U : Type u_1}

**The weighted area formula with multiplicity.** Integrating the geometric Jacobian
of a Lipschitz map against a nonnegative measurable weight equals the normalized Hausdorff
integral of the sum of the weights over each fiber. The parameter set may be Lebesgue
measurable rather than Borel, and infinite fibers use extended sums.

LinearPMap.isSelfAdjoint_iff_exists_isUn.doc:
**Stone's theorem.** An operator `A` on a complex Hilbert space is self-adjoint if and only if
`i • A` is the complex generator of a unitary C₀-group.

LinearMap.six_mul_apply_eq_of_cyclic_eq_.signature:

      (((T x) w) w) x

antisymmetric in its first and in its last pair of arguments and satisfying the first Bianchi
identity, `6 T(x, y, z, w)` is an explicit combination of values `T(a, b, b, a)`. This recovers
`T` itself only when multiplication by `6` is injective, see `LinearMap.eq_of_cyclic_eq_zero`.

LinearMap.separatingSpace.signature:
LinearMap.separatingSpace.{u_1, u_3, u_4} {R : Type u_1} {E : Type u_3} {F : Type u_4} [Ring R]
  [AddCommGroup E] [_root_.Module R E] [TopologicalSpace E] [IsTopologicalAddGroup E]

  [IsTopologicalAddGroup F] [ContinuousConstSMul R F] (T : E →ₗ[R] F) : Submodule R F
LinearMap.separatingSpace.doc:
The *separating space* of a linear map `T : E →ₗ[R] F` between topological modules: the
vertical fibre over `0` of the closure of the graph of `T`. For first countable spaces it
consists of the limits of `T xₙ` along sequences `xₙ → 0`
(`LinearMap.mem_separatingSpace_iff_exists_seq`).

LinearMap.continuous_iff_separatingSpace.signature:
LinearMap.continuous_iff_separatingSpace_eq_bot.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2}
  {F : Type u_3} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
  [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F] (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F) [CompleteSpace E] [CompleteSpace F] :
  Continuous ⇑T ↔ T.separatingSpace = ⊥
LinearMap.continuous_iff_separatingSpace.doc:
A linear map between Banach spaces is continuous if and only if its separating space is
trivial.

LinearMap.BilinForm.sesqComplexification.signature:
LinearMap.BilinForm.sesqComplexification.{u_1} {V : Type u_1} [AddCommGroup V] [_root_.Module ℝ V]
  (B : LinearMap.BilinForm ℝ V) : TensorProduct ℝ ℂ V →ₗ⋆[ℂ] TensorProduct ℝ ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ
LinearMap.BilinForm.sesqComplexification.doc:
**The sesquilinear complexification** of a real bilinear form `B`: the form
`h (x, y) = B_ℂ (conj x, y)` on `ℂ ⊗[ℝ] V`, conjugate-linear in the first argument and linear in
the second, with `h (z ⊗ v, w ⊗ u) = conj z * w * B (v, u)`
(`LinearMap.BilinForm.sesqComplexification_tmul_tmul`). For a Euclidean metric it is the
induced positive Hermitian form on the complexification.

LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.equivalent_if.signature:
LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.equivalent_iff_isSquare_det_mul_det_and_eight_dvd_of_odd.{u_1, u_2}
  {M : Type u_1} {N : Type u_2} [AddCommGroup M] [_root_.Module ℤ_[2] M] [AddCommGroup N]
  [_root_.Module ℤ_[2] N] {B : LinearMap.BilinForm ℤ_[2] M} {C : LinearMap.BilinForm ℤ_[2] N}
  (hB : B.IsSymm) (hC : C.IsSymm) {n : ℕ} (b : Module.Basis (Fin n) ℤ_[2] M)
  (c : Module.Basis (Fin n) ℤ_[2] N) (hBdet : IsUnit ((LinearMap.BilinForm.toMatrix b) B).det)
  (hCdet : IsUnit ((LinearMap.BilinForm.toMatrix c) C).det) (hBodd : ∃ x, IsUnit ((B x) x))
  (hCodd : ∃ y, IsUnit ((C y) y)) {w : M} {w' : N} (hw : B.IsCharacteristic w)
  (hw' : C.IsCharacteristic w') :

LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.equivalent_if.doc:
**Classification of odd unimodular forms over `ℤ_[2]`.** Let `B` and `C` be symmetric forms
over `ℤ_[2]` with unit Gram determinants in bases of the same size, each representing a unit, and
let `w` and `w'` be characteristic vectors for `B` and `C`. Then `B` and `C` are isometric exactly
when the product of their Gram determinants is a square and `B w w ≡ C w' w'` modulo `8`.

The second condition says that the oddities of `B` and `C` agree.

LieSubalgebra.lieChevalleyRestrictionIso.signature:
LieSubalgebra.lieChevalleyRestrictionIso.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} [Field K]
  [CharZero K] [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L] [LieAlgebra.IsKilling K L]

LieSubalgebra.lieChevalleyRestrictionIso.doc:
**Chevalley's restriction theorem.** Restriction of polynomial functions from `L` to `H`,
`TauCeti.lieCartanRestriction H`, is an isomorphism from the invariants `S(L)^L` onto the Weyl
invariants `S(H)^W`.

LieModule.Cohomology.twoCocycle_eq_range.signature:
LieModule.Cohomology.twoCocycle_eq_range_d₁₂.{u, v, w} {K : Type u} {L : Type v} {M : Type w}
  [Field K] [CharZero K] [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra K L] [LieAlgebra.IsKilling K L] [AddCommGroup M]

LieModule.Cohomology.twoCocycle_eq_range.doc:
**Whitehead's second lemma**, as an equality of submodules: the 2-cocycles of a
Lie algebra with nondegenerate Killing form in characteristic zero, with values in a
finite-dimensional module, are exactly the coboundaries.

LieDerivation.IsKilling.exists_eq_inner.signature:
LieDerivation.IsKilling.exists_eq_inner.{u, v, w} {K : Type u} {L : Type v} {M : Type w} [Field K]
  [CharZero K] [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra K L] [LieAlgebra.IsKilling K L] [AddCommGroup M]
  [_root_.Module K M] [LieRingModule L M] [LieModule K L M] [FiniteDimensional K M]
  (D : LieDerivation K L M) : ∃ m, (LieDerivation.inner K L M) m = D
LieDerivation.IsKilling.exists_eq_inner.doc:
**Whitehead's first lemma.** Over a field of characteristic zero, every Lie derivation from a
Lie algebra with nondegenerate Killing form (necessarily finite-dimensional) into a
finite-dimensional module is inner: it is `x ↦ ⁅x, m⁆` for some `m`.

LieAlgebra.LoopAlgebra.toHahnModule.signature:
LieAlgebra.LoopAlgebra.toHahnModule.{u_1, u_2, u_3} (R : Type u_1) (Γ : Type u_2) (L : Type u_3)
  [CommRing R] [AddCommMonoid Γ] [PartialOrder Γ] [IsOrderedCancelAddMonoid Γ] [LieRing L]
  [LieAlgebra R L] : LieAlgebra.loopAlgebra R Γ L →ₗ⁅R⁆ HahnModule Γ R L
LieAlgebra.LoopAlgebra.toHahnModule.doc:
The embedding of polynomial loops into `L`-valued Hahn series, sending `t ^ a ⊗ x` to the
monomial `x t ^ a`.

LieAlgebra.IsCentralizerRegular.signature:
LieAlgebra.IsCentralizerRegular.{u, u_1} (K : Type u_1) {L : Type u} [Field K] [LieRing L]
  [LieAlgebra K L] (x : L) : Prop
LieAlgebra.IsCentralizerRegular.doc:
An element `x` of a Lie algebra is **regular** when its centralizer `ker (ad x)` has minimal
dimension among the centralizers of all elements. The dimension is the cardinal `Module.rank`, so
that an infinite-dimensional centralizer is never smaller than a finite-dimensional one. Over a
field of characteristic zero this is the dimension of the group centralizer `C_G(x)` when the Lie
algebra is that of an affine algebraic group `G`. This differs from Mathlib's
`LieAlgebra.IsRegular`, which asks that the coefficient of index `LieAlgebra.rank` of the
characteristic polynomial of `ad x` be nonzero, and from minimality of the dimension of the Engel
subalgebra, the generalized `0`-eigenspace of `ad x`.

IsSl2Triple.root_apply_eq_zero_or_eq_one.doc:
**The simple root values of a dominant neutral element lie in `{0, 1, 2}`.** If the neutral
element `h` of an `sl₂` triple lies in the Cartan subalgebra `H` and every simple root takes a
natural value at `h`, then each simple root takes the value `0`, `1` or `2` at `h`. These values
label the weighted Dynkin diagram of the triple.

IsSl2Triple.isCompl_range_ad_e_ker_ad_f.signature:
IsSl2Triple.isCompl_range_ad_e_ker_ad_f.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} [Field K]

IsSl2Triple.isCompl_range_ad_e_ker_ad_f.doc:
**The transverse decomposition `L = [L, e] ⊕ ker (ad f)`.** For an `sl₂` triple `(h, e, f)` in a
finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a field of characteristic zero, the range of `ad e` and the
kernel of `ad f` are complementary.

IsSl2Triple.exists_lieEquiv_apply_eq.signature:
IsSl2Triple.exists_lieEquiv_apply_eq.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} [Field K] [CharZero K]

IsSl2Triple.exists_lieEquiv_apply_eq.doc:
**Kostant's conjugacy theorem.** Two `sl₂` triples `(h, e, f)` and `(h', e, f')` with the same
nilpositive element in a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a field of characteristic zero are
conjugate by an automorphism of `L` that fixes `e` and lies in the subgroup
`TauCeti.expAdSubgroup K e` generated by the automorphisms `exp (ad y)` with
`y ∈ ker (ad e) ⊓ [e, L]`.

IsSl2Triple.contractingAction.{u_1, u_2} {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} [Field K] [CharZero K]

IsSl2Triple.contractingAction.doc:
**The contracting action** of `Kˣ` on `L` attached to an `sl₂` triple `(h, e, f)`:
`c` acts by `c ^ 2 • gradingAut c⁻¹`, that is, by `c ^ (2 - j)` on the `j`-eigenspace of `ad h`
(`IsSl2Triple.contractingAction_apply_of_mem`). For an algebraic group with Lie algebra `L` and a
cocharacter `λ` with differential `h` this is `c ↦ c ^ 2 • Ad (λ c⁻¹)`. It fixes `e` and preserves
the Slodowy slice `e + ker (ad f)`, on which it extends to `c = 0`
(`IsSl2Triple.exists_contractingAction_eq`).

IsSelfAdjoint.add_of_isRelativelyBounded.doc:
**The Kato–Rellich theorem.** Let `A` be a self-adjoint partial linear map on a Hilbert space
and `V` a symmetric partial linear map that is relatively bounded with respect to `A` with
constants `a` and `b < 1`, that is `dom A ⊆ dom V` and `‖V x‖ ≤ a * ‖x‖ + b * ‖A x‖` on `dom A`.
Then `A + V`, whose domain is `dom A`, is self-adjoint.

IsQuotientCoveringMap.cwComplexQuotient.doc:
**The orbit space of a free cellular action is a CW complex.** Let `p : E → B` be the quotient
covering map of an action of `G` on the Hausdorff CW complex `E` that carries every open `n`-cell
onto an open `n`-cell, and carries an open cell onto itself only by `1`. Then `B` is a CW complex
whose `n`-cells are the `G`-orbits of `n`-cells of `E`
(`IsQuotientCoveringMap.cellQuotientEquiv`). The characteristic map of an orbit is `p ∘ φ`, for
`φ` the characteristic map of the chosen representative of the orbit
(`IsQuotientCoveringMap.map_cellQuotientEquiv_symm`).

**The Golod–Shafarevich inequality.** A nontrivial finite `p`-group `G`, with the discrete
topology, satisfies `d(G)² < 4 r(G)`, where `d(G)` is its generator rank and
`r(G) = dim_{𝔽_p} H²(G, 𝔽_p)` is its relation rank. Finite generation follows from
`TauCeti.isTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated_of_fg`.

**A complex manifold is a real-analytic manifold.** A complex manifold modelled on
`𝓘(ℂ, E)`, of class `C^m` for some `m ≠ 0` with `E` finite-dimensional, is with the same charts a
real `C^n` manifold modelled on `𝓘(ℝ, E)` for every `n`; for `n = ω` it is real-analytic.

The maximal abelian subgroups of a nontrivial free group are exactly the cyclic subgroups

IsFreeGroup.isCSA.doc: **Free groups are CSA**: every maximal abelian subgroup of a free group is malnormal.

IsCompact.isPolynomiallyConvex_of_forall.doc: Every compact subset of the real locus `ℝⁿ ⊆ ℂⁿ` is polynomially convex.

The root count of a coefficient vector `a : Fin n → K` in a subextension `L`: the number of
roots of the monic polynomial `monicOfCoeff a` lying in `L`, counted with multiplicity.

Int.IsFundamentalDiscr.existsUnique_fins.signature:

**Unique prime-discriminant factorization of a fundamental discriminant.** Every fundamental

**The Hurewicz theorem.** If `πₖ(X, x)` is trivial for every `k < n + 2`, then the Hurewicz
map `πₙ₊₂(X, x) → Hₙ₊₂(X; ℤ)`, `[p] ↦ p_*[Iⁿ⁺²]`, is bijective.

  (h₁ : HomologicalComplex.Acyclic S.X₁) (h₃ : HomologicalComplex.Acyclic S.X₃) {n₁ n₃ : ℤ → ℕ}

  (c₂ : (i : ℤ) → Module.Basis (Fin (n₁ i + n₃ i)) F ↑(S.X₂.X i))
  (hc₁ :

given by the dimensions of the boundaries `Bₖ,ⱼ ⊆ Cₖ,ⱼ`. This also holds when the complexes are
unbounded, both sides being `0`.

  (f : HeckeRing.GL2.Newform N k) (h : TauCeti.Nat.IsExactDivisor Q N) : ℂ
HeckeRing.GL2.Newform.atkinLehnerPseudoE.doc:
**The Atkin–Li pseudo-eigenvalue** `λ_Q(f)` of a newform `f` at an exact divisor `Q` of the
level: the scalar with `𝒲_Q f = λ_Q(f) • g`, where `𝒲_Q` is the slash by the Atkin–Li matrix
`atkinLiMatrix N Q` normalized by `(√Q) ^ (2 - k)` and `g = f.atkinLehnerTransform h` is the
transported newform. Since `g` has first Fourier coefficient `1`, it is the first Fourier
coefficient of `𝒲_Q f`.

HeckeRing.GL2.Newform.L_eulerProduct.signature:
HeckeRing.GL2.Newform.L_eulerProduct {N : ℕ} [NeZero N] {k : ℤ} (f : HeckeRing.GL2.Newform N k)
  (hk : 0 < k) {s : ℂ} (hs : ↑k / 2 + 1 < s.re) :
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun n =>
      ∏ p ∈ n.primesBelow,
        (1 - (PowerSeries.coeff p) (UpperHalfPlane.qExpansion 1 ⇑f.toCuspForm) * ↑p ^ (-s) +
            f.dirichletLift ↑p * ↑p ^ (k - 1) * ↑p ^ (-2 * s))⁻¹)
    Filter.atTop (nhds (ModularForm.L hk f.toCuspForm s))
HeckeRing.GL2.Newform.L_eulerProduct.doc: Finite Euler products converge to Mathlib's `ModularForm.L` for a newform.

HahnModule.instLieRing.doc: Hahn series with coefficients in a Lie ring form a Lie ring under the convolution bracket.

Group.IsPrimitive.signature: Group.IsPrimitive.{u} {G : Type u} [Group G] (x : G) : Prop
Group.IsPrimitive.doc: An element of a group is primitive when it belongs to some free basis of the group.

Graph.isBridge_iff_forall_cycle_notMem.signature:
Graph.isBridge_iff_forall_cycle_notMem.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {G : Graph α β} {e : β}
  (he : e ∈ G.edgeSet) : G.IsBridge e ↔ ∀ ⦃u : α⦄ (p : G.Walk u u), p.IsCycle → e ∉ p.edges
Graph.isBridge_iff_forall_cycle_notMem.doc: An actual edge is a bridge exactly when it lies on no cycle.

Graph.isBridge_iff_componentCount_delete.doc:
**Bridges by component counts.**  With finitely many connected components, an edge is a
bridge exactly when deleting it increases the number of connected components by one.

Graph.Walk.signature: Graph.Walk.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (G : Graph α β) : α → α → Type (max u v)
Graph.Walk.doc:
An edge-labelled walk in a multigraph. Each step records an edge together with its
incidence; a zero-length walk may be based at any ambient point.

Geometry.SimplicialComplex.space_cone_of.doc:
Coning a triangulation of the intrinsic frontier of a compact convex set `C` to a point of the
intrinsic interior of `C` triangulates `C`: every point of `C` is either the apex or lies on a
segment from the apex to a point of the intrinsic frontier.

Geometry.SimplicialComplex.cone.signature:
Geometry.SimplicialComplex.cone.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [Field 𝕜] [LinearOrder 𝕜]
  [IsStrictOrderedRing 𝕜] [AddCommGroup E] [_root_.Module 𝕜 E] [DecidableEq E]
  (K : Geometry.SimplicialComplex 𝕜 E) (p : E) (h : K.IsConeApex p) : Geometry.SimplicialComplex 𝕜 E
Geometry.SimplicialComplex.cone.doc:
The cone `pK` on a simplicial complex `K` with apex `p`. Its faces are the nonempty finite sets
whose vertices other than `p` form a face of `K` or are empty: the faces of `K`, the faces of `K`
with `p` adjoined, and the vertex `{p}`.

Geometry.SimplicialComplex.IsConeApex.signature:
Geometry.SimplicialComplex.IsConeApex.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [Field 𝕜]
  [LinearOrder 𝕜] [AddCommGroup E] [_root_.Module 𝕜 E] (K : Geometry.SimplicialComplex 𝕜 E)
  (p : E) : Prop
Geometry.SimplicialComplex.IsConeApex.doc:
A point `p` is a *cone apex* for a geometric simplicial complex `K` if `p ∉ |K|` and every
segment from `p` to a point `y ∈ |K|` meets `|K|` only at `y`. These are the conditions under
which joining `p` to the faces of `K` gives a simplicial complex, the cone `K.cone p h`.

Function.Involutive.orbitCount_finRotate.signature:
Function.Involutive.orbitCount_finRotate_mul_add_orbitCount_eq_iff {n : ℕ} [NeZero n]
  {σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)} (hinv : Function.Involutive ⇑σ) :
  TauCeti.orbitCount (finRotate n * σ) + TauCeti.orbitCount σ = n + 1 ↔ σ.IsNoncrossingMatching
Function.Involutive.orbitCount_finRotate.doc:
**The boundary-count criterion for noninterleaving.** A chord diagram on a nonempty boundary
circle, with matching an involution `σ` and `m = n - orbitCount σ` bands, has exactly `m + 1`
boundary cycles if and only if no two of its bands interleave.

FreeGroup.isConj_iff_isRotated_reduceCyc.signature:
FreeGroup.isConj_iff_isRotated_reduceCyclically.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [DecidableEq α]
  {x y : FreeGroup α} :
  IsConj x y ↔ FreeGroup.reduceCyclically x.toWord ~r FreeGroup.reduceCyclically y.toWord
FreeGroup.isConj_iff_isRotated_reduceCyc.doc:
**Conjugacy criterion in free groups.** Two elements of a free group are conjugate exactly
when the cyclic reductions of their reduced words are cyclic rotations of each other.

FormalGroup.logIso.signature:
FormalGroup.logIso.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (F : FormalGroup R) [Algebra ℚ R] :
  TauCeti.FormalGroupIso F FormalGroup.𝔾ₐ
FormalGroup.logIso.doc:
The normalized logarithm is a strict isomorphism from `F` to the additive formal group,
with the formal exponential as its inverse.

FormalGroup.height.signature: FormalGroup.height.{u_1} {K : Type u_1} [Field K] (F : FormalGroup K) (p : ℕ) : ℕ∞
FormalGroup.height.doc:
The **height** of a formal group law `F` over a field `K` of characteristic `p`: `⊤` if
multiplication by `p` on `F` is zero, and otherwise the exponent `h` such that the first nonzero
term of `[p]_F(T)` has degree `p ^ h` (see `FormalGroup.height_eq_natCast_iff`).

FormalGroup.exists_order_nsmulSeries_eq_.signature:
FormalGroup.exists_order_nsmulSeries_eq_pow.{u_1} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (F : FormalGroup R)
  [F.IsComm] {p : ℕ} (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hpR : ↑p = 0) (h0 : F.nsmulSeries p ≠ 0) :
  ∃ h, h ≠ 0 ∧ (F.nsmulSeries p).order = ↑(p ^ h)
FormalGroup.exists_order_nsmulSeries_eq_.doc:
**The `p`-series has order a power of `p`** in characteristic `p`: if `p` is a prime with
`p = 0` in `R` and `F` is commutative, then either `[p]_F = 0` or the first nonzero term of
`[p]_F` has degree `p ^ h` for some `h ≥ 1`.

FormalGroup.TopNilpotentPoint.signature:
FormalGroup.TopNilpotentPoint.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (F : FormalGroup R)
  (A : Type u_2) [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] : Type u_2
FormalGroup.TopNilpotentPoint.doc:
The **points of a formal group law `F` in `A`**: the elements of a topological ring `A`
satisfying `PowerSeries.HasEval`, that is, the topologically nilpotent elements. Evaluation of
power series over `R` at these elements converges when `A` is a complete, Hausdorff, linearly
topologised `R`-algebra; under those assumptions they form a group under `x +_F y = F(x, y)`.
This is the analogue for `A` of the power-series carrier `F.Point σ`.

This is a structure rather than a subtype of `A` so that its group law, which depends on `F`, is
not confused with the ring operations of `A`.

FirstOrder.Language.Theoryω.realize_conj.doc:
**A countable theory is one sentence.** A structure satisfies the conjunction of a countable
theory exactly when it is a model of the theory.

FirstOrder.Language.Theoryω.conjunction.signature:
FirstOrder.Language.Theoryω.conjunction.{u, v} {L : FirstOrder.Language} (T : L.Theoryω)
  (hT : Set.Countable T) : L.Sentenceω
FirstOrder.Language.Theoryω.conjunction.doc:
The **conjunction of a countable theory**: its sentences, enumerated into the carrier `ℕ`
along `IndexCoding.ofEncodableWith`, joined by one countable conjunction. Indices that code no
sentence carry `⊤`.

FirstOrder.Language.Theoryω.Model.signature:
FirstOrder.Language.Theoryω.Model.{u, v, w} {L : FirstOrder.Language} (T : L.Theoryω) (M : Type w)
  [L.Structure M] : Prop
FirstOrder.Language.Theoryω.Model.doc:
A structure is a **model** of an `L_{ω₁ω}` theory when it satisfies every sentence of the
theory.

FirstOrder.Language.Theoryω.signature: FirstOrder.Language.Theoryω.{u, v} (L : FirstOrder.Language) : Type (max u v)
FirstOrder.Language.Theoryω.doc: An `L_{ω₁ω}` theory: a set of `L_{ω₁ω}` sentences.

FirstOrder.Language.StrongHomClass.theor.doc: Isomorphic structures are models of the same `L_{ω₁ω}` theories.

FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormulaInf.re.doc:
**Transport a formula along a coding of its carrier**: each `ι`-indexed conjunction or
disjunction becomes the corresponding coded connective at carrier `κ`.

FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormulaInf.fr.signature:
FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormulaInf.freeVarSupport.{u, v, u', uι} {L : FirstOrder.Language}
  {α : Type u'} {ι : Type uι} {n : ℕ} : L.BoundedFormulaInf ι α n → Set α
FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormulaInf.fr.doc:
The **free-variable support** of an infinitary formula: the set of free variables that occur
in one of its atoms. Infinitary connectives take the union over all their branches, so the support
may be infinite.

FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormulaInf.signature:
FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormulaInf.{u, v, u', uι} (L : FirstOrder.Language) (ι : Type uι)
  (α : Type u') : ℕ → Type (max u v u' uι)
FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormulaInf.doc:
An infinitary bounded formula of `L_{∞ω}`, with infinitary conjunctions and disjunctions
branching over the fixed carrier `ι`, free variables indexed by `α`, and `n` additional bound
variables available.

Finset.integerProjection.signature:
Finset.integerProjection {n : ℕ} (P : Finset (MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) ℤ)) :
  Finset (MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ)
Finset.integerProjection.doc:
The Collins projection of a finite family `P` of integer polynomials in the variables
`X 0, …, X n`, computed over `ℤ`: single out the distinguished variable `X 0` and take the Collins
projection of the resulting family of polynomials in `X 0` over `ℤ[X 1, …, X n]`.

Finset.image_map_integerProjection.signature:
Finset.image_map_integerProjection {n : ℕ} [DecidableEq (MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℝ)]
  (P : Finset (MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) ℤ)) :
  Finset.image (⇑(MvPolynomial.map (Int.castRingHom ℝ))) P.integerProjection =
    P.integerFamily.collinsProjection
Finset.image_map_integerProjection.doc:
**The integer projection computes the real projection.** Mapping the integer projection of
`P` to `ℝ` gives the Collins projection of the real family of `P`.

Finset.IsSquarefreeBasis.signature: Finset.IsSquarefreeBasis.{u_1} {D : Type u_1} [CommRing D] (F B : Finset (Polynomial D)) : Prop
Finset.IsSquarefreeBasis.doc:
`B` is a squarefree basis of the finite family `F` of polynomials over `D`: its members
are primitive, squarefree, of positive degree and pairwise relatively prime, and every member
of `F` is a constant times a product of powers of members of `B`.

FDRep.trace_eq_smul.signature:
FDRep.trace_eq_smul.{u, v} {k : Type u} {G : Type v} [Field k] [Group G] {V : FDRep k G}
  (f : V ⟶ V) :
  TauCeti.trace f =
    (LinearMap.trace k ↑V.V) (ModuleCat.Hom.hom f.hom.hom) •
      CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id
        (CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategoryStruct.tensorUnit (FDRep k G))
FDRep.trace_eq_smul.doc:
The categorical trace of an equivariant endomorphism of a finite-dimensional representation
is its linear trace, acting on the trivial representation by scalar multiplication.

Equiv.isSemianalytic_image_iff.signature:
Equiv.isSemianalytic_image_iff.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] {s : Set E} (e : E ≃ F)
  (he : AnalyticOnNhd ℝ (⇑e) Set.univ) (he' : AnalyticOnNhd ℝ (⇑e.symm) Set.univ) :
  TauCeti.IsSemianalytic (⇑e '' s) ↔ TauCeti.IsSemianalytic s
Equiv.isSemianalytic_image_iff.doc:
**Analytic isomorphisms.** For a bijection `e` that is analytic with analytic inverse, the
image `e '' s` is semianalytic if and only if `s` is semianalytic.

Equidecomp.exists_iff_exists_finpartitio.signature:
Equidecomp.exists_iff_exists_finpartition.{u_1, u_2} {X : Type u_1} {G : Type u_2} [Group G]
  [MulAction G X] {A B : Set X} :
  (∃ f, f.source = A ∧ f.target = B) ↔
    ∃ P γ, ((↑P.parts).PairwiseDisjoint fun s => γ s • s) ∧ ⋃ s ∈ P.parts, γ s • s = B
Equidecomp.exists_iff_exists_finpartitio.doc:
**Equidecompositions as partitions.** Two sets `A` and `B` are related by an
equidecomposition exactly when there are a finite partition of `A` and a group element `γ s` for
each part `s`, such that the translates `γ s • s` are pairwise disjoint with union `B`.

Equidecomp.Equipartition.signature: Equidecomp.Equipartition.{u_1, u_2} (X : Type u_1) (G : Type u_2) [SMul G X] : Type (max u_1 u_2)
Equidecomp.Equipartition.doc:
An *equipartition* of `X` for an action of `G`: a finite set of pairs `(Aᵢ, gᵢ)` of a nonempty
source piece `Aᵢ : Set X` and a group element `gᵢ : G`, such that the source pieces `Aᵢ` are
pairwise disjoint and the target pieces `gᵢ • Aᵢ` are pairwise disjoint. When `G` is a group
acting on `X`, moving each `Aᵢ` by `gᵢ` is then an equidecomposition of the union of the `Aᵢ` with
the union of the `gᵢ • Aᵢ` (see `Equidecomp.Equipartition.toEquidecomp`).

DividedPowerAlgebra.isInternal_homogeneo.doc:
The homogeneous pieces of the divided power algebra form an internal direct sum: the sum
map `⨁ d, Γ^d_R(M) → Γ_R(M)` is bijective.

DividedPowerAlgebra.homogeneousLawEquiv.signature:
DividedPowerAlgebra.homogeneousLawEquiv.{u, u_1, u_2} (R : Type u) [CommSemiring R] (M : Type u_1)
  (N : Type u_2) [AddCommMonoid M] [_root_.Module R M] [AddCommMonoid N] [_root_.Module R N]
  (d : ℕ) :
  (↥(DividedPowerAlgebra.homogeneousSubmodule d) →ₗ[R] N) ≃ₗ[R]
    ↥(PolynomialLaw.homogeneousSubmodule R M N d)
DividedPowerAlgebra.homogeneousLawEquiv.doc:
**Roby representability**: composition with the universal law `γ_d` is a linear equivalence
between linear maps `Γ^d_R(M) → N` and homogeneous polynomial laws `M → N` of degree `d`.

DividedPowerAlgebra.gamma.signature:
DividedPowerAlgebra.gamma.{u, u_1} (R : Type u) [CommSemiring R] (M : Type u_1) [AddCommMonoid M]
  [_root_.Module R M] (d : ℕ) : M →ₚₗ[R] ↥(DividedPowerAlgebra.homogeneousSubmodule d)
DividedPowerAlgebra.gamma.doc:
The universal homogeneous polynomial law `γ_d : M → Γ^d_R(M)` of degree `d`. After scalar
extension to a commutative `R`-algebra `S` it sends `∑ⱼ sⱼ ⊗ mⱼ` to
`∑_{∑ⱼ nⱼ = d} (∏ⱼ sⱼ ^ nⱼ) ⊗ ∏ⱼ dp R nⱼ mⱼ` (see `gamma_toFun_sum_tmul`), and its ground value is
`m ↦ dp R d m` (see `ground_gamma_apply`).

DividedPowerAlgebra.baseChangeHomogeneou.signature:
DividedPowerAlgebra.baseChangeHomogeneousEquiv.{u_1, u_2, u_3} (R : Type u_1) [CommSemiring R]
  (M : Type u_2) [AddCommMonoid M] [_root_.Module R M] (S : Type u_3) [CommSemiring S] [Algebra R S]
  (d : ℕ) :
  TensorProduct R S ↥(DividedPowerAlgebra.homogeneousSubmodule d) ≃ₗ[S]
    ↥(DividedPowerAlgebra.homogeneousSubmodule d)
DividedPowerAlgebra.baseChangeHomogeneou.doc:
**Base change of homogeneous divided powers**: for a commutative `R`-algebra `S`, the base
change isomorphism restricts to an `S`-linear isomorphism
`S ⊗[R] Γ^d_R(M) ≃ₗ[S] Γ^d_S(S ⊗[R] M)` taking `1 ⊗ dp R d m` to `dp S d (1 ⊗ m)`
(`baseChangeHomogeneousEquiv_one_tmul_dp`). No flatness is assumed.

DividedPowerAlgebra.baseChangeEquiv.signature:
DividedPowerAlgebra.baseChangeEquiv.{u_1, u_2, u_3} (R : Type u_1) [CommSemiring R] (M : Type u_2)
  [AddCommMonoid M] [_root_.Module R M] (S : Type u_3) [CommSemiring S] [Algebra R S] :
  TensorProduct R S (DividedPowerAlgebra R M) ≃ₐ[S] DividedPowerAlgebra S (TensorProduct R S M)
DividedPowerAlgebra.baseChangeEquiv.doc:
**Base change of divided power algebras**: for a commutative `R`-algebra `S`, the canonical
map `S ⊗[R] Γ_R(M) → Γ_S(S ⊗[R] M)` is an isomorphism of `S`-algebras. No flatness is
assumed.

Distribution.translatePairing_eq_of_line.doc:
**Distributions with vanishing derivatives have locally constant regularizations.** If every
directional derivative of `T` vanishes, then `x ↦ T (ρ (· - x))` is constant on every
preconnected open set of translations for which `ρ (· - x)` is supported in `Ω`.

Distribution.fderiv_translatePairing_app.signature:
Distribution.fderiv_translatePairing_apply.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
  {Ω V : TopologicalSpace.Opens E} [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] (T : Distribution Ω F ⊤)
  (ρ : TestFunction V ℝ ⊤) {x : E} (hx : Set.MapsTo (fun x_1 => x_1 + x) (tsupport ⇑ρ) ↑Ω) (v : E) :
  (fderiv ℝ (T.translatePairing ρ) x) v = (LineDeriv.lineDerivOp v T).translatePairing ρ x
Distribution.fderiv_translatePairing_app.doc:
**The derivative of a regularization.** At every admissible translation, the derivative of
`x ↦ T (ρ (· - x))` in the direction `v` is the regularization of the distributional derivative
`∂_{v} T`.

Distribution.exists_norm_apply_le.signature:
Distribution.exists_norm_apply_le.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] {Ω : TopologicalSpace.Opens E}
  (T : Distribution Ω F ⊤) {K : TopologicalSpace.Compacts E} (hK : ↑K ⊆ ↑Ω) :
  ∃ N C,
    0 ≤ C ∧
      ∀ (φ : TestFunction Ω ℝ ⊤),
        tsupport ⇑φ ⊆ ↑K →
          ∀ (M : ℝ), 0 ≤ M → (∀ i ≤ N, ∀ (x : E), ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ i (⇑φ) x‖ ≤ M) → ‖T φ‖ ≤ C * M
Distribution.exists_norm_apply_le.doc:
**A distribution has finite order on each compact set.** For a compact `K ⊆ Ω` there are an
order `N` and a constant `C` such that `‖T φ‖ ≤ C * M` for every test function `φ` supported in
`K` whose derivatives of order at most `N` are all bounded by `M`.

DirichletCharacter.LFunction_apply_one_p.signature:
DirichletCharacter.LFunction_apply_one_pos {N : ℕ} {χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N} [NeZero N]
  (hχ : MulChar.IsQuadratic χ) (hχ₁ : χ ≠ 1) : 0 < DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ 1
DirichletCharacter.LFunction_apply_one_p.doc:
The value at `s = 1` of the `L`-function of a nontrivial quadratic Dirichlet character is a
positive real number.

Diffeomorph.restrictScalars.doc:
A `C^n` diffeomorphism for boundaryless models over `𝕜'` is a `C^n` diffeomorphism for
their scalar restrictions to `𝕜`, with the same underlying equivalence. For instance, a
biholomorphism between complex manifolds is a diffeomorphism of the underlying real manifolds.

Diffeomorph.mpullback_cotangent_symplect.signature:
Diffeomorph.mpullback_cotangent_symplecticForm.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5, u_6} {E : Type u_1}
  {H : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [TopologicalSpace H]
  {I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H} {M : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M] {F : Type u_4}
  {H' : Type u_5} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] [TopologicalSpace H']
  {J : ModelWithCorners ℝ F H'} {N : Type u_6} [TopologicalSpace N] [ChartedSpace H' N]
  [IsManifold I (↑⊤) M] [IsManifold J (↑⊤) N] (h : Diffeomorph I J M N ↑⊤) :
  (TauCeti.SmoothForm.mpullback ⇑h.cotangent ⋯) (TauCeti.CotangentBundle.symplecticForm J N) =
    TauCeti.CotangentBundle.symplecticForm I M
Diffeomorph.mpullback_cotangent_symplect.doc:
**Cotangent lifts are symplectic.** The cotangent lift of a smooth diffeomorphism pulls the
canonical symplectic form of `T*N` back to the canonical symplectic form of `T*M`.

Diffeomorph.isTopologicalGroup.signature:
Diffeomorph.isTopologicalGroup.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]
  {E : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {H : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace H]
  {I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H} {M : Type u_4} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M]
  {n : WithTop ℕ∞} [CompactSpace M] [LocallyCompactSpace E] [IsManifold I n M] [T2Space M] :
  IsTopologicalGroup (Diffeomorph I I M M n)
Diffeomorph.isTopologicalGroup.doc:
Self-diffeomorphisms of a compact Hausdorff manifold with a locally compact model space
form a topological group for the weak Whitney topology.

CoxeterSystem.MinimalCosetRepCovBy.signature:
CoxeterSystem.MinimalCosetRepCovBy.{u_1, u_2} {B : Type u_1} {W : Type u_2} [Group W]
  {M : CoxeterMatrix B} (cs : CoxeterSystem M W) (J : Set B) (y x : W) : Prop
CoxeterSystem.MinimalCosetRepCovBy.doc:
`y` is **covered by** `x` in the Bruhat order of the parabolic quotient `W / W_J`, modelled on
the minimal coset representatives: both are minimal coset representatives, `y < x`, and no minimal
coset representative lies strictly between them.

CovariantDerivative.hasConstantSectional.signature:
CovariantDerivative.hasConstantSectionalCurvature_iff_isConstantCurvatureTensor.{u_1, u_2, u_3}
  {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {H : Type u_2}
  [TopologicalSpace H] {I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H} {M : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace M]
  [ChartedSpace H M] [T2Space M] [IsManifold I (↑⊤) M]
  [Bundle.RiemannianBundle fun x => TangentSpace I x]
  [IsContMDiffRiemannianBundle I 2 E fun x => TangentSpace I x]
  (cov : CovariantDerivative I E fun x => TangentSpace I x) [cov.ContMDiffCovariantDerivative ↑⊤]
  (hcov : cov.IsMetricCompatible) (ht : cov.torsion = 0) (κ : ℝ) :
  cov.HasConstantSectionalCurvature hcov κ ↔
    Bundle.RiemannianBundle.g.IsConstantCurvatureTensor cov ⋯ κ
CovariantDerivative.hasConstantSectional.doc:
A metric-compatible torsion-free connection has constant sectional curvature `κ` if and only
if its curvature tensor is the constant-curvature tensor `R(w, u)v = κ (⟨u, v⟩ w - ⟨w, v⟩ u)` at
every point. Applied to the Levi-Civita connection, this identifies constant sectional curvature
of a Riemannian manifold with the constant-curvature equation.

the operator `1 - a • u` is invertible if and only if the value `H_u(a)` of the Fredholm series
`det (1 - T u)` is a unit of `R`.

order `h` of its Fredholm determinant `H_u`: `ΔʲH_u(a) = 0` for `j < h` and `ΔʰH_u(a)` is a unit.

ContinuousLinearMap.IsRowCompact.isEntir.doc:
**The Fredholm determinant is entire.** For a row-compact `u`, the principal-minor series
`det (1 - T u)` is a restricted power series at every radius.

ContinuousLinearMap.IsRowCompact.evalAt_.doc:
The zeros of the Fredholm series of a row-compact operator are exactly the inverses of its
nonzero eigenvalues. This conclusion concerns eigenvalues in the given coefficient field.

ContinuousLinearMap.IsRowCompact.doc:
A continuous linear map between model spaces is **row compact** if the entries of its matrix
are uniformly bounded and its row norms tend to zero along the cofinite filter of output indices.
The bound is automatic over Tate scalars (`ContinuousLinearMap.isRowCompact_iff_tendsto_rowNorm`);
it is part of the definition so that the real suprema defining the row norms are meaningful.

of a module with property (Pr) is the principal-minor series of its extension `i ∘ u ∘ r`
through any retract presentation `r ∘ i = id` of the module by a model space.

ContinuousLinearMap.IsCompletelyContinuo.doc:
A completely continuous perturbation of the identity is a Fredholm operator, over any
complete nontrivially normed field.

ContinuousAt.scalarCurvatureOfJet.doc:
**Scalar curvature is continuous in the second-order jet of the metric.** The scalar curvature
of a coordinate jet depends continuously on the jet at every jet whose Gram matrix is invertible.

ContMDiffVectorBundle.symmetricBilinearM.doc:
When two is invertible, the symmetric bilinear maps on the fibres of a `C^n` vector bundle
form a `C^n` vector bundle.

ContMDiff.restrictScalars.doc:
A `C^n` map for boundaryless models over `𝕜'` is `C^n` for their scalar restrictions
to `𝕜`. For instance, a holomorphic map between complex manifolds is smooth.

**Symmetric focal points.** For a holomorphic immersion and a normal vector `ν`, the points
`i x + ν` and `i x - ν` have the same focal multiplicity, possibly zero: one is a focal point of
`i` at `x` exactly when the other is, and the Hessians at `x` of squared distance from them have
null spaces of the same dimension.

ContDiffAt.finrank_genEigenspace_shapeOp.doc:
**Paired principal curvatures.** For a `C²` holomorphic map, multiplication by `I` identifies
the generalized `κ`- and `-κ`-eigenspaces of each shape operator, so they have the same
dimension. For `k = 1` these are the geometric multiplicities of the principal curvatures `κ`
and `-κ`.

**The Morse--Sard theorem.** The critical values of a sufficiently smooth map between
finite-dimensional real normed spaces, that is the values it takes at the points where its Fréchet
derivative is not surjective, form a set of additive Haar measure zero. No relation between the
two dimensions is required.

for every quadratic form on a finite-dimensional space,
`trace (x * ·) = 2 ^ finrank K V * scalarTrace Q x`. Every such form has an orthogonal basis, so
`CliffordAlgebra.trace_mulLeft_eq_finrank_mul_scalarTrace` applies.

CliffordAlgebra.spinGroupEquivNeg.{u, v} {R : Type u} {M : Type v} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M]

The Spin groups of `Q` and `-Q` are isomorphic, through Mathlib's identification
`evenEquivEvenNeg` of their even Clifford algebras. A product of two vectors `ι Q a * ι Q b` goes to
`-(ι (-Q) a * ι (-Q) b)`, and the vector actions agree.

CliffordAlgebra.scalarTrace_reverse_mul_.doc:
**Positivity of the trace pairing**: if `Q` is nonnegative on an orthogonal basis, then
`τ (reverse x * x) ≥ 0` for every `x`.

CliffordAlgebra.scalarTrace_reverse_mul_.doc:
**Faithfulness of the trace pairing**: if `Q` is positive on an orthogonal basis, then
`τ (reverse x * x) = 0` only for `x = 0`.

CliffordAlgebra.scalarTrace.signature:

CliffordAlgebra.scalarTrace.doc:
The **scalar part** of an element of a Clifford algebra: its degree-zero component under the
module isomorphism `CliffordAlgebra.equivExterior` with the exterior algebra.

CliffordAlgebra.realCliffordSpinGroupEqu.doc:
The Spin group of signature `(p, q)`, transported into the Clifford algebra of the negated
signature `(q, p)`. For `p = n` and `q = 0` this is the compact Spin group `Spin(n)` in the Clifford
algebra of the negative-definite coordinate form `realCliffordForm 0 n`.

CliffordAlgebra.range_spinToSpecialOrtho.doc: The image of the Spin action on `SO(Q)` is exactly the kernel of the spinor norm.

**Split `Spin₅` is `Sp₄`.** For a nondegenerate quadratic form on a five-dimensional space
whose even Clifford algebra splits, `C₀ ≃ M₄(K)`, the group `Spin(Q)` is isomorphic to the
symplectic group `Sp₄(K)`.

**`Spin₅` is a twisted form of `Sp₄`.** For a nondegenerate quadratic form on a
five-dimensional space and any separably closed extension `L / K`, there are a splitting
`e : C₀ ⊗ L ≃ M₄(L)` carrying reversal to the symplectic adjoint and an injective homomorphism
`f : Spin(Q) → Sp₄(L)` with `e⁻¹ (f s)` the scalar extension of `s`. Its image consists of exactly
those symplectic matrices `g` for which `e⁻¹ g` comes from `C₀`, so `Spin(Q)` is the group
`Sp(C₀, σ)` of `K`-rational points of `Sp₄(L)` for the `K`-structure `C₀ ⊆ C₀ ⊗ L`.

**Spin is the even unitary group in dimensions one to five.** For a nondegenerate quadratic
space of dimension between one and five, the even unitary carrier lies in the Lipschitz group.
Dimension zero is excluded, and the exclusion is not decoration: there the Lipschitz group is
trivial while the even unitary carrier is `μ₂`. The bound five is sharp, by
`CliffordAlgebra.not_evenUnitaryGroup_le_lipschitzGroup_of_six_le_finrank`.

conjugation `star = reverse ∘ involute` followed by complex conjugation of the coefficients. It
is an involutive anti-automorphism (`CliffordAlgebra.conjStar_mul`,
`CliffordAlgebra.conjStar_conjStar`) negating the real vectors.

**Frame independence of the chirality element**: `Γ = -c(e₁) c(e₂) c(e₃) c(e₄)` for every
positively oriented orthonormal basis `e`.

chirality element times the action of the two-form, `c₂(⋆α) = Γ c₂(α)`.

**The isomorphism `π₁(S¹) ≃* ℤ` is the degree.** The class of a loop is sent to its degree

cohomology of the inclusion `W ∖ S ⟶ W`.

then the cohomology groups `H_S^q(W, F)` with supports in `S` vanish for all `q < n` and every

the vertices `F(S)` of height `#S = r`, with differential the sum of the edge maps

characterised by the summand inclusions `Functor.cubeComplexι` and projections
`Functor.cubeComplexπ`, and by `Functor.ι_cubeComplex_d`.

Bundle.ContMDiffRiemannianMetric.weylTen.doc:
**Weyl tensor under conformal change.** Away from dimension `2`, the fully covariant Weyl
tensor of a conformally rescaled smooth metric `f g` is `f` times that of `g`:
`W^(f g)(u, v, w, z) = f W^g(u, v, w, z)`. Equivalently, the Weyl tensor of type `(1, 3)` is
conformally invariant.

Bundle.ContMDiffRiemannianMetric.scalarC.doc:
**The scalar curvature of a product metric** `g₁ × g₂` is the sum of the scalar curvatures of
the factors: `Scal(x, y) = Scal_{g₁}(x) + Scal_{g₂}(y)`.

and `A` the conformal connection tensor of a positive function `f`. Then the curvature of the
Levi-Civita connection of `f g` is

`R^(f g)(X, Y) Z = R^∇(X, Y) Z + (∇_X A)(Z, Y) - (∇_Y A)(Z, X) + A(A(Z, Y), X) - A(A(Z, X), Y)`,

function `f` are assumed `Cⁿ` on all of `M` for some `1 ≤ n`, and `Z` differentiable on all of `M`;
the remaining hypotheses are differentiability at `x` of `X`, `Y`, `∇_X Z`, `∇_Y Z`, `A(Z, X)` and
`A(Z, Y)`.

other.

Bundle.ContMDiffRiemannianMetric.IsLocal.doc:
**Local conformal flatness forces the Weyl tensor to vanish.** Away from dimension `2`, the
Weyl tensor of a locally conformally flat metric vanishes at every point. This is the easy half of
the Weyl–Schouten theorem.

A smooth Riemannian metric `g` is **locally conformally flat** if every point `x` has a
neighbourhood on which a conformal rescaling `f g`, by a smooth positive function `f`, is flat:
the curvature tensor of the Levi-Civita connection of `f g` vanishes at every point near `x`.

Bundle.ContMDiffRiemannianMetric.HasPosi.doc:
A smooth Riemannian metric has positive scalar curvature if its scalar curvature is positive
at every point.

AnalyticOnNhd.exists_complexification_pi.doc:
**Complexification of a real analytic map on an open set.** A map from `ι → ℝ` to `κ → ℝ`,
with `ι` and `κ` finite, that is analytic on an open set `U` extends to a map
`F : (ι → ℂ) → (κ → ℂ)` that is complex analytic on an open set `W` whose real points are exactly
those of `U`. The set `W` is invariant under complex conjugation, `F` agrees with `f` at the real
points of `U`, and `F` commutes with complex conjugation.

AnalyticOnNhd.exists_complexification.doc:
**Complexification of a real analytic function on an open set.** A function of finitely many
real variables that is analytic on an open set `U` extends to a function `F` of as many complex
variables that is complex analytic on an open set `W` whose real points are exactly those of `U`.
The set `W` is invariant under complex conjugation, `F` agrees with `f` at the real points of
`U`, and `F` commutes with complex conjugation.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.universally_isH.doc:
**The absolute Frobenius is a universal homeomorphism**: every base change of `F_X` is a
homeomorphism of underlying spaces.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isFinite_froben.doc:
**The absolute Frobenius of a scheme locally of finite type over a perfect ring is finite.**
For a scheme `X` locally of finite type over `Spec R`, with `R` a perfect ring of characteristic
`p`, the absolute Frobenius `F_X : X ⟶ X` is a finite morphism.

All nodes of a proper nodal curve split over one finite separable field extension.
For any chosen base change of the curve, its singular subscheme is the spectrum of a
product of copies of the extended field, as a scheme over that field. This includes the
smooth case, in which the node set is empty.

AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.existsUniqu.doc:
**The universal property of a contraction**, for a universally closed surjective morphism,
such as a proper surjective one, for which `𝒪_Y → c_* 𝒪_X` is an isomorphism.

Algebra.QuasiFinite.exists_fg_subalgebra.signature:
Algebra.QuasiFinite.exists_fg_subalgebra_and_span_eq_top.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2}
  [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] [Algebra.FiniteType R A] [Algebra.QuasiFinite R A] :
  ∃ A' s,
    (Subalgebra.toSubmodule A').FG ∧
      ↑s ⊆ ↑A' ∧ Ideal.span ↑s = ⊤ ∧ ∀ r ∈ s, ∀ (x : A), ∀ᶠ (m : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, r ^ m * x ∈ A'
Algebra.QuasiFinite.exists_fg_subalgebra.doc:
**Zariski's main theorem, global form.** A quasi-finite algebra `A` of finite type over `R`
has a module-finite subalgebra `A'` and finitely many elements `r ∈ A'` generating the unit ideal
of `A`, such that for every `x ∈ A` and every such `r`, all large enough powers of `r` move `x`
into `A'`. Geometrically, `Spec A` is covered by finitely many basic opens `D(r)` on which it
agrees with the finite `R`-scheme `Spec A'`.

AddMonoidHom.exact_completion.doc:
**Completion preserves strict exact sequences.** If `M → N → P` is exact with strict maps,
where `M` is a first-countable nonarchimedean group and `N` is a nonarchimedean group, then the
sequence of separated completions is exact. Its maps are again strict by
`AddMonoidHom.isStrictMap_completion` when `M` and `N` are first countable. No Hausdorff
hypothesis is needed.

AddEquiv.groupCohomologyπOdd_cyclicRep_e.doc:
**Odd-degree classes of the cyclic representation.** Two norm-zero elements `x` and `y`
have the same class in odd degree exactly when `y = x + (b - A b)` for some `b : T`.

AddCircle.fundamentalGroupMulEquiv_eq_wi.doc:
For positive periods, the chosen-lift equivalence agrees with Mathlib's winding-number
isomorphism. In particular it is independent of the chosen lift and has the same orientation.

AbstractMeasure.towerCoordinatesEquiv.{u_1, u_3} {Γ : Type u_1} [Group Γ] [TopologicalSpace Γ]

AbstractMeasure.towerCoordinatesEquiv.doc:
**Integral measures are the compatible families along a tower.** For a compact group with a
tower of finite quotients, sending an integral measure to its finite projections at all levels is
a linear equivalence onto the compatible families.

AbstractMeasure.norm_toCLMEquiv_eq_iSup_.signature:
AbstractMeasure.norm_toCLMEquiv_eq_iSup_coeff.{u_1} {p : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {K : Type u_1}

AbstractMeasure.norm_toCLMEquiv_eq_iSup_.doc:
**Mahler duality for field coefficients.** Over a complete ultrametric nontrivially normed
field with a contractive `ℤ_[p]`-algebra structure, such as a complete extension of `ℚ_p`, the
operator norm of a measure on `ℤ_p` is the supremum of the norms of the coefficients of its Amice
transform.

AbstractMeasure.mahlerMomentsEquiv.signature:
AbstractMeasure.mahlerMomentsEquiv.{u_1} (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (R : Type u_1)
  [NormedCommRing R] [TauCeti.NormedRing.IsTate R] [Algebra ℤ_[p] R] [IsBoundedSMul ℤ_[p] R]
  [IsUltrametricDist R] [CompleteSpace R] : AbstractMeasure ℤ_[p] R R ≃ₗ[R] ↥(lp (fun x => R) ⊤)
AbstractMeasure.mahlerMomentsEquiv.doc:
**Mahler duality.** Over a ring with a multiplicative pseudo-uniformiser, a measure on `ℤ_p`
is determined by its moments `μ (x ↦ x choose n)`, the coefficients of its Amice transform, and
every bounded sequence is the moment sequence of a measure. The inverse sends a bounded sequence
`b` to the measure `f ↦ ∑ n, Δ^n f (0) * b n`.

AbstractMeasure.extendCoefficients.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {X : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace X]
  {K : Type u_2} {O : Type u_3} [NormedField K] [CommRing O] [TopologicalSpace O]
  [IsTopologicalRing O] (j : O →+* K) [CompactSpace X] [IsUltrametricDist K] [T2Space X]

AbstractMeasure.extendCoefficients.doc:
**Extension of coefficients from the unit ball.** For a ring homomorphism `j : O →+* K`
into the closed unit ball of a complete ultrametric field, `extendCoefficients j hj μ` is the
`K`-valued measure on the profinite space `X` whose coefficient on each fibre of a map to a finite
discrete space is the image under `j` of the coefficient of `μ`
(`finiteProjection_extendCoefficients`). When `j` is continuous it is the unique `K`-valued measure
with `ι_j(μ)(j ∘ f) = j(μ(f))` for all `f ∈ C(X, O)` (`extendCoefficients_apply_comp`,
`eq_extendCoefficients_of_apply_comp`).

exactly when there is a unique `ℤ_p`-valued measure `μ` with `ν (f) = μ (f)` for every

**Integral measures on `ℤ_pˣ` from unit coordinates.** For every family of coefficients
`c n : (ℤ/p^nℤ)ˣ →₀ ℤ_p` compatible under the reductions `(ℤ/p^nℤ)ˣ → (ℤ/p^mℤ)ˣ`, there is a
unique integral measure on `ℤ_pˣ` whose finite projection along the reduction
`ℤ_pˣ → (ℤ/p^nℤ)ˣ` is `c n` for every `n`.

AbstractMeasure.completedGroupAlgebraEquiv.{u_1} {Γ : Type u_1} [Group Γ] [TopologicalSpace Γ]

AbstractMeasure.completedGroupAlgebraEqu.doc:
**Integral measures are the completed group algebra.** The canonical algebra equivalence
between integral measures on a profinite group and its completed group algebra.

For `ℤ_p`-valued measures, multiplication by `x` acts on the Amice transform as the Mahler
derivation: `A (x μ) = (1 + T) d/dT A_μ`.
